commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Keep whole-chunk max_load_tokens caps with sliding window groups
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With sliding window groups, the OffloadingConnector applied its prompt-end `-1` after the `max_load_tokens` / `max_num_new_tokens` caps, so a whole-chunk cap lost a chunk (a one-chunk cap loaded nothing). Follow-up to #55885.

## Claims

- With sliding window groups (and no partial-tail support, e.g. gpt-oss, Gemma 2/3), `max_load_tokens = k * tokens_per_chunk` now loads `k` chunks instead of `k - 1`.
- The same lost chunk is fixed for `max_num_new_tokens` (the bound from groups the connector does not offload).
- No change when there is no cap: the hit still stops before the last prompt token.

## Validation

New test `test_max_load_tokens_preserves_aligned_sliding_window_chunk` (16-token chunks, 65-token prompt, mixed full/sliding-window groups):

| Cap | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 16 tokens | 0 | 16 |
| 32 tokens | 16 | 32 |
| none | 64 | 64 |

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py \
  -k "max_load_tokens or sliding"   # 132 passed
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector
```

## Details

`_lookup_complete_chunks` computed `min(num_tokens, computed + cap) - 1`. The `-1` exists so a sliding-window hit stops before the last prompt token, which must be recomputed. When a cap ends earlier, it is already a supported boundary, but the `-1` moved it one token below, and the per-group `round_down` then dropped a whole chunk. The fix applies the `-1` to the prompt-end ceiling only: `min(num_tokens - 1, computed + cap)`. This matches the partial-tail path, which already uses `num_prompt_tokens - 1` with uncapped limits. Mamba alignment is unchanged.

No existing issue or PR covers this (searched `max_load_tokens`, `max_hit_size_tokens`, sliding window + offloading). Draft #62932 edits nearby lines for a different purpose (capacity-bounded loads); expect a trivial rebase for whichever lands second.

Test creation and validation assisted by Claude Code.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Abort inbound loads when draining for a cache reset
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

On a P2P consumer (decoder), `TieringOffloadingManager.reset_cache()` (`/reset_prefix_cache` with `reset_connector`, sleep, weight update) blocks the engine thread in `P2PSecondaryTierManager.drain_jobs()` for the full load timeout plus the abort-ack window (~35 s for PD, ~15 s symmetric) whenever a load waits on a prefiller that never writes. `has_pending_work` counts client loads, and the drain never aborts them.

This is the consumer-side counterpart of #63948, which #63988 fixes on the producer side (stores waiting for a fetch). It came up in review there.

`drain_jobs()` now aborts every inbound load not already aborting before it polls, through the same path a load timeout takes (#64256): `AbortFetch`, fail the job at once, defer the chunk release until the `AbortAck` or the session's `close()`. The drain then waits only for the acks, bounded by `_ABORT_ACK_TIMEOUT_S` (5 s, after which the session disconnects and `close()` releases), so every deferred release is set on return as the `drain_jobs()` contract in `tiering/base.py` requires. Lookup state is untouched.

## Test Plan

- `test_reset_cache_aborts_load_from_silent_peer` (test_manager.py): a real `TieringOffloadingManager` + CPU primary + `P2PSession`; a PD load whose peer only answers `AbortFetch`. `reset_cache()` returns after the ack, the job is finished, the chunk is released, and the session stays up. Fails on main ("drain_jobs waited on a load no peer will write").
- `test_abort_loads_fails_each_load_once` (test_sessions.py): `abort_loads()` aborts each load exactly once (skipping one already aborted by `finish_request`), fails it at once with a deferred release, and the acks release it.
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/ tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tier_poll_thread.py`

## Test Result

463 passed.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Fix flaky layer 0 bound in test_dsv4_mono_layers
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Raise the layer 0 bound of `test_mono_decode_matches_the_model` in `tests/models/test_dsv4_mono_layers.py` from 5% to 7%. The 5% bound sits inside the run to run noise of the vLLM reference path itself, so the test fails now and then on MI355 in `(MI355) DeepSeek-V4-Pro Mono Decode Numerics`. This is a stopgap until #63486 replaces this test.

## Claims

- Fixes the flaky layer 0 check in `test_mono_decode_matches_the_model`. Every CI failure since Oct 27 is this check on the same token (prompt 5541, position 5544) at 5.04% to 5.37%, and the retry passed each time.
- Only the layer 0 bound changes. Layers 1 to 4 stay at 10% and the residual and mix checks are unchanged.

## Validation

CI failures of the layer 0 check, all passed on retry

- https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97458#01a17ac4-7686-4f72-8ead-e40dd48b31e1 (5.37%)
- https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97976#01a182e3-a60b-4e26-968f-8e0402ebd6a7 (5.37%)
- https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98662#01a18c10-7a32-4ea0-aa42-c711c120ecc7 (5.22%)
- https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/99438#01a19f8b-f4e6-4cda-a62c-068654353a6b (5.05%)
- https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/100146#01a1aa23-6b81-4e6b-b58e-1502def2668d (5.04%)
- https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/100181#01a1aa94-8dec-4de8-99e1-5fe95c43b00c (5.05%)

Layer 0 relative error for the same decode tokens across separate runs with identical inputs and identical generated tokens (MI350X, 8 GPUs, CI image `rocm/vllm-ci:build-01a1a5a4-ac64-4181-8fd7-fb84016eddd6`)

| Comparison | Median | Max |
|---|---|---|
| vLLM path against itself | 0.96% | 4.23% |
| mono path against itself | 2.75% | 4.27% |
| mono against vLLM (what the test checks) | 3.07% | 5.04% |

Before the fix, 1 of 10 local runs on MI350X failed the layer 0 check at 5.04%.

After the fix, 20 of 20 runs passed on MI355X with the same image.

```bash
pytest -q tests/models/test_dsv4_mono_layers.py::test_mono_decode_matches_the_model
```

## Details

Layer 0 sees the same inputs on both paths, but the vLLM path is not deterministic run to run with these random weights (the comment in `_fill` already notes that the order of atomics moves vLLM's own logits). Its output moves by up to 4.3% between runs on its own, so a 5% bound between mono and vLLM leaves almost no room for the MXFP8 against FP8 difference the test is meant to allow. 7% covers the worst case seen in CI (5.37%) with some margin and still fails at once on a layer the kernels no longer follow, since layer 0 is hash routed and has no near tie exemption.

The test author confirmed the flakiness was already seen when the test was written, and the bound was set to 5% for a stable local pass.

#63486 rewrites this test with both paths on the same inputs and derived bounds, which removes this check. This PR does not overlap with it and only keeps CI stable until it lands.

The other test in the same job, `test_dsv4_mono_numerics.py::test_mono_decode_layer_matches_vllm`, also failed a few times recently (a replay mismatch and a NaN). That is a different problem and is not touched here.

AI assistance (Cursor) was used for the investigation and the change. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

commits.pr_title: [CI][Step5] Pin the starting block size in the CSA tail ring test
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`tests/models/step5/test_csa_tail_ring_block_size.py` (#65153) fails on main since #63231 changed the default `--block-size` from 16 to 64. Failing job: https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15772/list?jid=01a1ab28-6edc-4741-b70e-15b88984c0c5

## Claims

- Fixes 5/6 failing cases of `test_block_size_fits_tail_ring` (`assert 64 == 32`, `assert 64 == 16`).
- Test-only change; no change to Step5 or block size logic.

## Validation

Before (main):
```
pytest -q tests/models/step5/test_csa_tail_ring_block_size.py
5 failed, 1 passed
```

After:
```
pytest -q tests/models/step5/test_csa_tail_ring_block_size.py
6 passed
```

## Details

The test sets `cache_config.block_size = 16`, but `Platform.update_block_size_for_backend` picks the preferred size starting from `CacheConfig.DEFAULT_BLOCK_SIZE`, not from `cache_config.block_size`. After #63231 that start is 64, which already fits the tail ring, so every case ends at 64 and the 16 -> 32 path from #65153 is no longer exercised. The test now pins `CacheConfig.DEFAULT_BLOCK_SIZE` to 16 via `monkeypatch`, so it is independent of the global default again.

commits.pr_title: [Feature][MoE] Allow a shared routed-expert row restorer
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Allow MoE implementations to provide an optional shared routing-row restorer, so backends such as vLLM-Ascend can restore their token layout without replacing `capture()`. The existing upstream recovery algorithm remains the default.

Related to #61539. This consolidates the smaller implementation from #65321 into this PR.

## Claims

- Bind the first available `restore_routed_experts_rows(topk_ids, ctx)` method once for all captured layers. Existing capture sources need no changes.
- Preserve `_restore_local_topk_ids(topk_ids, ctx)`, capture/router signatures, microbatch offsets and buffer writes.
- Limit production changes to `routed_experts_capturer.py`; no changes to MoERunner, MegaMoE, ModelRunner or ForwardContext.

## Validation

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_PLUGINS='' HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -o addopts='' \
  tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_capture.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_ubatch_slicing.py -q
```

The previous head (`a109c1d`) produced **79 passed, 10 skipped** on CPU. The current head (`329840b`) replaces the broad parametrized test with two focused cases: exact buffer writes from one custom restorer, and use of the current forward context across two distinct layers. These cases have not yet been rerun on the current head.

Applicable pre-commit checks (including mypy and CI test selection) and `git diff --check` passed on the previous head; current-head local validation is pending. GPU-dependent skips are not graph-replay validation.

## Details

The selected restorer must handle every captured MoE layer using the current forward context, without depending on its provider's layer-specific state. It owns any required communication and padding removal. Providers must keep collectives rank-consistent and graph-replay safe.

This retains upstream shape inference and existing buffer semantics; it does not add per-layer restoration strategies or combine records written to the same layer slot.

### vLLM-Ascend integration

A local adapter was checked against the pre-rebase #65321 revision with 35 isolated CPU tests and 20 subtests. These exercise callback binding and restored buffer contents, including padded MC2/SP rows, with mocked collectives. NPU/HCCL, full-model serving and graph replay have not been validated for this implementation.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Report system_fingerprint from the engine's config hash
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Rust frontend returns `system_fingerprint: null` because the hash part of the fingerprint comes from `VllmConfig.compute_hash()`, and it has no `VllmConfig`. This PR has the engine report that hash (and `enable_expert_parallel`) in `EngineCoreReadyResponse`, and the Rust frontend builds `system_fingerprint` from it for every `--fingerprint-mode`.

## Claims

- The engine reports `config_hash`, the `compute_hash()` of its initialized `VllmConfig`, and `enable_expert_parallel` in `EngineCoreReadyResponse`. A hashing failure reports `None` and never fails startup.
- The Rust frontend supports `--fingerprint-mode` (`full`, `hash`, `custom`, `none`) and `--fingerprint-value`, which it previously rejected as unsupported.
- It reports `system_fingerprint` in Python's format (`vllm-<version>[-tpN][-ppN][-dpN][-ep]-<hash8>` for `full`) and placement: on non-streaming chat and completion responses, and on the last stream chunk (the finish chunk, or the usage chunk when `include_usage` adds one). Before this PR it was `null` and stream chunks lacked the key.
- The Python frontend is unchanged: it keeps hashing its own config copy, so the two frontends report different hash parts for the same deployment. A follow-up PR will switch the Python frontend to the engine-reported hash.

## Validation

**End to end** (GB200, `vllm serve` with `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1` and `vllm-rs` built from this change; the engine's `config_hash` logged from the ready response):

| Deployment | engine `config_hash` | Rust frontend `system_fingerprint` |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B | `6c364a3de1` | `vllm-…-6c364a3d` |
| ibm-research/PowerMoE-3b, DP 2, `--enable-expert-parallel` | `da24f3f92e` (both ranks) | `vllm-…-dp2-ep-da24f3f9` |
| Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B (hybrid) | `889b5c0aed` | `vllm-…-889b5c0a` |

The fingerprint appears on the non-streaming response, on the finish chunk without `include_usage`, and only on the usage chunk with it, matching Python's placement.

**Rust CI set** (`.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`), on this branch:

```bash
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check                                  # clean
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                                                         # clean
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans               # clean
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings  # clean
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2547 tests run: 2547 passed, 13 skipped
```

**Python:** `pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/engine/__init__.py vllm/v1/engine/core.py rust/src/engine-core-client/src/tests/python_compat.py` passes (ruff, mypy, and the other hooks).

New Rust tests:
- `fingerprint::tests::fingerprint_follows_python_modes`: all four modes, parallelism parts, and `nohash`.
- `fingerprint::tests::fingerprint_hashes_the_engine_with_the_smallest_max_model_len`: two engines with different auto-fitted lengths.
- `routes::tests::system_fingerprint_is_reported_on_the_last_message_like_python`: chat, completions, and prompt-only completions, non-streaming and streaming with and without `include_usage`. It fails with the base handlers restored.
- `cli::tests::fingerprint_flags_select_system_fingerprint_mode`: the flags and `--args-json`.
- `python_msgpack_fixtures_match_rust_encoding_and_record_nixl_metrics`: the two new ready-response fields decode from Python's encoding.

**Not a duplicate:** the open PRs that mention `system_fingerprint` or `--fingerprint-mode` (vllm-project/vllm#57390, vllm-project/vllm#57399, vllm-project/vllm#57400, vllm-project/vllm#57436, vllm-project/vllm#63814) change how the Python frontend handles the `none` and `custom` modes. None of them reports the config hash from the engine or touches the Rust frontend.

## Details

**Why the engine's hash rather than reproducing the Python frontend's:**
- **It describes what runs.** `compute_hash()` identifies the config that shapes the computation graph. Its value on the initialized config is the same kind of value as the torch.compile cache key, which the worker computes from its config (`compilation/backends.py`).
- **It is independent of VRAM.** Memory-derived values are ignored factors in `CacheConfig.compute_hash` (`num_gpu_blocks`, `kv_cache_size_tokens`, `gpu_memory_utilization`, `hash_block_size`, …), so the hash is stable across restarts of the same deployment. The one input that can depend on free memory is an auto-fitted `max_model_len` (`--max-model-len -1`), which does change which requests are accepted.
- **The Python frontend's hash is of a launch-config copy.** It is the launch config plus the few values `MPClient._apply_ready_response` syncs back. It misses what the engine resolves during initialization (`kv_cache_layout`, resolved in `EngineCore` before memory profiling and never synced back; on Qwen3-0.6B that field alone changes the hash) and keeps the deployment DP size that dense DP ranks reset to 1. Reproducing it would mean the engine keeping a copy of its launch config and mirroring the frontend's sync list.

**Engine** (`vllm/v1/engine/core.py`, `vllm/v1/engine/__init__.py`): `_make_ready_response` adds `config_hash` (guarded, so a hashing failure reports `None`) and `enable_expert_parallel`. Both fields have defaults, so existing consumers of the ready response are unaffected.

**Rust frontend:**
- `vllm-engine-core-client` decodes the two fields.
- The server owns the fingerprint (`fingerprint.rs`, `FingerprintMode::fingerprint`). It is built once at startup from the engine with the smallest `max_model_len` (dense DP ranks auto-fit it independently; Python's frontend keeps the smallest) and the deployment-wide DP size, stored on `AppState`, and stamped by the chat and completions handlers.
- The CLI maps `--fingerprint-mode` (the clap value enum `FingerprintModeArg`) and `--fingerprint-value` to the server's `FingerprintMode`, stored as `Config::fingerprint_mode` like Python's `fingerprint_mode`. As in Python, `custom` without a value reports no fingerprint.
- The render server has no engine and serves no response that carries the field.

**Deviations from Python:**
- The hash part is the engine's initialized-config hash, not a hash of a frontend config copy (see above); the follow-up PR aligns the Python frontend.
- When the engine reports no hash (`compute_hash()` raised in the engine, or an engine without the field), Rust reports `…-nohash`.
- Rust uses the engine-reported `vllm_version`, where Python uses its own `vllm.__version__`. They are the same install in every supported deployment.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write this change and this description. The human submitter reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Count vllm:watermark_requests from the engine-reported flag
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With a `watermark_config`, the Python frontend exports `vllm:watermark_requests{status}` (vllm-project/vllm#58715): every finished request counts once as `watermarked`, `skipped` (it asked for watermarking but the sampler cannot apply it, e.g. greedy or trace replay) or `not_watermarked` (it opted out with `watermarking=false`). The Rust frontend never exports the family, and `docs/features/watermarking.md` says so.

Since vllm-project/vllm#62966, EngineCore decides the final flag itself: `watermark_config.enforce` overrides request opt-outs, and the scheduler reports what the sampler applies in a new trailing `EngineCoreOutput.watermarking` field, set on the request's first output and only when the engine has a `watermark_config`. Python's `IterationStats` takes `is_watermarked` from that field. Rust decodes `EngineCoreOutput` with `AllowTrailingFields`, so today it silently drops the field.

This PR decodes the field and counts each finished request by the engine-reported flag, like Python.

## Claims

- `vllm-engine-core-client`: decode the trailing `watermarking: Option<bool>` on `EngineCoreOutput`; the Python msgpack fixture now sets it.
- `vllm-metrics`: register `vllm:watermark_requests` with labels `model_name`, `engine`, `status`.
- `vllm-llm`: the request metrics tracker keeps whether the request asked for watermarking (`EngineCoreSamplingParams.watermarking`, `true` unless the client opted out). When an output carries the engine's flag it picks the status (applied → `watermarked`; asked but not applied → `skipped`; opted out and not enforced → `not_watermarked`) and counts it once at finish, like Python's `update_from_finished_request`.
- Docs: drops the stale line in `docs/features/watermarking.md` saying the Rust frontend does not export the counter.

## Validation

New test `vllm-llm` `generate_records_watermark_status_reported_by_engine` drives three requests through a mock engine, each reporting the flag on a non-terminal first output and finishing on a later one: a greedy request reported as not applied (`skipped`), an opt-out the engine enforces (`watermarked`), and a plain opt-out (`not_watermarked`). It snapshots the counters before the first request (no series) and after each request. Red-green: classifying from the request alone (ignoring the engine flag), swapping `skipped` and `not_watermarked`, or reading the flag only from the terminal output each fail it. `python_msgpack_fixtures_match_rust_encoding_and_record_nixl_metrics` checks the new field against Python's msgpack encoding.

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`, on this branch (main `c58e7f6d05` + this PR):

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust   # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2544 tests run: 2544 passed, 13 skipped
```

`pre-commit run --files` on the changed Python fixture (`rust/src/engine-core-client/src/tests/python_compat.py`) and on `docs/features/watermarking.md`: passed.

The Python tests that pin the family are offline or in-process (`tests/watermarking/test_watermarking_e2e.py` through `vllm_runner`, `tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py`), not server-level, so nothing is added to the Rust frontend's Python e2e set. No GPU run: the change only adds a counter fed by an existing wire field, and the mock-engine test covers the wire-to-metric path.

## Details

**Layering.** The consumer of the new wire field is the per-request metrics tracker in `vllm-llm`, which already turns `EngineCoreOutput` fields into request counters (`num_nans_in_logits` → `vllm:corrupted_requests`). The engine owns the decision (enforcement, greedy, trace replay), so Rust takes the applied flag from it instead of re-deriving Python's frontend `resolve_watermarking`, and needs no `--watermark-config` in the frontend.

**Deviations from Python:**

- **Series appear on the engine's first report, not at startup.** Python creates the three series per engine from its own `vllm_config.watermark_config`. The Rust frontend has no copy of that engine config (a `--watermark-config` frontend arg could disagree with an externally launched engine; a new `EngineCoreReadyResponse` field would be a Python change), and the engine-reported field is the only signal. The three series of an engine are created together, at zero, when its first output carries `watermarking`.
- **Requests that finish before their first output are not counted** (aborted while queued, rejected by the engine): the engine never reports a flag for them. Python counts them by its frontend prediction. No tokens were sampled for them, so no status describes an output.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR adds `vllm:watermark_requests` or reads `EngineCoreOutput.watermarking` in the Rust frontend (searched open PRs for `watermark_requests`, `watermarking rust frontend` and `watermark metrics`). The open watermarking PR vllm-project/vllm#56859 adds a new algorithm on the Python side.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Frontend] Write run-batch JSON responses without parsing them back
commits.pr_body:
## Overview `vllm run-batch` parses every buffered JSON response body (`/v1/embeddings`, `/score`, `/rerank`) back into the response union and dumps it again to write the output line. This PR writes a successful JSON body as is instead. Follow-up to #63189, which made run-batch accept these buffered bodies. ## Claims - Writing one `/v1/embeddings` output line takes 4.8× less event-loop time for 128-dim embeddings (85.3 → 17.9 µs) and 6.4× less for 512-dim ones (188.1 → 29.4 µs), measured on main. - Embedding batches are bound by the frontend event loop, so this shows up end to end. On one H100 with a batch of 864,891 short inputs, the same change on v0.33.0 cut the wall time by 12.5% (a 128-dim embedding model) and 18% (Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, 512 dims). - Output values do not change. Only the number formatting can differ, because the line now keeps the handler's formatting instead of pydantic's: orjson for embeddings (e.g. `0.000007177709` instead of `7.177709e-6`), `json.dumps` for score and rerank (e.g. `1e-06` instead of `1e-6`). - Behavior changes: - A NaN or Inf embedding, which orjson writes as `null`, is now written as is with status 200, as the online `/v1/embeddings` server returns it. On main it became a "Request must not be sent in stream mode" error line. - A `Response` with a status other than 200 or a media type other than JSON, or a return value of any other type, now gets an error line that says so ("Unexpected response status code: …", "Unsupported response media type: …", "Unsupported response type") instead of the stream mode error. No run-batch handler returns these today. ## Validation **Tests.** - `test_batch_embedding_json_body_is_written_as_is` builds the body the way `EmbeddingServing` does (a float32 array written by orjson, with a NaN) and checks that the line carries it verbatim with no error. The parsing path would rewrite `0.000007177709` as `7.177709e-6` and reject the `null`. - `test_batch_json_responses` checks the written line for embedding and score bodies, from both `JSONResponse` and `create_json_response`. - `test_batch_rejects_unsupported_responses` covers the error lines: `StreamingResponse`, async generator, non-200 status, non-JSON media type, other types. - `test_requests_and_responses_reuse_type_adapters` returns a 400 `JSONResponse`, so it now expects the status code error. ``` # main (d8588b71ff), this PR's tests with the fix reverted $ pytest tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_run_batch.py -k "json_body or unsupported_responses" FAILED ...::test_batch_embedding_json_body_is_written_as_is FAILED ...::test_batch_rejects_unsupported_responses[status] FAILED ...::test_batch_rejects_unsupported_responses[media_type] FAILED ...::test_batch_rejects_unsupported_responses[other] 4 failed, 2 passed # this PR $ pytest tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_run_batch.py -k "json_response or json_body or unsupported_responses or type_adapters" 11 passed, 62 deselected ``` The whole file gives 61 passed and 12 failed locally, against 54 passed and 12 failed on main. The same 12 tests fail on both. They launch `vllm run-batch` with a model, which needs a vLLM build I don't have on macOS, so they are left to the Entrypoints Unit CI step. **Microbenchmark.** Apple M1 Pro, CPU only. `run_request` and the output line write for 3,000 responses per round, 7 alternating rounds, median with the range in brackets. The handler returns what `EmbeddingServing._openai_json_response` builds for `encoding_format=float`: `create_json_response()` of a dict with a float32 ndarray embedding, so both columns include that serialization. All 3,000 lines parse to the same values (ids aside) before and after, with no error lines. | embedding dims | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | 128 | 85.3 µs [83.5–103.6] | 17.9 µs [17.7–22.4] | | 512 | 188.1 µs [184.9–192.0] | 29.4 µs [28.9–32.7] | **End to end.** I have not run end to end on main. On v0.33.0 (before #63189, so both arms carry a small patch that parses these bodies with `json.loads` + `validate_python`), I applied an equivalent write-as-is patch and ran one embeddings batch file: 864,891 lines, averaging 15–21 prompt tokens depending on the tokenizer, `max_inflight` default. One H100 per run, 3 runs per arm on the same node. | model | v0.33.0 | write as is | output check | |---|---|---|---| | 128-dim embedding model | 680 s [671–686] | 595 s [588–606] (−12.5%) | values identical on the first 2,000 lines | | Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B (512 dims) | 751 s [747–757] | 616 s [611–622] (−18%) | values identical on the first 2,000 lines | Event-loop CPU per request fell from 0.61 to 0.51 ms and from 0.68 to 0.53 ms. GPU utilization was 5–10%, so the loop was the bottleneck. On main the response path is a bit heavier than on v0.33.0. `validate_json` is slower than `json.loads` + `validate_python` for these float-heavy bodies, and the union has gained `CompletionResponse`. So the gain on main should be at least as large.
Benchmark script (python bench_run_batch_response.py before/run_batch.py after/run_batch.py) ```python """Per-response cost of writing a /v1/embeddings output line in run-batch. Usage (from the vLLM repo root): python bench_run_batch_response.py The handler returns the body the embeddings server builds for encoding_format=float: create_json_response() of a dict whose embedding is a float32 ndarray (EmbeddingServing._openai_json_response). """ import asyncio import importlib.util import json import statistics import sys import time import numpy as np import vllm.entrypoints.launchers # noqa: F401 (parent package) from vllm.entrypoints.pooling.embed.protocol import ( EmbeddingResponse, EmbeddingResponseData, ) from vllm.entrypoints.serve.engine.protocol import UsageInfo from vllm.entrypoints.serve.utils.api_utils import create_json_response def load(name, path): spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location( f"vllm.entrypoints.launchers.{name}", path ) mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec) spec.loader.exec_module(mod) return mod def body_dict(dim, rng): v = rng.standard_normal(dim).astype(np.float32) v /= np.linalg.norm(v) item = EmbeddingResponseData(index=0, embedding=[]).model_dump() item["embedding"] = v resp = EmbeddingResponse( id="embd-x", created=0, model="vllm", data=[], usage=UsageInfo(prompt_tokens=16, total_tokens=16), ).model_dump() resp["data"] = [item] return resp def write_line(output): to_line = getattr(output, "to_json_line", None) return to_line() if to_line is not None else output.model_dump_json() async def run(rb, payloads, request): it = iter(payloads) async def handler(_body): return create_json_response(next(it)) t0 = time.perf_counter() lines = [write_line(await rb.run_request(handler, request)) for _ in payloads] return lines, (time.perf_counter() - t0) / len(payloads) * 1e6 def main(): mods = {"before": load("rb_before", sys.argv[1]), "after": load("rb_after", sys.argv[2])} n, rounds = 3000, 7 for dim in (128, 512): rng = np.random.default_rng(0) payloads = [body_dict(dim, rng) for _ in range(n)] times = {k: [] for k in mods} lines = {} for r in range(rounds): for name, rb in (mods.items() if r % 2 == 0 else reversed(mods.items())): request = rb.BatchRequestInput.model_validate_json( json.dumps( { "custom_id": "k", "method": "POST", "url": "/v1/embeddings", "body": {"model": "vllm", "input": "x", "dimensions": dim}, } ) ) out, per = asyncio.run(run(rb, payloads, request)) times[name].append(per) lines[name] = out def values(line): d = json.loads(line) d.pop("id") d["response"].pop("request_id") return d same = sum(values(a) == values(b) for a, b in zip(lines["before"], lines["after"])) errors = {k: sum(json.loads(x)["error"] is not None for x in v) for k, v in lines.items()} med = {k: statistics.median(v) for k, v in times.items()} rng_ = {k: (min(v), max(v)) for k, v in times.items()} print( f"dim={dim} before={med['before']:.1f}us [{rng_['before'][0]:.1f}-{rng_['before'][1]:.1f}] " f"after={med['after']:.1f}us [{rng_['after'][0]:.1f}-{rng_['after'][1]:.1f}] " f"speedup={med['before'] / med['after']:.1f}x same_values={same}/{n} errors={errors}" ) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ```
## Details **Root cause.** Since #58660, the embeddings server returns a buffered orjson `Response`, and #63189 made `run_request` parse it with `_ALL_RESPONSE_ADAPTER.validate_json` so the line is not reported as an error. Score and rerank `JSONResponse` bodies took the same parse. Parsing validates every float of every embedding against the response union, and `model_dump_json` writes them all again. In an embeddings batch this runs on the event loop for every line. **Why skipping the parse is safe.** No run-batch handler needs it, as found in review: - Chat, completions, transcriptions and translations return the response models or `ErrorResponse`, which are written as before. - Embeddings (`float`, `base64`) returns an orjson `Response`, and `bytes` returns a `StreamingResponse`, which stays an error line. - Score and rerank return `JSONResponse(content=response.model_dump())`. - Pooling handlers raise on errors, and `run_request` turns the exception into an `ErrorResponse`, so no handler returns a non-200 JSON body. A 200 JSON body is built from the response models, so parsing it back only re-checks what was just serialized. The parse only fails for a non-finite embedding: orjson writes NaN and Inf as `null`, which the models reject. That failure was not handled on purpose. The line fell through to the "Request must not be sent in stream mode" error, while the online server returns the same body with status 200, and run-batch also wrote `null` when the handler returned `EmbeddingResponse` objects (pydantic writes NaN as `null` too). This PR writes these bodies as the online server returns them. **Shape of the result.** `run_request` returns early for each response type, as suggested in review. For a JSON body line, `BatchRequestOutput.response.body` is `None`. The handler's bytes are kept in a private attribute and spliced in by `BatchRequestOutput.to_json_line()`, which the writer now calls instead of `model_dump_json()`. Lines without a raw body are serialized exactly as before. `run_request` is internal to run-batch, and the output file is the contract, which the tests check. `_ALL_RESPONSE_ADAPTER` is removed. **Scope.** I measured `/v1/embeddings` only. Score and rerank bodies take the same path now, with one float per document, so I expect a smaller gain there. **Overlap.** #65670 (completion-order output) touches the same `model_dump_json()` write line in `dispatch_batch`, so whichever lands second needs a one-line rebase. **Duplicate check.** As of 2026-11-05, open PR searches for `run_batch orjson`, `run-batch validate_json`, `run-batch embeddings response` and `run-batch output line` return nothing that changes this path. Among open PRs touching run-batch, #65670, #65029, #64102, #63848, #62895, #61145 and #51859 do not change the response conversion. ---

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Add the max_lora label to vllm:lora_requests_info
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Rust frontend's `vllm:lora_requests_info` gauge omits the `max_lora` label that the Python frontend sets, so dashboards and alerts that select or group by `max_lora` find nothing under the Rust frontend. This PR adds it, reading `max_loras` from the engines' ready responses.

## Claims

- With `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1` and LoRA enabled, `/metrics` exports `vllm:lora_requests_info{max_lora="<max_loras>",running_lora_adapters="...",waiting_lora_adapters="..."}`, the same label set and order as Python's `prometheus_client` output.
- No CLI or server wiring changes: the value comes from the startup handshake.

## Validation

`metrics::tests::lora_info_emits_clears_stale_and_drains` now snapshots the full label set (`max_lora="4"` first); it fails if the exporter emits a constant instead of the configured value. The label order was checked against `prometheus_client.generate_latest`, which sorts labels by name.

Rust CI set (`.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`) on this branch:

```bash
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check                    # clean
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                                           # clean
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # clean
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings  # clean
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2556 tests run: 2556 passed, 13 skipped
```

## Details

Python's `PrometheusStatLogger` registers the gauge with `max_lora` (`vllm_config.lora_config.max_loras` as a decimal string), `waiting_lora_adapters` and `running_lora_adapters` (`vllm/v1/metrics/loggers.py`).

- `LoraInfoLabels` (`vllm-metrics`) gains `max_lora` as its first field; field order is the exposition order.
- `ClientInner::new` (`vllm-engine-core-client`) already receives the connected engines and `validate_lora_capabilities` already requires them to agree on `max_loras`, so it keeps the value next to `engine_stats_enabled`, and the output dispatcher loop builds `LoraInfoExporter` from it. The exporter stays local to the dispatcher task, which is the only one that mutates it.

**Not a duplicate.** vllm-project/vllm#63261 (open, Python) fixes which adapters Python reports as waiting versus running; it does not touch the label set or the Rust frontend. No open PR adds `max_lora` to the Rust gauge.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Export vllm:cache_config_info like Python
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Rust frontend does not export `vllm:cache_config_info`, which the Python frontend exports as an info gauge labeled with every `CacheConfig.metrics_info()` field plus `engine`. This PR has the engine report `CacheConfig.metrics_info()` in its ready response, and the Rust frontend export the gauge from it, one series per engine. Closes vllm-project/vllm#65277.

## Claims

- With `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`, `/metrics` exports `vllm:cache_config_info`, value `1`, one series per engine, with the same label set as the Python frontend (every `CacheConfig.metrics_info()` field plus `engine`).
- Like Python, the gauge exists only when engines record stats (Python creates it with its stat logger).
- Engine side: `EngineCoreReadyResponse` gains an optional `cache_config_info: dict[str, str]`, set from the engine's `CacheConfig` after initialization. The Python frontend ignores it.

## Validation

GB200, `vllm serve` with the Python frontend and with the Rust frontend (`VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`, `vllm-rs` built from this change), `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` with `--data-parallel-size 2`, scraping `/metrics`:

| Frontend | Series | Label set | Values that differ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Python | `engine="0"`, `engine="1"` | 40 labels | — |
| Rust | `engine="0"`, `engine="1"` | the same 40 labels | `kv_cache_layout` `LBHNC` (Python `None`); `num_gpu_blocks` `39936` per engine (Python `79872`, the sum) |

Single-engine `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, hybrid `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B`, and `ibm-research/PowerMoE-3b` with DP2 and EP show the same label set as Python, with only the differences described under Details.

Rust CI set (`.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`) on this commit:

```bash
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check                    # clean
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                                           # clean
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # clean
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings  # clean
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2544 tests run: 2544 passed, 13 skipped
```

New tests, both failing without this change:
- `cache_config_info_exports_each_engine_cache_config`: two engines, one series each with their own labels.
- `python_msgpack_fixtures_match_rust_encoding_and_record_nixl_metrics` (extended): the new ready-response field decodes from Python's msgpack encoding.

`pre-commit run --files` on the changed Python files (ruff, mypy and the other hooks): clean.

## Details

**Why the engine reports the labels.** The Rust frontend has no source for most of these fields: the startup handshake carries only `num_gpu_blocks`, `block_size` and `kv_cache_size_tokens`, while Python's label set is the whole `CacheConfig.metrics_info()`. The labels describe the engine's cache, so the engine reports them after initialization (`EngineCoreProc._make_ready_response`, one line plus the field). On the Rust side, `vllm-engine-core-client` decodes the field, and `SchedulerStatsRecorder::new`, where the per-engine metric handles are resolved, sets one series per engine. The family lives with the other scheduler-stats families in `vllm-metrics`.

**Differences from the Python frontend.** Label values come from the engine's config after initialization, not from the Python frontend's copy of it:
- Labels the Python frontend never syncs carry the engine's resolved values: on `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, `kv_cache_layout` `LBHNC`, `hash_block_size` `16` and `cache_hit_alignment_tokens` `16`, where Python reports `None`; on the hybrid `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B`, also `mamba_page_size_padded`.
- Under DP, each engine's series carries that engine's own capacity labels. The Python frontend's copy sums `num_gpu_blocks` across engines and keeps the first engine's `kv_cache_size_tokens` and `kv_cache_max_concurrency` (`MPClient._apply_ready_response`), and repeats those values on every engine's series.

**Not a duplicate.** vllm-project/vllm#65462 (opened 2026-11-03) also targets this metric, but exports only the three capacity labels the handshake already carries. That keeps the Rust family's label set different from Python's, so queries and dashboards that select other labels (for example `tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py` reads `mamba_block_size`) would not work on the Rust frontend. This PR exports the full label set from the engine. No other open PR covers it.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Use a repository-scoped Docker Hub secret for release publishing
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Move Release v2 Docker Hub publishing to a repository-scoped organization token stored in Buildkite Secrets. Update nightly cleanup to authenticate with that token and document its access policy.

## Claims

- All seven Docker Hub publishing steps request `VLLM_DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` as `RELEASE_DOCKERHUB_TOKEN`, using organization username `vllm`.
- Nightly cleanup uses the organization-token-compatible Hub API, keeps credentials out of shell traces and command arguments, and exits on authentication, listing, or deletion HTTP failures.
- Publishing destinations and nightly retention rules are unchanged.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run --files .buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml .buildkite/scripts/cleanup-nightly-builds.sh .buildkite/scripts/rocm/publish.sh docs/contributing/ci/nightly_builds.md` — passed.
- `bash -n` and `shellcheck` on both modified shell scripts — passed.
- Local fixture harness against the actual cleanup script: empty results, authentication failure, listing failure, successful retention of 14 tags, and deletion failure — passed. The harness also rejected credentials in command arguments or shell traces and checked all seven secret mappings and publishing queues.
- Live credential validation: https://buildkite.com/vllm/release-v2/builds/10075 — passed. All four repositories passed image pushes, amd64/arm64 manifest inspection, tag listing and deletion. Writes to Omni and Router were denied, and a CPU build worker was denied access to the publishing secret. Temporary tags from this run and previous failed runs were removed.
- No model or serving changes; model evaluations are not applicable. This is not a full release build.

## Details

The secret must already exist in the dedicated release cluster, restricted to Release v2, `main` / `releases/*`, and the small CPU publishing queue. Its Docker Hub Image Push, Image Delete, and Tag Admin permissions cover only `vllm-openai`, `vllm-openai-cpu`, `vllm-openai-rocm`, and `vllm-openai-xpu`. Agent 3.106.0 or newer is required for step-level secrets.

Image Push + Tag Admin alone produced HTTP 500 on tag deletion in live validation; adding Image Delete resolved it on all four repositories.

Legacy credentials should be removed only after production cutover and verification of all remaining consumers. This PR changes credential consumption; it does not itself revoke credentials or configure external secret policies.

Open-PR searches for Docker Hub secrets and release credentials found no duplicate. This complements the merged ROCm build-login removal in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65889. commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Accept an empty tools array like OpenAI
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

vllm-project/vllm#65547 made the Python frontend accept `tools: []` on `/v1/chat/completions` like OpenAI: the empty list behaves like an omitted `tools`, and `auto`/`required` fall back to `none` because there is nothing to call. The Rust frontend still returns 400 "`tools` must not be an empty array" (from vllm-project/vllm#63060, which matched the old Python behavior). This PR removes the rejection and applies the same fallback.

## Claims

- `tools: []` with `tool_choice` absent, `none`, `auto` or `required` is served as a plain chat (`required` makes no tool call), on `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/chat/completions/render`.
- A named `tool_choice` with `tools: []` is still a 400 (no matching function).
- Tools declared in a developer message stay available: `[]` behaves exactly like an omitted `tools`.

## Validation

OpenAI API (2026-11-04, `tools: []`): `tool_choice` absent, `none`, `auto`, `required` → 200 (no tool call for `required`); named `f` → 400 "no function named 'f' was specified".

New tests: `prepare_chat_request_treats_empty_tools_as_omitted`, `prepare_chat_request_keeps_developer_tools_with_empty_tools`, `prepare_chat_request_rejects_named_tool_choice_with_empty_tools`, and the render-route test `chat_render_treats_empty_tools_as_omitted` (replaces `chat_rejects_empty_tools_array`; each case returns the same body as a request without `tools`). On the base every case fails with the old 400; with only the `tool_choice` mapping reverted, `auto`/`required` fail with `ToolChoiceRequiresTools`.

Rust CI set (`.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`) on this branch:

```bash
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check                    # clean
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                                           # clean
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # clean
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings  # clean
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2559 tests run: 2559 passed, 13 skipped
```

Once this lands, `tests/tool_use/test_chat_completions.py::test_chat_completion_with_empty_tools` can drop its `skipif(VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND)`.

## Details

- `validate.rs`: the empty-list rejection is removed; tool-type checks for non-empty lists stay.
- `prepare_chat_request` (shared by chat and chat render): when `tools` is an explicit `[]` and no developer message declares tools, `auto` and `required` map to `none` before `ResolvedToolContext::new`, which would otherwise return `ToolChoiceRequiresTools`. `ResolvedToolContext` is unchanged, so an omitted `tools` with `auto`/`required` still behaves as in Python.
- Python ignores developer-message tools in this check; Rust already resolves `auto` against them for an omitted `tools`, so `[]` keeps them available rather than introducing a second behavior.
- The named-choice error keeps Rust's existing message ("tool_choice function `f` was not found in the available tools"), which `/v1/responses` shares; only the wording differs from Python.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR changes the Rust handling of an empty `tools` array.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Return FastAPI-style JSON 400 errors for bad dev route query strings
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Rust frontend answers a bad query value on `/get_world_size`, `/server_info` and `/reset_prefix_cache` with axum's plain-text 400, and on every dev route reports `param: null` (or a hard-coded `"mode"`) and `type: "BadRequestError"`. The Python frontend sends all of them through FastAPI's validation handler: a JSON `ErrorResponse` with `param: "query.<name>"` and `type: "Bad Request"`. This PR matches that on every Rust dev route with query parameters.

## Claims

- `/sleep`, `/pause`, `/checkpoint/prepare`, `/get_world_size`, `/server_info` and `/reset_prefix_cache` return `400 application/json` for an invalid query value, with `param` naming the failing field (`query.include_dp`, `query.mode`, `query.clear_cache`, ...) and `type: "Bad Request"`, like Python.
- `--log-error-stack` (vllm-project/vllm#65001) now sees these errors, since they are `ApiError`s.
- Not matched: the message stays serde's deserializer text (Python prints pydantic's error list).

## Validation

`dev_routes_reject_invalid_query_with_json_error` sends a bad value to each of the six routes, asserts `400` with `Content-Type: application/json`, and snapshots `param` and `type`; `pause_route_rejects_invalid_mode` now expects `query.mode` and `Bad Request`. On the base the first fails at JSON decoding (axum's plain-text body) and the second on `type`. Python's routes return the same status, content type, `type`, `param` and `code` for the same requests.

This also unblocks `tests/entrypoints/rl/state_transitions/test_pause_resume.py::test_invalid_mode_preserves_state` and `test_sleep.py::test_sleep_route_rejects_invalid_query_before_dispatch` under the Rust frontend, which pin the `query.<name>` format.

Rust CI set (`.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`) on this branch:

```bash
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check                    # clean
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                                           # clean
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # clean
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings  # clean
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2557 tests run: 2557 passed, 13 skipped
```

## Details

Two commits:

1. **JSON 400 on every dev route.** `/sleep`, `/pause` and `/checkpoint/prepare` already mapped `QueryRejection` to `ApiError`; `/get_world_size`, `/server_info` and `/reset_prefix_cache` used the plain `Query` extractor.
2. **Name the failing field.** New `ApiError::InvalidQuery { message, param }` with `impl From<QueryRejection>`, next to `From<JsonRejection>`. Axum's `Query` deserializes through `serde_path_to_error`, so the conversion walks the rejection's source chain for that error and reports its path as `query.<name>`; without a path, `param` stays unset. Every dev route converts with `?`, and the per-route helpers are gone. `vllm-server` depends on `serde_path_to_error` directly (already a workspace dependency, and axum's).

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR changes the Rust dev routes' query errors.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Model Loader] Make the EP weight filter EPLB-aware
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Let `--enable-ep-weight-filter` work with `--enable-eplb`. Since #37322 the loader turns the filter off whenever EPLB is enabled, so every rank of an EPLB deployment reads every expert weight. This derives the experts each rank needs from EPLB's initial placement instead. Follow-up to #37136, #37351 and #37322.

## Claims

- With EPLB, each rank reads only the experts its physical slots hold in the initial placement, including redundant replicas. DeepSeek-R1-0528-NVFP4-v2 with DEP8 and 32 redundant experts: **105.2 GiB per rank instead of 384.9 GiB** (the plain EP filter without EPLB reads 100.1 GiB).
- Outputs match EPLB without the filter within run-to-run noise, across 32-33 rebalancing steps: GSM8K 0.9636 vs 0.9621 (A/A 0.9629), and the same final answer on 97.4% of questions, equal to the A/A agreement. Weight loading on a warm page cache: 43.6 s to 39.8 s (A/A 43.9 s).
- The comparison is sensitive: a negative control that applies the plain EP filter under EPLB (main without #37322's guard) falls far outside the run-to-run noise.
- Falls back to loading every expert, as on main, for elastic EP and whenever the model's MoE layout (`num_logical_experts`, `num_physical_experts`) differs from the config, e.g. for MoE models that don't implement `MixtureOfExperts`.

## Validation

**Unit tests** (macOS CPU, `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`):

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_ep_weight_filter.py
# 44 passed (7 new)
```

The new unit tests check the expert set against `determine_expert_map` plus the initial map on every rank, coverage of all logical experts, an iterator-level regression for redundant slots, and the model-side round-robin to linear fallback under EPLB that the filter relies on.

**End-to-end test** (new, `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_ep_weight_filter_eplb.py`, 2 GPUs): `luccafong/deepseek_mtp_main_random`, already used in CI, with TP2 + EP + synchronous EPLB and 2 redundant experts, so rank 1's redundant slots replicate experts from rank 0's EP shard. Under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` (set by the test), the filter-off and filter-on runs must produce identical tokens while EPLB rebalances mid-generation, and the filter must log that it engaged. It runs in a new nightly 2xB200 step and is skipped on ROCm, where MLA lacks batch invariance.

Run on 2xB300 in the same nightly image as the A/B below, first as is (main) and then with this PR's two loader files mounted:

```bash
python -m pytest -v -s tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_ep_weight_filter_eplb.py
```

main, where the filter never engages under EPLB:

```
E           AssertionError: expected the filter on
FAILED tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_ep_weight_filter_eplb.py::test_ep_weight_filter_matches_unfiltered_with_eplb
```

this PR (EPLB rearranged experts 12 times across the two runs):

```
(Worker_TP0_EP0 pid=3272835) INFO 10-28 02:16:45 [default_loader.py:511] EP weight filter: ep_size=2, ep_rank=0, loading 37/72 experts
PASSED
========================= 1 passed in 89.80s (0:01:29) =========================
```

**End-to-end A/B** (one 8xB300 node, `vllm/vllm-openai:cu134-nightly-5d35ce3934a7804b298559d2d99eec33792e1eb9` with this PR's two loader files mounted over the image's copies, as of 2cbb82aee4; later commits change only comments, docs and tests; the A/A arm reruns the unmodified image to measure noise):

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/DeepSeek-R1-0528-NVFP4-v2 --data-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --enable-eplb --eplb-config '{"window_size":100,"step_interval":200,"num_redundant_experts":32,"use_async":false,"communicator":"torch_nccl"}' \
  --enable-ep-weight-filter --max-num-seqs 64
```

The small EPLB window and interval make rebalancing happen during the evaluation.

| | main (filter skipped) | this PR | main again (A/A) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `EP weight filter` log | none | `loading 36/256 experts` | none |
| `Rearranged experts` events | 33 | 32 | 33 |
| GPU KV cache tokens | 4,779,264 | 4,779,264 | 4,779,264 |
| GSM8K accuracy (1319 questions, max_tokens 2048) | 0.9621 | 0.9636 | 0.9629 |
| GSM8K same final answer as main | — | 97.4% | 97.4% |
| greedy smoke identical to main (4 prompts) | — | 1/4 | 2/4 |
| prompt-logprob top-1 agreement with main (640 / 20k / 118k tokens) | — | 95.8% / 94.6% / 77.9% | 95.9% / 94.7% / 77.8% |
| `Loading weights took` (rank 0) | 43.62 s | 39.81 s | 43.88 s |
| `Model loading took` (8 ranks) | 57.4-58.1 s | 54.2-54.8 s | 56.5-56.8 s |

This configuration is not bitwise deterministic even between two runs of the same image, so the PR column is compared with the A/A column rather than expecting identical outputs.

**Negative control** (separate job on the same kind of node, smoke only): mounting the nightly loader with only #37322's EPLB guard removed, i.e. the plain EP partition under EPLB (`loading 32/256 experts`), leaves 144 of the 288 physical slots without their weights. Compared with main in the same job, greedy outputs are identical for 0/4 prompts and prompt-logprob top-1 agreement drops to 75.3% / 80.4% / 31.5%, far outside the A/A noise above (95.9% / 94.7% / 77.8%). Its short greedy answers can still be correct, so the logprob comparison, not answer accuracy alone, is what separates a wrong expert set from run-to-run noise.

Load times were measured with the checkpoint already in the page cache (NFS, where vLLM also auto-prefetches), the same condition as #37136's numbers; the saving comes from not materializing non-local expert tensors. The 8 ranks of one node share the page cache and together need every expert, so reads from storage don't shrink on a single node; the per-rank saving matters more where ranks read independently, e.g. EP across nodes or a page cache that cannot hold the checkpoint.

pre-commit passes.

## Details

- **Root cause.** EPLB allocates N + R physical slots per MoE layer and splits them linearly across EP ranks. Slot p initially holds logical expert `initial_map[p]` from `EplbState.build_initial_global_physical_to_logical_map` (identity, then `i % N` for the redundant slots), so a rank's redundant slots replicate experts from other ranks' default partitions. The plain filter skips those, which left the replicas uninitialized; #37322 therefore disabled the filter under EPLB.
- **Fix.** The filter keeps `{initial_map[p] for p in this rank's physical slots}`, built from the same map `RoutedExperts.build_expert_params_mapping` uses to route checkpoint tensors to slots, so the two cannot disagree. Rebalancing moves weights GPU-to-GPU and never re-reads the checkpoint, so loading only has to satisfy the initial placement. Custom initial maps (#49572, open) are applied after loading through `rearrange_expert_weights_inplace`, so they stay compatible.
- **Linear placement.** `determine_expert_placement_strategy` refuses round-robin when EPLB is enabled, so the filter always splits physical slots linearly; a test pins this.
- **Layout check.** The expert set comes from the config, so it is used only when the model reports the matching `MixtureOfExperts` layout (resolved with `get_mixture_of_experts_model`, which unwraps VLMs). This matters because `--enable-eplb` is accepted for MoE models that don't implement `MixtureOfExperts`: EPLB is simply not registered for them, and they allocate only N slots, so the EPLB set would skip experts they need.
- **Loaders.** Every loader that consumes `local_expert_ids` uses the new set under EPLB: the safetensors iterator (all load strategies; auto-prefetch on NFS still reads whole files, but tensors are skipped per name) and InstantTensor (#61167), which was not validated end to end. The multi-threaded and fastsafetensors loaders don't filter at all (#48891 addresses the former).
- **Test coverage.** The fallback for a mismatched layout has no automated test: exercising it needs a MoE model whose layout disagrees with its config, and the guard is a single comparison.
- **Unchanged.** Elastic EP keeps loading every expert (padded capacity, placement evolves at runtime). Scale and metadata tensors are still never filtered, so #37322's NVFP4 fix is untouched.
- **Not a duplicate.** Open PRs and issues searched for "EP weight filter EPLB", "ep_weight_filter", "enable-ep-weight-filter", "37322 in:body" and "weight filter redundant experts" found nothing equivalent. Related but orthogonal: #48891 (apply the filter in the multithreaded safetensors loader) and #63075 (EPLB expert-weight regions in `RoutedExperts`).
- **Limitations.** Not validated with speculative decoding; DeepSeek MTP's MoE follows the same EPLB layout and passes the check, but the run above has no drafter.

AI assistance (Kimi Code and Claude Code) was used to write this change and run the validation above. I reviewed every changed line and the results.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Echo prompt-cache and safety_identifier fields in Responses
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Rust Responses API drops `prompt_cache_key`, `prompt_cache_options`, `prompt_cache_retention` and `safety_identifier`, so its response objects lack keys that the Python frontend (vllm-project/vllm#62856, vllm-project/vllm#32824) and OpenAI echo back, and invalid values such as `prompt_cache_retention: "1w"` are accepted. This PR declares and echoes them like Python. vLLM does not act on any of them.

## Claims

- The four fields are echoed on every response object (non-streaming, and `response.created`, `response.in_progress`, `response.completed`), `null` when absent, like Python.
- `prompt_cache_options` gets Python's defaults (`mode: "implicit"`, `ttl: "30m"`, `comparison_response_id: null`) and drops the request-only `prewarm`; `prompt_cache_retention` accepts the legacy `in-memory` spelling and echoes `in_memory`.
- Unknown retention, mode and ttl values are a 400 at deserialization, like Python's `Literal` fields.
- Not added: Python's vLLM-only `input_messages`/`output_messages` keys (always `null` without `enable_response_messages`, which the Rust frontend rejects; OpenAI has no such keys).

## Validation

OpenAI Responses API (2026-11-04, `store: false`): it echoes all four fields and applies the same `prompt_cache_options` defaults, dropping `prewarm`. The remaining differences are Python's, kept for parity: OpenAI rejects `in-memory`, reports its model-default retention instead of `null`, and omits `null` option keys.

- `responses_echoes_prompt_cache_and_safety_fields`: absent fields as present `null` keys on the non-streaming response; populated fields on all three lifecycle events. It ports the cases of `tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_serving_responses.py` (`test_prompt_cache_key_is_echoed`, `test_safety_identifier_is_echoed`, `test_prompt_cache_options_echo_applied_defaults`, ...), which are in-process unit tests.
- `responses_rejects_invalid_controls_before_inference`: three new 400 rows (retention, mode, ttl).

Both fail on the base (`missing prompt_cache_key`; `"1w"` returns 200).

Rust CI set (`.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`) on this branch:

```bash
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check                    # clean
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                                           # clean
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # clean
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings  # clean
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2557 tests run: 2557 passed, 13 skipped
```

## Details

The fields are wire-only, so they stay in the Responses DTO (`routes/openai/responses/types.rs`). Together with three existing fields that the route also only validates (at most) and echoes (`max_tool_calls`, `metadata`, `user`), they live in `ResponseEchoFields`, which is `#[serde(flatten)]`ed into both `ResponsesRequest` and `ResponsesResponse` and carried on `ResponseMeta` as one value instead of being declared, destructured and reassigned field by field. The JSON is unchanged except that the response now serializes these keys after its other keys. Fields the route reads or transforms (`service_tier`, `previous_response_id`, `text`, `truncation`, `reasoning`, `top_logprobs`, `tools`, `tool_choice`) stay as they are.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR adds these fields to the Rust Responses API.

**AI assistance.** This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). The human submitter reviewed every changed line and the validation results.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Support namespace tools in the Responses API
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Rust frontend rejects every `/v1/responses` request that carries a `namespace` tool (`unknown variant 'namespace'`, 400), so Codex-style clients that group MCP tools under namespaces cannot use it. This PR supports namespace tools the way the Python frontend does (vllm-project/vllm#47024, vllm-project/vllm#53763, vllm-project/vllm#59723).

## Claims

- Each function of a `namespace` tool is shown to the model as a flat function tool named `<namespace>__<name>`, in request order, keeping its description, parameters and `strict`.
- A call of a flat name is reported as a `function_call` item with the function's own `name` and its `namespace`, in the non-streaming output and in the streamed `output_item.added`, `function_call_arguments.done` and `output_item.done` events. The flat name is never exposed.
- A `function_call` history item with a `namespace` is replayed under the flat name.
- A named `tool_choice` resolves by exact name first (including the flat name), then by a function name defined in exactly one namespace; an ambiguous name is a 400 with Python's message.
- Differences from Python: a call without a namespace omits the `namespace` key instead of serializing `null`, like the other optional keys Rust's output items already omit; a `custom` tool inside a namespace is a 400 instead of being dropped silently, as a top-level `custom` tool already is.

## Validation

- `routes::tests::responses::responses_namespace_tool_call_reports_function_name_and_namespace`: HTTP route against the mock engine, the model emitting the flat `mcp__computer_use__get_app_state` call through the Qwen tool parser; checks the non-streaming output, the streamed events, the terminal response and the echoed `tools`. Its assertions port those of `tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_namespace_tool_separator.py`.
- `namespace_tools_reach_the_model_by_their_flat_names`: the flat tool list, the resolved and echoed `tool_choice`, and history replay.
- `tools::tests`: flattening order and fields, inner `custom` rejection, the reverse map, and tool-choice resolution (exact, flat, unique local name, ambiguous and missing).

On `main` every request with a `namespace` tool is a 400; disabling the reverse map or the flattening fails the corresponding tests. `test_namespace_tool_separator.py` is server-level and fits the existing Rust Frontend Responses API CI step; it can be enabled there after this lands.

Rust CI set (`.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`) on this branch:

```bash
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check                    # clean
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                                           # clean
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # clean
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings  # clean
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2562 tests run: 2562 passed, 13 skipped
```

## Details

Namespaces are a Responses wire concept: the chat layer and the tool parsers only ever see flat function tools. So the naming lives in a new `responses/tools.rs` in the Responses route:

- `ToolIdentity { namespace, name }` is the client-side identity; its `flat_name` is the only place the `__` spelling is built.
- `ResponsesToolNames::convert` walks the request tools once, producing the flat tool list handed to `ResolvedToolContext` and a request-local map from each flat name to its namespace length. `decode` slices the identity out of a called name, and `resolve_choice` resolves a named `tool_choice`.
- `OutputItemStreamer` takes the map at construction (non-streaming consumes the same streamer), and `create_responses` builds the streamer once for both paths.

Like Python, the flattening is a mechanical join without collision handling: a plain tool named `crm__get` next to namespace `crm` with function `get` both reach the model as `crm__get`. The `__` join reproduces the flat names Codex itself used before namespaces (`mcp__<server>__<tool>`), and Codex already deduplicates on its side.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR adds namespace tools to the Rust Responses API; vllm-project/vllm#58783 (draft) predates the stateless Responses API on `main` and does not cover namespaces.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Keep whitespace in HY tool-call argument names
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Rust HY tool parser (shared by `hy_v3` and `hy_v4`) trims tool-call argument names, so schema keys that differ only by surrounding whitespace collide. vllm-project/vllm#61542 made the Python HYV4 streaming parser keep argument names exactly ("Property names are exact schema keys, including whitespace"); this PR does the same in Rust for both dialects, streaming and non-streaming.

## Claims

- With properties `count` (string) and ` count ` (integer), the call `count=2, " count "=7` now parses to `{"count": "2", " count ": 7}`; before, the second key overwrote the first and took the wrong schema type (`{"count": "7"}`).
- Function names are still trimmed, as in Python.

## Validation

New test `tool::hy::tests::whitespace_distinguishes_argument_names` (both dialects, complete input and one-character streaming), ported from `tests/tool_parsers/test_hy_v4_tool_parser.py::test_whitespace_distinguishes_argument_names`. It fails with the `trim()` restored (`left: {"count": "7"}`).

Rust CI set (`.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`) on this branch:

```bash
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check                    # clean
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                                           # clean
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # clean
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings  # clean
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2557 tests run: 2557 passed, 13 skipped
```

The first workspace nextest run had one unrelated failure, `vllm-engine-core-client` `tests::client::connect_times_out_without_ready_message` (a timing-sensitive mock-engine test in a crate this PR does not touch); it passes alone and in a full rerun, which is the summary above.

## Details

HY calls carry each argument as `<arg_key>NAME</arg_key><arg_value>VALUE</arg_value>`, where `NAME` is a property key of the tool's schema. The fix drops the `trim()` on `NAME` in the shared parameter parser in `vllm-parser`; the downstream schema lookup already keys on the exact name, and Rust's HY structural tag already emits each key as an exact constant, so under constrained decoding the parser now agrees with the grammar.

The Hy3 chat template renders history keys verbatim, so trimming is lossy cleanup rather than a protocol rule. Python's non-streaming HYV3 and HYV4 parsers already kept the names verbatim; Python's HYV3 streaming parser still strips them (`hy_v3_tool_parser.py`), which Rust does not reproduce, since it has one parser for both modes.

**Not a duplicate.** The open HY parser PRs (vllm-project/vllm#60788, Python streaming JSON for duplicate keys; vllm-project/vllm#54488, empty function names) touch different behavior.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Support echo with truncate_prompt_tokens
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Python accepts `echo=true` together with `truncate_prompt_tokens` on `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/completions`. The Rust frontend rejected the combination with a 400 ("`echo=true` is not supported with `truncate_prompt_tokens`") in the shared `validate_generation_prompt_truncation`. This PR lifts the rejection and makes the completions echo match the tokens actually sent to the engine, as Python's renderer does since vllm-project/vllm#61876.

## Claims

- The 400 is gone on both routes; `validate_generation_prompt_truncation` keeps only its `>= -1` check.
- **Chat** echoes the last assistant message's content, which truncation does not change (Python `chat_completion/serving.py`); Rust's chat echo already comes from the request messages.
- **Completions, token-ID prompt**: truncation is applied up front and the echo is the decode of the tokens that remain, matching Python's renderer (`renderers/base.py`, `test_detokenization_matches_truncated_tokens`).
- **Completions, text prompt**: echoes its text as sent, truncated or not, as Python `main` does today. Token-ID prompts with `return_token_ids` still echo an empty string. Both unchanged.

## Validation

New tests in `vllm-server` (all three fail on `main`; with the rejection removed but the echo still decoding the untruncated IDs, the two completions tests fail):

- `routes::tests::non_stream_completions_echo_reports_the_truncated_prompt`: token IDs of `hello world`, `truncate_prompt_tokens=5` (left): the engine gets `world`, the response text is `worldhi`, `prompt_tokens=5`.
- `routes::tests::completions_echo_stream_reports_the_truncated_prompt`: streaming, right side, limit 5: token IDs of `hello world` echo `hello`; the text prompt `hello world` echoes `hello world`.
- `routes::tests::chat_completions_echo_stream_with_prompt_truncation`: the engine gets 4 prompt tokens and the stream content is `Sure, hi`.

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`, all green on this branch's head:

```bash
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust   # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2546 tests run: 2546 passed, 13 skipped
```

Python tests: no server-level Python test pins echo with truncation on `main`; `test_detokenization_matches_truncated_tokens` is a renderer unit test whose token-ID left and right cases the tests above mirror. The change touches only `rust/`.

## Details

**Ownership.** Truncation stays in `vllm-text` (`PromptTruncation::apply`, reached through `TextRequestProcessor`), the only code that knows which prompt tokens remain. The completions converter in `vllm-server`, which builds the echo, asks it for the final tokens instead of decoding the request's: a token-ID prompt with `echo` goes through `TextRequestProcessor::tokenize_in_place`, the existing entry point chat uses to get final prompt tokens before submission. The request then carries the final token IDs, so generation does not truncate again. Without truncation the call only validates and keeps the IDs, and the echo is the decode of the whole prompt, as before.

**Signature change.** `prepare_completion_request` (and `lower_completion_request`, used by `/v1/completions/render`) now takes the `TextRequestProcessor` instead of the bare tokenizer it used only for echo; the convert tests build one from a two-method test backend (mechanical change at 20 call sites). `/v1/completions/render` shares this lowering, so it also computes the echo it discards; the extra work is one decode of a token-ID prompt that render tokenizes anyway, as it already did for untruncated token-ID echo.

**Known follow-up: text prompts.** Python echoes a truncated text prompt as sent, because the tokenizer truncates while encoding and the renderer only detokenizes prompts without text. Open vllm-project/vllm#62691 changes that for an explicit `truncation_side`, excluding the special tokens the tokenizer added (BOS, appended EOS) through an encoding-time special-tokens mask. This PR follows Python `main`. Porting that behavior to Rust needs the same mask: locating the text's own tokens by re-encoding cannot tell an added BOS or EOS from the same token written by the client (for example a literal `"<s>"` in the prompt), and `vllm-tokenizer` does not expose the mask yet. That is a follow-up once vllm-project/vllm#62691 lands.

**Contract.** OpenAI has no `truncate_prompt_tokens`. For token-ID prompts, echo plus logprobs now reports the kept tokens' logprobs against the kept tokens' text.

**Not a duplicate.** vllm-project/vllm#62691 changes the Python renderers for text prompts and does not touch the Rust frontend. vllm-project/vllm#62684 edits the same Rust completions files but changes echo with `return_token_ids` for string prompts, not truncation. No other open PR lifts the Rust echo/truncation rejection.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this change; the human submitter reviewed every changed line.
