commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Restore engine memory budget after IPC fallback
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

When `ipc_cache` falls back to disk (e.g. the daemon is reachable but its weights do not match the engine config), the worker keeps charging the daemon's weights against its memory budget even though it no longer maps them, so the KV cache is smaller than with a direct disk load by the daemon's weight size. This removes the charge of each model that falls back, so a fallback is sized exactly like a direct disk load.

Follow-up to #62583.

## Claims

- After an IPC disk fallback, the engine budget and KV cache size match a direct disk load (Qwen3-4B, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.1`: KV cache 10.82 → 18.34 GiB, equal to the direct load).
- Only the charge of the model (target or draft) that fell back is removed; models still mapped from the daemon keep theirs.

## Validation

Setup: NVIDIA B300, TP1, eager, `max_model_len=1024`, `max_num_batched_tokens=1024`, `max_num_seqs=1`, FlashInfer autotune off. The daemon (`vllm preload --dtype bfloat16`) and the engine (`dtype="float16"`, `load_format="ipc_cache"`, `fallback=True`) differ in dtype, so the engine logs `Weight cache unusable (WeightCacheKey mismatch on fields: ['dtype']); falling back to disk loading`. Direct-load baselines use `load_format="auto"` with the same daemon running. Outputs are greedy, 8 tokens, for "The capital of France is". The `gpu_memory_utilization=0.1` runs shared the GPU with an unrelated workload.

**Regression test** (`test_ipc_fallback_restores_memory_budget`, Qwen3-0.6B, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.1`):

| Model runner | upstream main (`c126ebf159`) | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| MRV2 (extensible KV cache) | failed: `assert 27539026292 == 28741612340` | passed |
| MRV1 (estimate-based sizing) | failed: `assert 27539026292 == 28741612340` | passed |

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn \
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py::test_ipc_fallback_restores_memory_budget
# Repeat with VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 for MRV1.
```

**Fallback vs. upstream main** (Qwen3-4B, extensible KV cache, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.1`):

| | upstream main, fallback | This PR, fallback | Direct disk load |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Engine budget | 19.27 GiB | 26.77 GiB | 26.77 GiB |
| KV cache | 10.82 GiB | 18.34 GiB | 18.34 GiB |
| Output | identical | identical | reference |

**Sizing modes with this PR:**

| Case | Fallback | Direct disk load |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-0.6B, extensible off, util 0.1 | budget 26.77 GiB, KV 25.5 GiB, same output | budget 26.77 GiB, KV 25.5 GiB |
| Qwen3-4B, extensible off, util 0.980986 (full budget exceeds startup free memory by 4 GiB) | `ValueError: Free memory on device cuda:0 (258.59/267.68 GiB) on startup is less than desired GPU memory utilization (0.980986, 262.59 GiB)` | same `ValueError` |
| Qwen3-4B, extensible on, util unset (1.0) | budget 267.68 GiB, KV 247.49 GiB, 0.32 GiB free after the KV cache is extended, output correct | budget 267.68 GiB, KV 248.34 GiB, 0.17 GiB free |

In the last row, the fallback's KV cache is 0.85 GiB smaller because post-warmup free memory was lower (248.44 vs. 249.31 GiB); the cause was not investigated.

Unit tests and lint:

- `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py::test_external_weight_fallback_preserves_other_role`, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py::test_request_memory_charges_external_weights`: **46 passed**.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: passed.

CI coverage: `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py` runs in `:nvidia: (H200 MIG 18GB) V1 Executor + Worker`. The single-GPU tests in `test_weight_cache.py`, including the regression test, run only in `:amd: (MI300) Model Executor`, because the NVIDIA Model Executor step is commented out in `.buildkite/test_areas/model_executor.yaml`; the NVIDIA results above were run locally. Not validated: TP > 1, ROCm, and an end-to-end run where only one of the target and draft falls back (covered by the accounting unit test).

## Details

**Root cause.** `Worker.init_device` charges daemon-held weights (`get_external_weight_memory`, added in #57298) before the model is loaded. If `IpcModelLoader.load_model` then falls back to disk, the engine allocates its own copy of the weights, but `requested_memory` still excludes the daemon's copy, so KV sizing pays for weights the engine does not map.

**Fix.**

- `IpcModelLoader` records each zero-copy daemon's charge by socket and role when it is queried, and after a successful disk fallback reports that role's charge once.
- `ExternalWeightCharges.track()` binds the worker's charges during the query and the model load and accumulates `fallback_bytes`.
- `Worker._resolve_requested_memory()` recomputes the budget with `external_weight_memory - fallback_bytes`, leaving `external_weight_memory` as queried at startup. It runs after `load_model` when a fallback happened, and in `disable_extensible_kv_cache`, which re-sizes after loading. Without a fallback, both paths behave as on main.

**Tradeoff.** A fallback now behaves like a direct disk load with the daemon as another process on the GPU. The daemon's resident weights are already excluded from `init_snapshot.free_memory`, so `request_memory`'s free-memory check and the extensible KV cache's measured sizing still bound physical memory. With estimate-based sizing, a configuration that fits only because the daemon's weights were charged (budget above startup free memory) now fails at startup after a fallback, as a direct disk load would, instead of running with a smaller KV cache.

**Duplicate work.** Searched open PRs for "ipc fallback memory budget", "external_weight_memory" and "weight cache fallback": no equivalent fix. #59813 restores model state before an IPC fallback; this PR fixes memory accounting after a successful fallback.

AI assistance (Codex and Claude Code) was used for implementation, review, and validation.

commits.pr_title: [Core][MLA] Cross-layer KV cache sharing for attention layers
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Model-agnostic enablement for MLA models in two areas: cross-layer KV sharing and PCP+DCP decode handling. No behavior change for existing models; each piece is opt-in or additive.

Not a duplicate: searched open PRs for KV-sharing / MLA enablement / PCP+DCP work — the open items cover KV-sharing prefill perf for a specific model family (#60445), DSv4.1 pipeline partitions (#63106), and compressed-MLA offloading (#63586); none generalize cross-layer KV sharing over `AttentionLayerBase` or move the PCP+DCP LSE merge into the base MLA forward.

## Claims

- **Cross-layer KV sharing:** `kv_sharing_target_layer_name` is declared on `AttentionLayerBase` and plumbed through `MLAAttention`. A layer that shares another layer's KV cache skips its own cache write, and the V2 runner resolves consumers to the sharing target's KV cache spec (`get_shared_kv_cache_layers` now walks `AttentionLayerBase`).
- **Sparse MLA only, with forced MQA:** KV sharing is supported by sparse MLA backends, and a sharing layer requires `sparse_mla_force_mqa`. The sparse MHA prefill paths attend over the layer's own new latent KV rather than the cache, and a sharing layer has no latent of its own, so the model must opt into the MQA path; otherwise initialization raises a `ValueError`. Dense MLA still rejects sharing, since its prefill always uses the layer's own latent.
- **PCP+DCP:** the decode-only LSE merge moved into the base `MLAAttention` forward (as DeepSeek-V3.2 does in its own forward), so MLA models opt in with `supports_pcp_dcp` instead of overriding `forward`.

## Validation

Unit tests on GB300:

```bash
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py        # 53 passed (extended by this PR, wired into CI)
pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_sharing.py          # 2 passed
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_pcp_manager.py   # 95 passed
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_dcp_a2a_pack_mask.py  # 354 passed
```

End to end on a tiny DeepSeek-V3-style DSA checkpoint (8 layers, 16 heads, random weights, `index_topk=512`) where layers 4 and 6 share the KV cache of layers 3 and 5 (test-only hook, not part of this PR), TP2 on the V2 runner, greedy 32 tokens, compared by the first diverging token against the same model without sharing:

| Config | Result |
|---|---|
| Sharing without `sparse_mla_force_mqa` (before the guard) | sharing layers ran dense MHA prefill over their own latent; all medium prompts diverged at token 0. Now rejected at init. |
| `sparse_mla_force_mqa`, sharing layers' own latent zeroed | identical to the unzeroed run, so the sharing layers read only the shared cache |
| DCP2, `--dcp-comm-backend ag_rs` | within run-to-run noise, no crash |
| DCP2, `--dcp-comm-backend a2a` (eager and FULL_DECODE_ONLY CUDA graphs) | within run-to-run noise, no crash |
| PCP2xDCP2, `ag_rs`, `fp8_ds_mla` | within run-to-run noise, no crash |
| PCP2xDCP2, `a2a` | rejected at startup by the existing MRV2 PCP check (`dcp_comm_backend='ag_rs'` required) |

On `--dcp-comm-backend a2a`: without PCP the partial-row LSE merge always takes the full-batch path, so a2a behaves as before. The partial-row merge is only reached under PCP, where a2a cannot be selected.

## Details

- The KV-sharing attribute is a typed default (`None`) on `AttentionLayerBase`, so discovery no longer relies on `getattr`/`hasattr` probing of arbitrary layers.
- Under PCP+DCP only the decode rows carry an LSE (prefill rows attended over the gathered KV), so the merge now applies to just those rows; the full-batch path is unchanged.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Pass assistant and tool content parts to HF templates like Python
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Rust frontend's HF chat renderer now passes assistant and tool message content to chat templates in the same shapes as the Python frontend: assistant text parts stay separate parts (joined with `"\n"` under the `string` content format), and a text-only tool result reaches the template as one string.

## Claims

- Assistant content parts are no longer concatenated without a separator: `["a", "b"]` renders as `"a\nb"` under `string` and as two text parts under `openai`, as in Python.
- A tool-call-only assistant message (`content: null`) gets `[]` under `openai` instead of `[{"type": "text", "text": ""}]`, which is truthy in Jinja.
- A text-only tool result reaches the template as one `"\n"`-joined string in both content formats, as in Python (vllm-project/vllm#39899, vllm-project/vllm#40190). Tool content with a non-text part stays a list.

## Validation

- New test `renderer::hf::tests::assistant_and_tool_content_parts_reach_templates` renders five messages through `tojson` under both content formats. Its snapshot matches Python's shapes (table below), except for the one documented difference. Red-green on the PR base `c58e7f6d05`: with only the production change reverted, the test fails (assistant parts render as `"ab"`, `openai` gets one merged part, `[{text: ""}]` for the tool-call-only message, and tool text stays a list); with the change, it passes.
- Rust CI set from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`, run on the branch head:
  - `cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check`: clean
  - `cargo sort --workspace --check rust`: clean
  - `cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans`: clean
  - `cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings`: clean
  - `cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast`: 2544 passed, 13 skipped
- No Python test pins these shapes (vllm-project/vllm#39899 and vllm-project/vllm#40190 added none); this PR changes no Python code.

## Details

**Python's behavior.** Python parses assistant and tool content with the same `parse_chat_message_content_parts` as every other role, then normalizes tool content (`vllm/renderers/chat_utils/chat_message.py`):

- **Assistant, `string`:** non-empty text parts joined with `"\n"`.
- **Assistant, `openai`:** the list of text parts as sent; `[]` for a message with only `tool_calls`.
- **Tool, either format:** a text-only content list is collapsed to one `"\n"`-joined string, because most templates only handle string tool content, and clients such as Claude Code and Cursor send tool results as text parts (vllm-project/vllm#39899). A list with a non-text item stays a list (vllm-project/vllm#40190).

Shapes from Python's `parse_chat_messages` on current `main`:

| Message | `string` | `openai` |
|---|---|---|
| assistant `["a", "", "b"]` | `"a\nb"` | `[{text: "a"}, {text: ""}, {text: "b"}]` |
| assistant, `content: null` + `tool_calls` | `""` | `[]` |
| tool `["x", "", "y"]` | `"x\ny"` | `"x\n\ny"` |
| tool `"x"` | `"x"` | `"x"` |

**Root cause in Rust.** The HF renderer built assistant content from `AssistantContentBlock::text()`, which concatenates the text blocks (one per request part) with no separator, and then lowered that single string. So `openai` templates got one text part (an empty one for tool-call-only messages). Tool content went through the generic path, so text parts stayed a list under `openai`.

**Change** (`rust/src/chat/src/renderer/hf/mod.rs`):

- `to_template_message` maps each assistant `Text` block to one text content part and lowers them through `to_template_content`, the path every other role already uses.
- New `to_template_tool_content` renders a text-only tool result as one string in both formats and leaves other tool content as before.

**Ownership and layering.** The consumer is the HF renderer, which builds the template's `messages`, so the fix stays in its message conversion. The shared `AssistantContentBlock::text()` is unchanged: output aggregation and the Harmony and GLM-5 Next renderers rely on plain concatenation. The dedicated renderers (DeepSeek V3.2, Inkling, Kimi K3) own their encodings and are out of scope.

**Other producers of assistant text blocks.**

- Chat completions makes one `Text` block per request content part, so the blocks are the parts.
- The Responses API conversion (vllm-project/vllm#63902) flattens each assistant input item to one text block per turn, so its rendering does not change.
- `/v1/messages` is not served by the Rust frontend.

**Why Python's behavior is the right target.** The assistant `"\n"` join is the general parts semantics Python applies to every role; in Rust, user and system content already followed it, and the server's own `continue_final_message` helper already joins assistant parts with `"\n"` (`chat_completions/convert.rs`). The tool collapse is deliberate (vllm-project/vllm#39899, refined by vllm-project/vllm#40190). OpenAI allows text parts for both roles; the join and the tool-string normalization are vLLM's template-input contract that HF templates are written against.

**One intentional difference.** An empty text part inside a text-only tool list is dropped under `openai` too (`"x\ny"`), as Python's own `string` path does. Python keeps it under `openai` (`"x\n\ny"`) only because its `openai` collapse is a separate join.

**No duplicate.** I searched open upstream PRs for assistant/tool content parts and HF template content in the Rust frontend. The nearest is vllm-project/vllm#65293, which chooses *which* content format a template gets by probing it; this PR fixes the *shape* of assistant and tool content within a given format, in a different function. vllm-project/vllm#64471 (accepting empty message content) changes request parsing in the server crate, not the renderer.

**AI assistance.** This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code). The human submitter reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Accept refusal content parts in assistant messages
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

OpenAI's chat API allows a `refusal` content part in assistant messages (`ChatCompletionContentPartRefusalParam`; the assistant `content` array is `text | refusal`), so a client that replays a model's refusal as structured history sends it. The Python frontend accepts it and replays the refusal string as text. The Rust frontend rejects the whole request at deserialization (`unknown variant 'refusal'`), because `ContentPart` only knows `text`, the three media URLs and `input_audio`.

This PR adds `ContentPart::Refusal` and lowers it where the role is known.

## Claims

- **Assistant messages:** a refusal part becomes an `AssistantContentBlock::Text`, like a text part, so every renderer sees it as the turn's text (the same choice the Rust Responses conversion already makes for `refusal` input parts). `echo` includes it, as Python's echo of the parsed last message does.
- **Other roles:** 400 with OpenAI's message, "Only assistant messages can have a 'refusal' content type."

## Validation

Python `vllm launch render` vs Rust `vllm-rs render` with this commit, both on `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` (HF renderer), `POST /v1/chat/completions/render` (measured on the same commit over main `39dbf51839`):

- assistant `[{"type":"refusal","refusal":"I can't."}]`: identical token IDs on both, and identical to the same turn sent as `"content": "I can't."`.
- user `[{"type":"refusal",...}]`: Python renders it as text; Rust returns the 400 above (intended, per OpenAI; see Details).

New tests in `vllm-server` `routes::openai::chat_completions::convert`, both failing on `main` (the request does not deserialize):

- `prepare_chat_request_replays_assistant_refusal_parts_as_text`: a JSON request whose assistant message is one refusal part (OpenAI's documented shape), with `echo`; asserts one assistant text block and the echo text.
- `prepare_chat_request_rejects_refusal_parts_outside_assistant_messages`: a user refusal part returns OpenAI's message.

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`, on this branch (main `c58e7f6d05` + this commit):

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust   # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2545 tests run: 2545 passed, 13 skipped
```

Model evaluation: none run. The change only affects requests that were previously rejected, and the token-ID comparison above checks the rendered prompt directly.

## Details

**Layering.** The role-dependent rule lives in the server's DTO lowering (`convert_assistant_text_blocks` / `convert_content` in `chat_completions/convert.rs`), the only place that knows the role; `vllm-chat` already has the text block it maps onto.

**Scope and intentional deviations from Python.** Python also accepts `input_text`, `output_text`, `input_image`, `thinking` and bare-string parts on chat completions, but only because its chat parser is shared with the Responses path (`MM_PARSER_MAP` in `vllm/renderers/chat_utils/chat_message.py`). A live probe of the OpenAI API (2026-11-03, one request per case) settles which are contract:

| Part on `/v1/chat/completions` | OpenAI | Python | Rust before | Rust after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `refusal` in an assistant message | 200 | text | 400 | text |
| `refusal` in a user message | 400 "Only assistant messages can have a 'refusal' content type." | text | 400 (serde) | 400 (OpenAI's message) |
| `input_text`, `output_text` (any role) | 400 "Invalid value" | text | 400 | 400 (unchanged) |
| `input_image` | 400 "Invalid value" | image | 400 | 400 (unchanged) |
| bare string in the parts list | 400 "expected an object" | text | 400 | 400 (unchanged) |

So only the assistant `refusal` part is implemented, and a `refusal` part outside assistant messages follows OpenAI rather than Python. Clients with Responses-shaped content can use the Rust `/v1/responses` route (vllm-project/vllm#63902), which accepts all of these. Python's Mistral `thinking` part (vllm-project/vllm#21333) is out of scope here.

**Harmony.** Python's Harmony path (gpt-oss) drops an assistant refusal part (`harmony_utils.py`, `TODO: Support refusal`); Rust's Harmony renderer keeps it as text like every other renderer.

**Known difference not changed here.** An assistant message with several text-like parts is joined with `"\n"` by Python and concatenated by Rust's HF renderer (`[text "Sorry.", refusal "I can't."]` renders `Sorry.\nI can't.` vs `Sorry.I can't.`). The same already holds for multiple text parts and is a separate fix.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR adds `refusal` content parts to the Rust frontend. Open PRs mentioning refusal parts target Python paths: Harmony (vllm-project/vllm#55479) and Responses input reconstruction (vllm-project/vllm#49130, vllm-project/vllm#48237). vllm-project/vllm#56648 also extends Rust chat content types but adds `image_embeds` in `vllm-chat`, not refusal parts.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this change; I reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][CI] Fix duplicate max_num_seqs in Llama Nemotron VL pooling test
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_llama_nemotron_vl.py::test_image_embeddings_without_chunked_prefill` fails on ROCm in both of its parametrisations:

```
TypeError: tests.conftest.VllmRunner() got multiple values for keyword argument 'max_num_seqs'
```

Seen in the `(MI355 DPX) Multimodal Models (Extended Pooling) Shard 1/2` step of [build 100175](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/100175/list?jid=01a1aa9f-d8ba-44ee-aa29-e22baeae7304&tab=output).

The test was added in 947bd30e0b (#65399). It passes `max_num_seqs=2` directly and also unpacks `**ROCM_ENGINE_KWARGS`. That constant is empty on CUDA, so the duplicate never shows up there, but on ROCm it carries `max_num_seqs`, and Python rejects the call while binding the arguments, before the model is loaded.

## Fix

I merge the two so the explicit value wins, which keeps `enable_prefix_caching=False` from the ROCm set and leaves CUDA unchanged. The test needs `max_num_seqs=2` rather than the ROCm value of 1, since both requests have to be resident at once for the encoder cache to come under pressure, which is what the test is checking.

## Validation

On MI355X, 2 passed in 52.08 s.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MiniMax-M3.1] Reserve MSA Q8KV4 prefill workspace
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #60791 item 7: reserve MSA Q8KV4 prefill split partials at model load so profiling counts them before KV cache sizing.

## Claims

- Share one reservation per `(device, topk_blocks, max_tokens, num_q_heads)` key per process, avoiding 60 layers × 8.6 GiB.
- Net -70 lines, mostly deleting the SM107 builder path and metadata plumbing.

## Validation

- B300: `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_msa_cutlass_sparse_decode.py` — **53 passed**; the 3 CUDA >=13.4-gated Q8KV4 prefill tests (shared workspace reservation, Triton agreement) **passed** with toolkit **13.4.1**.
- 4x B300 serving, MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, NVFP4 KV, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.92`: DEP4+EP startup on all ranks, KV cache **2,027,507 tokens**, `vllm bench serve` **100/100** requests; PP2 with `--max-num-batched-tokens 32768` progresses past MSA.
- Pre-commit passed.

## Details

vLLM memory profiling skips attention, so Q8KV4 prefill split partials allocated after KV-pool sizing cause startup OOM (60 layers × ~8.6 GiB if reserved per layer); see [#60791 item 7](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60791) for the full repro.

Reserving at attention-impl initialization includes the workspace in the profiling snapshot, with per-layer impls sharing one reservation through a process-local `WeakValueDictionary`; the old builder ran after KV sizing, so dropping its SM107 gate alone would not help.

- **Sleep/wake:** With cumem enabled, single-locality-domain GPUs offload/restore the runtime-pool workspace; on multi-domain Rubin, the pinned [MSA library](https://github.com/vllm-project/MSA) uses raw driver allocations that stay resident during sleep—pre-existing on main, unchanged here; follow-up belongs in MSA.
- **Scope:** NVFP4 prefill only; BF16-KV prefill still allocates per call (kernel follow-up); the PP2 FlashInfer MoE autotune startup failure remains separate and unresolved ([#60791](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60791)).
- **No duplicate:** [#60186](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60186) covers a different allocation site at KV init; no open PR covers #60791 item 7.

AI assistance (Kimi Code CLI) was used. The submitting human reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][DSA] Token-sharded sparse-MLA prefill under TP; remove indexer row sharding
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Shard DSA sparse-MLA prefill across TP ranks by token instead of by head ("ShardQ", Ulysses style) and remove the indexer TP row sharding from #54951, which it supersedes, including in GLM-5.3-Flash's k-pool indexer. Enabled by default for steps with >= 1024 tokens after the decodes (`sparse_mla_shard_q_min_tokens`), including mixed prefill + decode steps (whose decode tokens stay head-sharded); at 4K the gain is small and within end-to-end noise. Validated on GLM-5.3; GLM-5.3-Flash is covered by a forward-time microbenchmark and a greedy retrieval A/B.

## Claims

- GLM-5.3 (NVFP4, TP4, GB200, default FlashInfer sparse MLA backend) TTFT at concurrency 1: **1.24x at 32K, 1.29x at 64K, 1.40x at 128K** prompts.
- Per-step prefill forward is **1.11x-1.70x faster** than main, growing with context length (16K-token chunk at 128K context: 926 ms -> 544 ms), and **1.18x-1.25x faster than the removed row sharding** even with row sharding forced on. With default settings row sharding never engages: it needs >= 65536 prefill rows in one step, above the default `max_num_batched_tokens`.
- At 64K-token chunks, where main's row sharding engages by default, per-step forward is **1.14x-1.26x faster than row sharding** (B300; 64K chunk at 1M context: 11.17 s -> 9.83 s).
- GLM-5.3-Flash (k-pool indexer, now ShardQ-enabled): per-step forward at 64K-token chunks is **1.08x-1.13x faster than row sharding**, which this PR replaces there too.
- Mixed prefill + decode steps (one prefill chunk plus 32 decodes, GLM-5.3, B300): per-step forward is **1.16x-2.90x faster than main** on FlashInfer and **2.04x-2.97x** on FlashMLA sparse with `fp8_ds_mla`. Before mixed-step support, this PR was up to 2.4x slower than main's row sharding on such steps at a 64K budget.
- B300 serving A/B with the #54951 protocol (GLM-5.3 NVFP4, TP4, concurrency 1, 256 output tokens, four fresh-process pairs): server TTFT **1.19x at 8K, 1.29x at 32K, 1.46x at 128K, 1.99x at 512K and 2.62x at 1M** (162.5 s -> 62.0 s); 1K-4K prompts (below the threshold) unchanged; generated tokens identical to main in 132/132 matched retrieval probes.
- No accuracy change on gsm8k (5-shot and ~10K-token 45-shot prompts) or long-context passkey retrieval.

## Validation

The performance and accuracy numbers below were measured before the restructure from ZJY0516/vllm#24 (exchanges around the regular `forward_mqa`, indexer chunked over each rank's tokens) and with the earlier 8192-token default threshold; they have not been re-run on the current head.

All numbers: GLM-5.3 NVFP4, TP4 on one GB200 tray (4 GPUs).

**TTFT** (real weights, `vllm serve` defaults plus `--max-model-len 524288`; `vllm bench serve` random prompts, 1 output token, concurrency 1, 3-8 prompts per length after a warmup; both servers on the same node, one after the other):

| prompt | ShardQ off | ShardQ on | |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4K (below the threshold, ShardQ inactive) | 191 ms | 233 ms | run-to-run noise |
| 8K | 203 ms | 232 ms | within noise |
| 16K | 327 ms | 294 ms | 1.11x |
| 32K | 634 ms | 511 ms | 1.24x |
| 64K | 1228 ms | 950 ms | 1.29x |
| 128K | 2546 ms | 1819 ms | 1.40x |

`--max-model-len 524288` is needed because the 1M default needs 46.6 GiB of KV cache per GPU at TP4, independent of this PR.

**Accuracy** (real weights, same server settings, greedy):

| eval | ShardQ off | ShardQ on |
|---|---|---|
| gsm8k 5-shot, concurrency 128 (short prompts take dense MHA; ShardQ inactive) | 0.9196 | 0.9196 |
| gsm8k 45-shot (~10K-token prompts), concurrency 1, 200 samples: every prefill goes through ShardQ | 0.930 | 0.925 |
| passkey retrieval, 8K-128K prompts, 15 prompts | 15/15 | 14/15 |

The one passkey miss is a near tie on the first answer token (the off run picks the key with p = 0.64); the off run has a similar near-tie detour at 32K that still contains the key. Confident tokens have matching logprobs.

**Forward time** (dummy weights, prefix caching off) (`vllm bench forward`, median per step, CUDA-graph timed; `NK@MK c` = an N-token chunk whose prefix up to M tokens came from earlier chunks):

| step | main | main, row sharding forced (`indexer_tp_shard_min_rows=4096`) | this PR | vs main | vs row sharding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fresh prefill 4K | 142.0 ms | 143.0 ms | 127.7 ms | 1.11x | 1.12x |
| fresh prefill 8K | 278.5 ms | 277.1 ms | 233.9 ms | 1.19x | 1.18x |
| fresh prefill 16K | 550.1 ms | 539.5 ms | 444.3 ms | 1.24x | 1.21x |
| 16K @ 32K c | 612.6 ms | 574.3 ms | 460.9 ms | 1.33x | 1.25x |
| 16K @ 64K c | 701.8 ms | 602.8 ms | 483.1 ms | 1.45x | 1.25x |
| 16K @ 128K c | 926.3 ms | 676.3 ms | 544.4 ms | 1.70x | 1.24x |

This PR with `sparse_mla_shard_q=false` measures 141.9 / 278.4 / 546.6 / 608.7 / 697.7 / 922.6 ms, matching main: removing row sharding costs nothing at these shapes.

```bash
torchrun --nproc-per-node=4 -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench forward \
  --model nvidia/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 -tp 4 --max-model-len 131072 --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 \
  --kv-len-jitter 0 --case p4k=4096 --case p8k=8192 --case f16k=16384 \
  --case c32k=16384@32768c --case c64k=16384@65536c --case c128k=16384@131072c
# baseline arm: --attention-config.sparse_mla_shard_q false
# row sharding arm (on main): --attention-config.indexer_tp_shard_min_rows 4096
```

**Forward time at 64K-token chunks, where row sharding engages by default** (B300, `--max-num-batched-tokens 65536`, otherwise as above; median per step):

| step | main, row sharding (default) | main, row sharding off | this PR | vs row sharding | vs row sharding off |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fresh prefill 64K | 2237 ms | 2442 ms | 1769 ms | 1.26x | 1.38x |
| 64K @ 128K c | 2470 ms | 3144 ms | 1959 ms | 1.26x | 1.60x |
| 64K @ 256K c | 2958 ms | 4648 ms | 2388 ms | 1.24x | 1.95x |
| 64K @ 512K c | 4793 ms | 11542 ms | 4115 ms | 1.16x | 2.80x |
| 64K @ 1M c (1,000,000) | 11166 ms | not measured | 9834 ms | 1.14x | |

- **Row sharding is effective at this size:** 2.41x over no sharding at 512K, unlike at the 16K chunks above.
- **The margin narrows with context:** both methods split the indexer, whose cost grows with context. ShardQ also splits the sparse attention, whose per-token cost is fixed by the top-k.
- **Checks:**
  - This PR with `sparse_mla_shard_q=false` measures 2429 / 3135 / 4645 / 11463 ms on a different node, within 0.7% of main with row sharding off.
  - Sample spread is at most 0.7%.
  - A 16K @ 128K reference case in the same runs gives 920 ms for main and 534 ms for this PR, consistent with the table above.
- **Setup:**
  - One process per arm.
  - The KV cache is capped with `--kv-cache-memory-bytes 64424509440` so the 64K-token graph fits.
  - Both trees include the FlashInfer sparse MLA fix from #64122. Without it, main's 65,536-token steps silently skip the attention kernel (see "Batch budget" below).
- **Mixed prefill + decode steps:** ShardQ now also covers them (see "Where it applies" and the mixed-step table below).

```bash
torchrun --nproc-per-node=4 -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench forward \
  --model nvidia/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 -tp 4 --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-batched-tokens 65536 \
  --kv-cache-memory-bytes 64424509440 --kv-len-jitter 0 --iters 5 --samples 3 \
  --case f64k=65536 --case c128k=65536@131072c --case c256k=65536@262144c \
  --case c512k=65536@524288c --case c1m=65536@1000000c --case ref16k_128k=16384@131072c
# row sharding off (on main): --attention-config.indexer_tp_shard_min_rows 1000000000
```

## Details

**How it works.** Under TP every rank holds `H / tp` heads, so each rank runs the indexer over all prefill tokens, and the sparse attention kernel processes all tokens for its few heads. ShardQ instead gives each rank a slice of the step's tokens:

1. Tokens split zigzag: each request cuts into `2 * tp` chunks, and rank `r` owns chunks `r` and `2 * tp - 1 - r`, which balances the causal indexer cost.
2. The indexer scores only this rank's tokens and writes their top-k compactly, after the decode tokens' top-k, to the shared top-k buffer.
3. An all-to-all moves the MQA query from `[T, H / tp, D]` to `[T / tp, H, D]`; the sparse attention kernel attends all heads over the replicated KV cache.
4. A second all-to-all restores `[T, H / tp, 512]` for the `W_UV` projection.

The exchanges sit around the regular `forward_mqa` call, next to DCP's `query_gather` and combine; there is no ShardQ-specific attention entry point. They push tokens directly into peers' symmetric-memory buffers with one Triton kernel, falling back to NCCL `all_to_all_single` when the TP group has no symmetric memory. The fp8 query of the FlashInfer backend is exchanged as is.

**Where it applies.**
- Steps with at least `sparse_mla_shard_q_min_tokens` tokens after the decodes, one of whose requests is longer than the top-k; shorter prefills already take dense MHA.
- Mixed prefill + decode steps:
  - Only the tokens after the decodes are split. Decodes here are requests of at most `1 + num_speculative_tokens` tokens, and stay head-sharded.
  - The indexer scores every decode token in place, then this rank's tokens compactly after them, so tokens that the indexer treats as prefill but MLA treats as decode stay consistent.
  - The attention layer calls `forward_mqa` twice: once for the decode tokens with the step's metadata, once for this rank's tokens with ShardQ's narrowed metadata (`ShardQMetadata.attn_metadata`, which reads the top-k from `topk_start`). FlashMLA's token-sharded call uses its own lazily initialized scheduler metadata.
  - The decode output is written in place before the restored tokens rather than concatenated.
- The indexer metadata builder chunks only the decode tokens and this rank's tokens (`shardq_gather_indices`), each at its own position, so it makes fewer, fuller launches.
- TP > 1, no DCP/PCP/HiSparse, and no FULL CUDA graphs for mixed batches.
- Backends opt in with `SparseMLACommonImpl.supports_shardq`: FlashInfer sparse MLA and FlashMLA sparse (fp8 mixed-batch path).
- Models mark eligible layers with `MLAAttention(shardq_eligible=...)`: DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash (NVIDIA k-pool indexer) do. Other sparse MLA models keep the head-sharded path.
- The sparse MLA and indexer metadata builders both call `build_shardq_split` and, like every TP rank, derive the same split from the same batch.
- MTP layers are not eligible, including GLM-5.3-Flash's: draft steps reuse each token slot's top-k.

**Config.** New `AttentionConfig` fields `sparse_mla_shard_q` (default `True`) and `sparse_mla_shard_q_min_tokens` (default 1024). `indexer_tp_shard_min_rows` is deprecated, has no effect, and is removed in v0.34.0.

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**
- Memory: the exchange buffers (above) come out of the KV cache budget.
- GLM-5.3-Flash's k-pool indexer, which #54951 row-sharded, now follows the ShardQ split instead. Its MTP layers no longer shard the indexer.

**Not duplicating existing work.** No open PR implements token-sharded sparse-MLA prefill. #54394 and #56944 shard only the indexer rows (like the removed `PrefillRowShard`) and keep attention head-sharded.

commits.pr_title: [Core] Change default --block-size from 16 to 64
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Changes the default `--block-size` for `vllm serve` / `EngineArgs` from 16 to 64, via `CacheConfig.DEFAULT_BLOCK_SIZE`. Also teaches `RocmAttentionBackend` to prefer 16-token blocks for default-sized runs, keeping ROCm on its native paged-attention kernel.

## Claims

- `CacheConfig()` (and therefore `vllm serve` without `--block-size`) now resolves to `block_size=64`; an explicit `--block-size` still sets `user_specified_block_size=True` and takes precedence.
- Platforms/attention backends that declare a preferred or restricted block size continue to override the default exactly as before: `update_block_size_for_backend` only consults `DEFAULT_BLOCK_SIZE` when the user did not specify `--block-size`.
- ROCm runs without an explicit `--block-size` keep the native C++ paged-attention kernel (block sizes 16/32) instead of silently falling back to the slower Triton path that any other multiple of 16 routes to.

## Validation

- Full Buildkite CI build [#97300](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97300) passed (171 jobs), including the suites that caught regressions in the first run (#96922): H200/MI355 KV connector offload, MI250 PyTorch fullgraph cudagraph compatibility, and model executor.
- First CI run (#96922, default alone) failed exactly where 16-token assumptions were baked in: offloading-connector chunk sizes (48/16 vs the 64 GPU block), shared-storage connector hash-count expectations, an autotune cache-key test using 64 as a "non-default" control, and a 25-minute MI250 hang in RocmAttn with 64-token blocks (engine never returned from a step). All are fixed by this PR; the MI250 job went from timeout to passing in 8m51s, confirming the hang was block-size-related, not a flake.
- `tests/config/test_config_utils.py` (includes new `test_cache_config_default_block_size`): 28 passed.
- `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py`: 159 passed.
- `tests/kernels/attention/test_attention_selector.py`: 16 passed, 93 skipped.
- `tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py::test_autotune_cache_key_normalizes_kv_init_fields`: passed locally.
- `pre-commit run` on changed files: passed (ruff check/format, mypy, new-test CI-tethering check).
- Sanity check on CPU: `CacheConfig().block_size == 64`, `CacheConfig(block_size=16).user_specified_block_size is True`.

Still missing: a 16-vs-64 throughput/memory benchmark on a real serving workload. This change is motivated by per-block bookkeeping overhead; reviewers with GPU access should run `vllm bench serve` (or equivalent) on a representative model before merging if quantitative gains are required.

## Details

Motivation: a 64-token block reduces per-block bookkeeping overhead (block tables, allocator metadata, prefix-cache hash operations per token) and matches the granularity many attention backends already prefer. `user_specified_block_size` keeps explicit user settings authoritative, and the per-platform `get_preferred_block_size` / `get_supported_kernel_block_sizes` negotiation in `Platform.update_block_size_for_backend` is unchanged, so backends that cannot run with 64 still select a supported size automatically.

ROCm specifics: the native ROCm paged-attention C++ kernel only supports block sizes 16 and 32 (shared-memory/LDS constraints); every other multiple of 16 is routed to a Triton fallback (see `get_supported_kernel_block_sizes` in `vllm/v1/attention/backends/rocm_attn.py`). With the new default, `get_preferred_block_size(64)` returned 64 because 64 is nominally "supported", pushing every default-sized ROCm run onto that fallback — which is where build #96922's MI250 job hung. The new `RocmAttentionBackend.get_preferred_block_size` returns 16 unless the user passes an explicit `--block-size`, restoring pre-PR behavior on ROCm.

Tradeoffs:
- Prefix-cache hits land on 64-token boundaries instead of 16, so short shared prefixes (< 64 tokens) may no longer hit. Workloads with many short shared prefixes can pass `--block-size 16` to restore old behavior.
- Coarser blocks waste more KV memory per request on ragged tails (up to 63 tokens per request, vs 15).
- Third-party configs that hardcode chunk/block sizes as multiples of 16 (e.g. KV connector `kv_connector_extra_config["block_size"]`) now fail validation at startup against the 64-token default; the error message suggests the nearest valid value.
- This is a user-visible behavioral default change; docs use 16 only as an illustrative example and were not updated.

Not a duplicate: searched open PRs/issues (`block size default`, `block_size in:title`) — no open PR changes the global default. Related but distinct open PRs (e.g. #62265, #60880) fix backend-specific preferred-size selection, which this change composes with.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][MLA] Add opt-in FlyDSL FP8 prefill attention for AITER MLA
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Adds `ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8`, an opt-in MLA prefill backend that runs AITER's FlyDSL FP8 flash attention on dynamically per-tensor quantized Q/K/V, for Kimi-K3 on MI355X (gfx950). Port of the approach in [ROCm/ATOM#2191](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/pull/2191); supersedes #62447, which its author closed in favor of this PR.

## Claims

- New tokens, context chunks and context-free prefills all run FP8 FlyDSL attention. Selected with `--attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8"}'`; not auto-selected.
- Kimi-K3 TP8/DCP8 agentic replay (InferenceX agentx-mvp, c48): total throughput +4.5%, TTFT p90 -15.8%, ITL p90 -8.7%.
- 8K fresh prefill on current main and AITER v0.1.27, against the ASM FP8 prefill it replaces: TTFT mean -2.5%, p90 -9.1%.
- Accuracy unchanged. With DSpark MTP on current main: GPQA Diamond 91.4% in both arms, RULER NIAH 100% at 32K and 128K in both arms, DSpark acceptance length 3.819 vs 3.823, GSM8K 0.9651 vs 0.9591 (within one standard error of the difference). Earlier revision, without MTP: GSM8K 0.9621 in both arms; Kimi tool-call eval within run-to-run noise.
- No model or shape is hard-coded: availability and head dims come from AITER's `flydsl_flash_attn_fp8_supported`; inputs the kernel cannot take (empty, or at least 2^31 elements) fall back to the parent BF16 `ROCM_AITER_FA` path.

## Validation

Unit tests, MI355X, main @ `410ab341a8` + this PR:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py        # 935 passed, 349 skipped (GLM dims, TRTLLM-only params)
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_flydsl_fp8_prefill.py \
    tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_selector.py tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_registry.py   # 64 passed (kernel tests included)
```

`ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8` is in `PREFILL_BACKENDS_TO_TEST`, so `test_backend_correctness` and `test_chunked_context_backend_correctness` check it against SDPA; a `context_free_prefill` spec checks context-free batches against SDPA with this backend selected. That spec checks output only: it also passes with `_asm_fp8_prefill_superseded` forced to `False`, so it does not show which kernel ran; the e2e runs below confirm the backend from the server log.

CI coverage: only the MI355 `test_mla_backends.py` step runs with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, so it is the one CI job that exercises this backend. The FlyDSL kernel test and the head-dim selector test skip in CI (the `kernels/attention` step runs on MI300/gfx942, and the selector step does not enable AITER); I ran them on MI355X above.

End-to-end, 8x MI355X. Server (InferenceX `kimik3_fp4_mi355x` config; the arms differ only in `mla_prefill_backend`):

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_ASM_PADDING=asm vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 8 --dcp-comm-backend a2a \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8"}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --enable-prefix-caching --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 96 \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --language-model-only --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":224875000000,"lazy_offload":false}}'
# baseline: --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FA"}' (ASM FP8 prefill for context-free batches)
```

| Benchmark | Command | Baseline | FlyDSL FP8 |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| GSM8K 5-shot (strict / flexible) | `lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5` | 0.9621 / 0.9621 | 0.9621 / 0.9621 |
| Agentic replay, c48, 3600 s | `aiperf profile --scenario inferencex-agentx-mvp --concurrency 48 --benchmark-duration 3600 --public-dataset semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126` | 91,787 tok/s, TTFT p90 3690 ms | 95,931 tok/s, TTFT p90 3106 ms |
| 8K fresh prefill x128, c16, 2 runs | `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1 --ignore-eos --num-prompts 128 --max-concurrency 16` | TTFT mean 6414 ms, p90 7303 ms | TTFT mean 6255 ms, p90 6638 ms |

Accuracy with DSpark MTP, current main + this PR at `4d1ee17353` (code identical to `aea6855e4d`), AITER v0.1.27. Same server plus `--speculative-config '{"model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":4,"method":"dspark","attention_backend":"ROCM_AITER_MLA","kv_cache_dtype":"fp8","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block"}'`; one run per arm.

| Benchmark | Command | Baseline | FlyDSL FP8 |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| GPQA Diamond, 198 questions | `evalscope eval --eval-type openai_api --datasets gpqa_diamond --eval-batch-size 32 --generation-config '{"max_tokens": 100000, "temperature": 1.0, "top_p": 0.95}' --seed 42` | 91.4% | 91.4% |
| RULER NIAH, 8 `niah_*` tasks x 50 samples per length | `lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks niah_single_1,...,niah_multivalue --metadata '{"max_seq_lengths":[32768,131072]}'` | 100% / 100% (32K / 128K) | 100% / 100% (32K / 128K) |
| GSM8K 5-shot (strict / flexible) | as above | 0.9651 / 0.9651 | 0.9591 / 0.9591 |
| DSpark acceptance length / rate, over the GSM8K run | `vllm:spec_decode_*` counters | 3.819 / 0.705 (35,781 drafts) | 3.823 / 0.706 (35,608 drafts) |

The GSM8K gap is 8 of 1319 questions, 0.8 standard errors of the difference (per-arm stderr 0.51% / 0.55%), so it is within noise. NIAH uses lm-eval's RULER generator with 50 samples per task and length instead of 500, and both arms read the same generated samples.

<details><summary>Run details and more results</summary>

- The 8K row and the unit tests use current main with AITER v0.1.27. The GSM8K and agentic rows were measured on the first revision of this PR (same kernel calls behind an env flag, AITER 0.1.22 with the FlyDSL FP8 sources from AITER main); `cross_seqlen=True` since then is bit-identical.
- Full server command and environment:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_ASM_PADDING=asm SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4=1 AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1 AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 \
AITER_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM=1 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 \
VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_A2A=0 VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_Q_GATHER=0 VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_KV_GATHER=0 \
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --trust-remote-code --moe-backend auto --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --load-format fastsafetensors --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --language-model-only --max-num-seqs 96 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --enable-prefix-caching --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8"}' --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL","max_cudagraph_capture_size":96,"custom_ops":["+fused_rms_norm_gated"],"cudagraph_capture_sizes":[2,3,...,96]}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":224875000000,"lazy_offload":false}}' \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 8 --dcp-comm-backend a2a
```
- Agentic replay, full table:

| Metric | Baseline | FlyDSL FP8 |
|---|---:|---:|
| TTFT p50 / p90 / p99 (ms) | 1176 / 3690 / 22443 | 1119 / 3106 / 16155 |
| ITL p50 / p90 / p99 (ms) | 51.1 / 74.6 / 188.0 | 49.2 / 68.2 / 130.5 |
| Total / output tok/s | 91,787 / 609.2 | 95,931 / 638.5 |

- Kimi Vendor Verifier `kimi_tool_call_schema_full` (408 records), two runs per arm: baseline 0.9779 / 0.9877, FlyDSL 0.9755 / 0.9951.
- Prefill TTFT, first revision: 32K chunked -1.6%, 128K -7.3%, 64K with a 56K cached prefix -6.2%.
- Backend micro-benchmark (12 heads, qk 192 / v 128, FP8 time includes quantization), BF16 vs FlyDSL: 1x8192 causal 313 vs 229 us; q 1024 + context 64K 1278 vs 549 us; q 128 + context 64K 1251 vs 351 us.

</details>

## Details

- **Backend.** Subclasses `ROCM_AITER_FA`. Q is quantized once per forward and reused by every context chunk; each chunk quantizes only its own K/V. The LSE layout is unchanged, so `merge_attn_states` is reused.
- **Context-free prefills.** With this backend selected, `ROCM_AITER_MLA` no longer runs its ASM FP8 prefill (`mla_prefill_ps_asm_fwd`) or allocates its PS workspace; the gate is `_asm_fp8_prefill_superseded`, shared by the metadata builder and `forward_mha`.
- **Quantizer.** `triton_per_tensor_fp8_quant.py`, adapted from ATOM#2191's fused QKV quantizer (MIT), quantizes up to three strided tensors in two launches with no atomics and no recompiles across batch shapes. Existing ops do not fit: `ops.scaled_fp8_quant` matches numerically but takes the per-row path on strided V (65K tokens: 10.2 ms for Q/K/V vs 0.35 ms here), and `rocm_aiter_ops.per_tensor_quant` returns wrong results on strided V.
- **Docs.** `mla_prefill_backend`'s docstring, which renders the CLI reference, now lists the ROCm prefill backends.
- **AITER.** Needs `flydsl_flash_attn_fp8_supported` (ROCm/aiter#5718); main's pinned AITER v0.1.27 has it, along with `softmax_scale`, short-query split-K and the AOT `varlen_cross` kernels for `kimi_k3_tp8` (ROCm/aiter#5796, #5901). The new-token call uses `cross_seqlen=True` so it hits those AOT kernels; output is bit-identical to `cross_seqlen=False`.
- **Not a duplicate.** #62447 (same idea inside `ROCM_AITER_FA`) is closed in favor of this PR. #51551 is a gfx942 Gluon path with static per-head scales.

commits.pr_title: [HiSparse][Core] Move HiSparse hot-page stride alignment into its spec
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Remove the `isinstance(spec, HiSparseHotSpec)` special case from general KV cache planning. `_get_kv_cache_bytes_per_block` added the hot page size to the stride alignments by type check; `HiSparseHotSpec` now provides it through the existing `get_block_stride_alignment()` extension point. No behavior change.

**Why it's equivalent:** hot groups always carry per-layer names that share the spec, so the hot page size still enters the LCM. The override takes `lcm(page_size, super())`, and `super()` is 1 because hot specs don't set `block_stride_alignment`. On the layer-outermost path, `_get_layer_block_stride` rounds the hot page up to itself, which is a no-op.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py tests/v1/core/test_contiguous_kv_packing.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_config_builder.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -k "not test_num_hash_lookahead_tokens"
```

Existing planning and HiSparse layout tests cover the hot-group stride; no new test.

## Test Result

- **macOS (CPU), head fa71506595:** all pass. `test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_num_hash_lookahead_tokens[dspark]` (excluded above) fails identically on `main`.
- **GPU (4x B200, CUDA 13.0), earlier revision be49e2c334 vs `main` dc45a5f552:** that revision also carried scheduler and CoW changes that have since been dropped. The alignment change computes the same stride.
  - `pytest tests/v1/core/test_deferred_block_free.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k "hisparse or test_deferred_block_free"`: 88 passed. `pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py`: 5 passed.
  - `vllm serve GLM-5.3-NVFP4 -tp 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 --max-model-len 24576 --max-num-seqs 64 --num-gpu-blocks-override 12000 --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":64}}'` (`GPU + host KV cache size: 31,561 tokens`, forcing host offload). Greedy outputs match `main` up to `main`'s own run-to-run nondeterminism.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] Kimi-K3 prefill GEMMs on AITER tuned kernels
commits.pr_body:
Ready for review. No blocking issues. ## Overview Online FP8 prefill for Kimi-K3 on MI355X is slower than BF16 today. This PR quantizes `routed_expert_down_proj` online and builds AITER's tuned GEMMs at startup. ## Claims - `routed_expert_down_proj` follows the online quantization config. Its checkpoint weights are BF16, so the checkpoint config is still bypassed. - `kernel_config.enable_rocm_aiter_gemm_warmup` (off by default) runs one dummy forward per AITER GEMM M bucket during kernel warmup. - Kimi-K3 agentic PD benchmark, with in_proj padded to 128 on AITER v0.1.24.post1: +2.1% total tok/s/GPU and mean TTFT 5.35 s to 4.05 s over online FP8 prefill without this PR, +0.7% over BF16 prefill. ## Validation - New `test_rocm_aiter_gemm_warmup.py` covers bucket coverage and the opt-in. A new KDA online-loading test checks the alignment padding: loading completes after six shards and the padding stays zero. pre-commit clean; GPU reload tests in `test_reload.py` not run. - End to end: one run per configuration, below. No accuracy evaluation. Variance not measured; the closest pair, BF16 with and without warmup, differs by 0.4% in throughput and 0.01 s / 1.2 s in mean / p90 TTFT. - KDA in_proj keeps main's 16-row alignment: AITER v0.1.27, main's pin, tunes 6288x7168 at the latency of 6400x7168. Not re-run end to end on v0.1.27.
End-to-end benchmark Kimi-K3, agentic multi-turn trace at concurrency 48, 1 prefill + 1 decode instance on 2 nodes of 8x MI355X, TP8 + DCP8, FP8 KV cache, MoRIIO. vLLM ROCm nightly `81198e97` with these changes mounted as file overlays. Online FP8 prefill means `--quantization-config` with `fp8_per_channel` targets on the attention projections, shared experts and dense MLPs, plus `re:.*\.routed_expert_down_proj$: mxfp4` and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM=1` from the down_proj step on. | Prefill | Run | Total tok/s/GPU | TTFT mean / p90 | |---|---|---|---| | BF16 GEMMs | [run](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/39140308384) | 10775 | 4.50 s / 9.22 s | | Online FP8 | [run](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/39226586488) | 10626 | 5.35 s / 13.31 s | | + down_proj MXFP4 | [run](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/39253422535) | 10663 | 5.14 s / 12.73 s | | + in_proj pad 128 | [run](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/39260261980) | 10552 | 5.78 s / 14.18 s | | + GEMM warmup (this PR) | [run](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/39352208397) | 10851 | 4.05 s / 8.50 s | | BF16 GEMMs + warmup only | [run](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/39487012805) | 10729 | 4.51 s / 10.45 s | The `+ in_proj pad 128` step was needed on that nightly's AITER v0.1.24.post1, whose table tunes 6400x7168 but not 6288x7168; this PR no longer pads. In v0.1.27's `a8w8_bpreshuffle_tuned_gemm_kimik3.csv` (gfx950, 256 CUs) the 6288/6400 latency ratio has median 1.00 and range 0.92 to 1.09 over the 52 M values from 256 to 8192, and both shapes use the same FlyDSL kernel at M=8192. Padding alone is slower because the newly tuned kernels are built on first use while serving; the warmup moves that to startup. Warmup without online quantization gives no gain. Load-time checks: 92 `routed_expert_down_proj` on `Mxfp4OnlineLinearMethod`, 69 `in_proj_qkvgfab` on `AiterPreshuffledPerTokenFp8ScaledMMLinearKernel`.
## Details - Warmup sizes: AITER buckets up to `max_num_batched_tokens`, multiples of 8 up to 512, and `max_num_batched_tokens - 1` for Triton's divisibility specialization; 164 forwards at 8192 tokens, 541 to 585 s on the Kimi-K3 prefill instance (104 s without online quantization). The measured runs added a second timing sweep, dropped here. - An online config whose `linear` default does not ignore `routed_expert_down_proj` now quantizes it; add it to `ignore` to keep BF16. ---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Use the default template of multi-template processors
commits.pr_body:
## Overview Processors that ship several chat templates (e.g. `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-Reranker-2B`, `ModernVBERT/colmodernvbert-merged`) expose `chat_template` as a `{name: template}` dict. `_try_get_processor_chat_template` returned it as is, so chat rendering fails with `TypeError: unhashable type: 'dict'`. This PR uses the `"default"` entry and carries forward #46801 (@shun-cohere). ## Claims - Chat-style requests to these models return 200 instead of 400 `unhashable type: 'dict'`. They use the `"default"` template, as `ProcessorMixin.apply_chat_template` does (content format `openai`, not `string`). - Other processors are unchanged. A dict without `"default"` raises a `TypeError` in the existing `try` (logged at debug level), so resolution falls through to the tokenizer template. ## Validation Main 9a56d4fec, CPU-only Linux VM, transformers 5.20.2. The main column uses main's `vllm/renderers/hf.py`. | Command | main | this PR | | --- | --- | --- | | `pytest tests/renderers/test_hf.py::test_processor_multiple_chat_templates_uses_default` | failed | passed | | `pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_launch_render.py` | new test: `assert 400 == 200` | 9 passed | | `cd tests && pytest -v -s renderers` | 4 failed, 689 passed | 3 failed, 690 passed | | `vllm launch render Qwen/Qwen3-VL-Reranker-2B`, `POST /v1/chat/completions/render` | 400 | 200, expected `token_ids` | | `vllm serve ModernVBERT/colmodernvbert-merged`, `POST /pooling` with `messages` | 400 | 200 | The 3 shared failures are gated repos (no HF token); main's extra one is the new unit test. pre-commit passes. CI runs the tests in `entrypoints-integration-api-server` and `cpu-reasoning-renderers`. ## Details - Root cause: transformers keeps `processor.chat_template` as a dict when a repo has `additional_chat_templates/*.jinja`. Without tools, `resolve_chat_template` returns it, and the `lru_cache` of `_cached_resolve_chat_template_kwargs` raises. - On main the servers still start (the warmup only logs the `TypeError`; since #64020 the Anthropic inline-system probe no longer aborts on the dict), but chat-style requests fail. commits.pr_title: [CI] Pass --models=llama3.2 so Rust Frontend Tool Use gets a shard plan
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Rust Frontend Tool Use and its AMD mirror are enrolled in `automatic_shard`, but the planner never plans them: their command passes `--models llama3.2` as two words. `--models` is a conftest option (`tests/tool_use/conftest.py`), not a pytest one, so the planner reads `llama3.2` as a test path, can't find it, and falls back to one job. Writing `--models=llama3.2` lets it plan.

## Claims

- The planner plans both jobs instead of reporting "no plan (`llama3.2` ... is not in the checkout)".
- The tests that run are unchanged: pytest reads `--models=llama3.2` the same as `--models llama3.2`.
- Both jobs plan one shard today; they shard once their tests grow past the 20-minute target.

## Validation

- Planner on main: `no plan (llama3.2 of pytest -v -s tool_use --ignore=tool_use/mistral --models llama3.2 is not in the checkout)`. On this branch: 1 shard for the NVIDIA job and 1 for the AMD mirror.
- pytest with a conftest declaring `--models` as `nargs="+"`: `--models=llama3.2` and `--models llama3.2` both give `['llama3.2']`.
- No step's jobs each run the whole suite (the enrollment split check).
- `/ci run` build 100042 on this head, against main build 100025 (no test change between them): both jobs ran the same 630 node IDs as main with the same outcomes (515 passed, 115 skipped), none missing, added or duplicated; each job ran once, 11.8 and 9.7 min including setup.

## Details

- **YAML, not the planner.** The planner knows only pytest's own value-taking options; teaching it vLLM's conftest options would couple ci-infra to vLLM's tests. Every other conftest option in CI YAML already uses the `=` form.
- **Limit:** the `=` form passes one model. A command needing several would need the conftest option changed from `nargs="+"` to `action="append"` (`--models=a --models=b`); no CI command does that today.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Shard Spec Decode AL MTP automatically and split its Gemma4 test by dataset
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Enrolls the nightly Spec Decode AL MTP + Other Acceptance step and its AMD mirror in automatic sharding, and splits the Gemma4 MTP acceptance test so that no shard needs more than 20 minutes.

- The hand split (three parallel jobs, each running a different `pytest` command through `$BUILDKITE_PARALLEL_JOB` guards) becomes one plain `pytest` command, which the pipeline generator shards from recorded per-file timings.
- `test_gemma4_mtp_acceptance_lengths` ran all three datasets (MT-Bench, HumanEval, GSM8K) in one test, over 20 minutes per case on its own, so no shard count could bring its shard under the target. It is now parametrized by dataset: 6 cases of about 8 to 10 minutes instead of 2 of over 20.

## Claims

| Job | Main | Plan |
|---|---|---|
| `spec-decode-mtp-other-acceptance-nightly` | 3 fixed jobs | 4 shards |
| its AMD mirror | 3 fixed jobs | 2 shards |

- Same coverage: the same prompts, model config and thresholds per dataset, for both `use_mrv2` values. Each dataset now starts its own engine.
- Every shard stays under the 20-minute target, setup included.
- New tests in the folder are planned automatically instead of landing in shard 0.

## Validation

`/ci run` build 100083 (NVIDIA) and scoped build 100090 (AMD mirror) on head c4fa77fda5, against main nightly 100007.

| | Shards, wall time incl. setup | Main's slowest job | Machine time vs main |
|---|---|---|---|
| the step | 17.7 / 18.0 / 19.4 / 2.1 min | 28.4 min | -1% |
| its AMD mirror | 14.1 / 16.7 min | 17.6 min | -11% |

- All 7 tests pass on both: the 6 Gemma4 cases and the synthetic test. Main's 2 Gemma4 node IDs became 6 by design; nothing else changed.
- Every dataset reaches the same acceptance length as on main, for both `use_mrv2` values: MT-Bench 2.28, HumanEval 2.69, GSM8K 2.67; synthetic 1.876.
- Wall time is each job's start to finish: it excludes queue time and includes checkout, image pull and setup. No automatic retries.
- `split_check.py`: no step runs the whole suite in each of its parallel jobs.

## Details

- **Timings before merge.** Main has no timings for the new command or the new test IDs, so build 100069 of this PR's commit on the OTel treatment branch recorded them (that build ran the step as one job, with the timeout raised in that commit only; the next commit restores it). The command drops its trailing slash so that its timings come only from that build, not from an earlier bootstrap build of the two long cases. Main's own runs replace them after merge.
- **Margin.** The slowest shard has about half a minute to spare; main's nightlies have run these tests somewhat slower than PR builds, and the planner re-plans from main's timings once they exist.
- **Timeouts unchanged.**

commits.pr_title: [CI] Run Distributed Features examples once and shard its pytest commands
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Splits Distributed Features into two steps and shards the pytest one automatically:

- **Distributed Features Examples** (new, NVIDIA step and AMD mirror) runs the example scripts once, as one job. It isn't enrolled: the planner shards only pytest commands.
- **Distributed Features** keeps its pytest commands, in main's order, and the step and its AMD mirror are enrolled in `automatic_shard`.

With the examples left in the sharded step, the planner treats them as setup and every shard repeats them (about 5 minutes per shard).

## Claims

| Job | Main | Plan |
|---|---|---|
| `distributed-tests-2xh100-2xmi300` | 1 job | 2 shards |
| its AMD mirror | 1 job | 2 shards |
| `distributed-examples-2xh100` (new) | in the step above | 1 job |
| its AMD mirror (new) | in the step above | 1 job |

- Every pytest node ID runs exactly once, with the same outcome as on main; every example command runs once.
- Every job stays under the 20-minute target, setup included.
- Machine time is lower than main's on both platforms, the extra examples job included.

## Validation

`/ci run` build 100068 (NVIDIA) and scoped build 100074 (both AMD mirrors) on head 3729373c87, against main build 100007, the newest main build where both jobs passed.

| | Pytest node IDs (passed / skipped) | Missing / added / outcome changed | Slowest job, setup included | Machine time vs main |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| the step | 271 (241 / 30), same as main | 0 / 0 / 0 | 10.6 min (examples job 4.7) | -9% |
| its AMD mirror | 302 (261 / 41), same as main | 0 / 0 / 0 | 14.7 min (examples job 5.3) | -6% |

- Per command, every pytest command's passed and skipped counts match main's, and every example script exits 0.
- Wall time is each job's start to finish: it excludes queue time and includes checkout, image pull and setup. Machine time sums every job of both steps. No automatic retries.
- `split_check.py` finds no step whose jobs each run the whole suite; the sharding harness (each shard's commands against a mock test tree, as a PR build and as main with the OTel wrapper) shows every test runs once, for the step and its mirror.

## Details

- **Mirror dependencies.** The new examples mirror keeps the old mirror's `source_file_dependencies` minus its test files; the pytest mirror drops the two example scripts.
- **Timeouts.** The pytest step keeps its timeouts; the examples step uses 30 minutes on both platforms.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Shard Quantization Kernels automatically instead of by hand
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Replaces the fixed 6-way split of Quantization Kernels (`parallelism: 6` with `--shard-id`/`--num-shards`) with `automatic_shard`, for the step and its AMD mirror. The planner then sizes the step from main's per-file timings on every build, so it no longer needs a hand-tuned shard count as its tests change.

## Claims

| Job | Before | Plan |
|---|---|---|
| `kernels-quantization-test` | 6 fixed shards | 3 shards |
| its AMD mirror | 6 fixed shards | 3 shards |

- Every test runs exactly once, with the same outcome as on main.
- Every shard stays under the 20-minute target, setup included.
- `test_cutlass_scaled_mm.py` and `test_fp8_quant.py` each run in their own pytest command. In one shared process, `test_fp8_quant.py` ran 2.4 times slower after `test_cutlass_scaled_mm.py`, which pushed one shard past 28 minutes.
- Half the jobs and less machine time.

## Validation

`/ci run` build 100067 on this head (rebased onto 46f36fa294, after #65542's Marlin change), against main build 100030, the newest main build that ran both jobs. No quantization test changed between the two revisions.

| | Node IDs (passed / skipped) | Missing / added / outcome changed | Slowest shard, setup included | Machine time vs main |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| the step | 6,761 (3,317 / 3,444), same as main | 0 / 0 / 0 | 19.1 min | -22% |
| its AMD mirror | 6,501 (2,909 / 3,592), same as main | 0 / 0 / 0 | 14.8 min | -27% |

- Per command, the step's three commands pass 2,432 + 638 + 247 = 3,317 tests, main's one command 3,317. The pytest summary's skipped count is 90 lower (70 on the mirror) only because a file that skips at module level is counted once per pytest process, and main runs six processes. The per-node-ID skip lists are identical.
- Wall time is each job's start to finish, so it excludes queue time and includes checkout, image pull and setup. No automatic retries.
- The sharding harness (each shard's commands run against a mock test tree, as a PR build and as main with the OTel wrapper) shows every test runs exactly once, for both the step and its mirror. `split_check.py` finds no step whose jobs each run the whole suite.

## Details

- **Timings until merge.** Main has these files under the old `--shard-id` command only, so the new commands borrow those timings and the plan stays conservative until main records the new labels.
- **Labels** drop the `Shard %N` suffix; the generator adds `shard N/M` to sharded jobs.

commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Enable existing native 8/16/32-head kernels in SM90 BF16 sparse FlashMLA for sufficiently large query batches, avoiding unnecessary computation from padding heads to 64.

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61615

## Claims

- Reduce head-padding overhead in the BF16 sparse attention path.
- Preserve the padded path for small query batches, where native small-head kernels can be slower.
- Improve output throughput by 10.0% in the recorded GLM-5.3-Flash serving benchmark.

## Validation

Serving benchmark: GLM-5.3-Flash, TP4 with EP, BF16 KV cache, 16,384 input tokens, 512 output tokens, 128 requests, concurrency 32.
