commits.pr_title: [Online quantization] Support activation quant key override for online MXFP4 linear/MOE quant methods
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Support activation quant key override in online MXFP4 quantization as e.g.:

```bash
--quantization online --quantization-config.targets '{"*experts*":{"weight":"mxfp4","activation":null}}'
# dispatching to AITER_MXFP4_BF16 on ROCm.

--quantization online --quantization-config.targets '{"*experts*":{"weight":"mxfp4","activation":"mxfp8"}}'
# (unsupported on ROCm atm, see below)
```

An activation override that the selected MXFP4 backend cannot compute raises instead of silently running another activation format. For example, `"activation":"mxfp8"` on ROCm (MI350X, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`) raises:

```text
NotImplementedError: online MXFP4 MoE backend 'Mxfp4MoeBackend.EMULATION' cannot honour activation=QuantKey(f8e4m3fn,scale(u8,dynamic,GroupShape(row=1, col=32)),symmetric); it computes activation=QuantKey(u8,scale(u8,dynamic,GroupShape(row=1, col=32)),symmetric).
```

Similarly, e.g. `"fp8_per_tensor_static"` is rejected for online quantization, which has no calibrated activation scales.

**Other online quantization weight keys than MXFP4 still raise `NotImplementedError` in case activation key is overriden. This will be updated once all oracles share the same logic for activation quant key override.**

Currently, activation override for online quantization raises a `NotImplementedError`, but overriding the activation quant key is truly needed to dispatch on preferred MOE backends (e.g. `AITER_MXFP4_BF16`, `AITER_MXFP4_MXFP4`) that can not be selected in any other way.

More context at https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52167

## Claims

Only the MXFP4 online methods (`Mxfp4OnlineLinearMethod`, `Mxfp4OnlineMoEMethod`) accept an activation override, which is what the MXFP4 backend dispatch needs. Any other online method raises `NotImplementedError: activation override is not supported for online <method class>` at config-resolution time (`OnlineRequantizationMixin.resolve_activation_quant_key` raises unless the method class sets `accepts_activation_override = True`). Only the MXFP4 online methods take an `activation_quant_key` constructor argument (defaulting to `kMxfp4Dynamic`); other online methods keep their class-level `activation_quant_key`, unchanged from `main`.

An online MXFP4 MoE override that the selected backend does not compute raises `NotImplementedError`, and static activation keys are rejected for every online method.

An explicitly configured `activation: null` requests unquantized (BF16) activations, for `linear` and `moe` alike, on online targets and on pre-quantized checkpoints. On a pre-quantized MXFP4 MoE checkpoint that declares its own activation, an explicit `moe.activation` (`null` included) now overrides the checkpoint's activation with a warning, like linear layers already do, instead of raising.

For the `mxfp4` / `mxfp8` shorthands, which may name either an online scheme or the checkpoint format, the shorthand defaults are merged with `--quantization-config` only once the model is known to be unquantized (`merge_quantization_config` in `get_quant_config`). On a pre-quantized checkpoint, e.g. `--quantization mxfp4 --quantization-config.moe.activation mxfp8` on gpt-oss, an activation override alone therefore no longer online-quantizes the layers the checkpoint leaves unquantized (on `main`, it did so for linear layers).

On a pre-quantized checkpoint, a `targets` spec without a `weight` (e.g. `{"targets": {"*experts*": {"activation": null}}}`) overrides the activation of the matching layers' checkpoint quant method only: `resolve_quant_method` applies it while that method is built, and `user_activation_override` reads it before the global `linear` / `moe` override.

`--moe-backend aiter_mxfp4_fp8` with online MXFP4 MoE is not rejected up front, but it already fails at weight processing, as online quantization has no static activation scales (unchanged from `main`):

```
ValueError: W4A8 (AITER_MXFP4_FP8) requires static input scales, but found w13_input_scale or w2_input_scale is None.
```

Left to other PRs:

- [ ] Add `__str__` method to QuantKey directly.
- [ ] Per-layer `targets` activation overrides on pre-quantized checkpoints only reach the quant methods that select their kernel / backend when they are built. Quark MXFP4 linear (`QuarkOCP_MX`) selects its kernel in `create_weights`, and the Humming MoE input schema is built at weight processing, so both only see the global `linear` / `moe` override. This should be handled in the oracles, independently of the quant methods, rather than per quant method.
- [ ] Let the OCP MX emulation MoE backend compute the requested activation format for online MXFP4. Today, EMULATION only computes MXFP4 activations, so for online MXFP4 MoE any other requested activation key (`null`/BF16, MXFP6, FP8, and `mxfp8` on ROCm) raises `NotImplementedError` ("online MXFP4 MoE backend ... cannot honour activation=...") instead of silently running MXFP4 activations, as before this PR. The oracle hard-codes MXFP4 activations for EMULATION here: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/790be385c8a69f45ec9a7a85ef00836d1684060f/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/mxfp4.py#L2240-L2250
- [ ] Make the activation override independent of the oracle: today only `Mxfp4OnlineLinearMethod` and `Mxfp4OnlineMoEMethod` support it with this PR. Generalize it so any oracle can accept an activation override, and move some of the logic to oracles rather than online quantization.

## Validation

Tests new or modified in this PR, on MI350X:

```bash
pytest -q \
    tests/quantization/test_quantization_config_args.py \
    tests/quantization/test_online.py \
    tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_shared_expert.py \
    tests/quantization/test_config_utils.py \
    tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp4_w4a8_rdna3.py \
    tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py \
    -k "test_quantization_config_args or test_activation_only_override_applies_to_checkpoint_method or test_resolve_colliding_shorthand_is_deferred or test_moe_activation_override_wins_over_checkpoint or test_args_resolve_ambiguous_strings_by_field or test_quant_spec_equality_ignores_explicit_field_metadata or test_online_shorthands_do_not_set_activation_defaults or test_resolve_preserves_explicit_null_activation or test_hadamard_size_composes_with_quantization_config or resolve_activation_quant_key or activation_override or honoured_or_rejected or hadamard_target_wraps_resolved_method or activation_only_spec_raises or test_log_online_quantization or fse_compares_resolved_keys or fused_shard_targets_compare_resolved_specs or resolve_linear_activation_key or selects_w4a8"
```

On 3ae6779169, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=0`:

```
127 passed, 4 skipped, 589 deselected, 14 warnings in 61.06s (0:01:01)
```

On 3ae6779169, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`:

```
127 passed, 4 skipped, 589 deselected, 14 warnings in 61.47s (0:01:01)
```

Potentially impacted tests: the full suites of the files this PR touches, plus the suites exercising the online MXFP4 methods, the MXFP4 MoE oracle and the fused shared-expert / requantization paths:

```bash
pytest -q \
    tests/quantization/test_online.py \
    tests/quantization/test_quantization_config_args.py \
    tests/quantization/test_config_utils.py \
    tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_shared_expert.py \
    tests/quantization/test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py \
    tests/quantization/test_online_mxfp4.py \
    tests/quantization/test_keep_param_objects.py \
    tests/quantization/test_input_hadamard.py \
    tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp4_w4a8_rdna3.py \
    tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py \
    tests/quantization/test_gfx950_moe.py \
    tests/quantization/test_humming_mxfp4_block_fp8.py \
    tests/kernels/moe/test_b12x.py \
    tests/kernels/moe/test_cutlass_moe.py
```

On 3ae6779169, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER` unset:

```
1 failed, 653 passed, 676 skipped, 14 warnings in 746.75s (0:12:26)
```

The failure, `tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py::test_rocm_mxfp4_moe_oracle[16-256-256-8-4-AITER_MXFP4_BF16]` (`Mismatch percentage is 0.3704 for rtol 0.1 (threshold: 0.3000)`), only happens within this full run: the test passes in isolation, on both this branch and `main`.

Example usage on MI350:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B \
    --quantization online \
    --quantization-config.targets '{"*experts*":{"weight":"mxfp4","activation":null}}' \
    --tensor-parallel-size 1
```

showing:

```
[mxfp4.py:749] Using 'AITER_MXFP4_BF16' Mxfp4 MoE backend.
[base_loader.py:164] Quantizing 40 layers of types: mlp.experts: 40 (from targets: *experts*, {"weight":"mxfp4","activation":null})
```

The server then served the model (`Application startup complete`, `/v1/chat/completions` returns tokens) on a single MI350X GPU.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Honor checkpoint FP8 KV scales in Qwen4Exp QSA
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Load checkpoint K/V scales into the host floats used by Qwen4Exp QSA with an FP8 KV cache. This splits the fix out of #59209. The CUDA reproducer runs with HiSparse disabled. [Original review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59209#discussion_r4471891384)

## Claims

- On CUDA, the fused cache writer and sparse attention reader use the checkpoint scales.
- On ROCm, the sparse attention reader requires both scales to be `1.0`. Its existing check now sees the loaded values and rejects a non-unit K or V scale.

## Validation

Both checks used safetensors with `k_proj.output_scale=0.5` and `v_proj.output_scale=2.0`.

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| CUDA engine startup (SM100, `fp8_e4m3`) | Device K/V = 0.5/2.0, host K/V = 1.0/1.0. Scale assertion failed. | Device and host K/V = 0.5/2.0. Scale assertion passed. |
| ROCm QSA implementation exercised on CPU (PyTorch 2.13.0) | Host K/V = 1.0/1.0. The reader passed the unit-scale check. | Host K/V = 0.5/2.0. The reader raised its existing `NotImplementedError` before GPU dispatch. |

The CPU probe used the AMD QSA layer, the vLLM safetensors loader and the standard post-load pass. It also checked that `fp8` with K/V = 1.0/2.0 is rejected, and that unit-scale FP8 and BF16 reach the GPU dispatch boundary. I haven't run the ROCm backend on AMD hardware. Repository pre-commit checks passed.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the CUDA result or check on ROCm hardware</summary>

The original CUDA run used upstream `fd75a7a920`, an SM100 GPU, PyTorch `2.14.0+cu130`, and native extensions from the `0cb25c3574` wheel for both runs. Both generated identical checkpoint weights. To repeat the check in a disposable checkout with the PR commits available, restore the original test and run it:

```bash
git diff 58bfefd8^ 58bfefd8 -- tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py | git apply
pytest -q tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py::test_qsa_fp8_uses_checkpoint_kv_scales
```

For ROCm, save the [same one-layer checkpoint](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/58bfefd8a077d223f555878a763285e58ab11409/tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py#L253-L281) and run one request with the code below. With K/V = 0.5/2.0 the expected error includes `requires unit scales on the AMD path`. With K/V = 1.0/1.0 the request should produce one token.

```python
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

if __name__ == "__main__":
    llm = LLM(
        model="./checkpoint", dtype="bfloat16", kv_cache_dtype="fp8_e4m3",
        skip_tokenizer_init=True, enable_prefix_caching=False, enforce_eager=True,
        max_model_len=128, max_num_seqs=2,
    )
    result = llm.generate(
        {"prompt_token_ids": [1, 2]},
        SamplingParams(max_tokens=1, temperature=0, detokenize=False),
    )
    assert len(result[0].outputs[0].token_ids) == 1
```

</details>

## Details

The loader populates `_k_scale` and `_v_scale`, which the unfused writer reads directly. Both platform implementations also keep Python floats initialized to `1.0`. The post-load hook copies the tensor values into those floats once per FP8 layer.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Apply DeepSeek-V4 compressor and wo_a adapters
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Since #53361 ("Support LoRA for DeepSeek V4") and #55897, DeepSeek-V4 has declared `SupportsLoRA`. On the CUDA path, though, adapters on the compressor's `wkv`/`wgate` and on `wo_a` are silently dropped. Both projections run their GEMM directly on the base weight, which bypasses the LoRA wrapper.

#57245 already fixed this for DeepSeek-V4.1. It added LoRA wrappers plus V4.1-local copies of the two layers those wrappers match. This PR builds V4's projections as the same layers and moves the layers from V4.1 into V4, so the two models share one copy.

## Claims

- Adapters on `compressor.wkv`/`wgate`, `indexer.compressor.wkv`/`wgate` and `wo_a` now apply on all three V4 CUDA attention backends (FlashMLA, FlashInfer SM100, FlashInfer SM120).
- Without LoRA, every changed V4 projection runs the same kernels on the same inputs as before, so outputs are bit-identical (the tests assert this).
- FlashInfer RopeQuant (SM100) is turned off when LoRA is enabled. It writes only FP8 attention output, and the `wo_a` adapter needs the BF16 input.
- DeepSeek-V4.1 behavior is unchanged. It now imports the two layers from V4 instead of keeping copies that matched V4's apart from import paths.

## Validation

Run on an H20 (SM90) with:

```bash
pytest -v tests/lora/test_layers.py -k "dsv4 or grouped_o_projection or compressor_projection"
pytest -v tests/v1/attention/test_deepseek_v4_swa_visible.py tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py
```

| Test | With this PR | Fix reverted (`attention.py`, `nvidia/flashmla.py`, `nvidia/flashinfer_sparse.py` from `main`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test_dsv4_compressor_projections_apply_lora_with_fp32_output` (main and indexer compressor) | passed | failed: adapter check, `Mismatched elements: 3049 / 8704` |
| `test_dsv4_grouped_o_projection_applies_each_tokens_adapter` (all three backends) | passed | failed: adapter check, ~35% of elements mismatched |
| `test_dsv4_rope_quant_is_off_with_lora` | passed | n/a |
| Existing V4.1 tests, now built from the shared V4 layers: `test_grouped_o_projection_*` (3 BF16 + 2 fully sharded), `test_compressor_projection_applies_lora_with_fp32_output` (4), `test_dsv41_gemm_rs_is_not_set_up_with_lora` | 10 passed | 10 passed |
| `test_grouped_o_projection_applies_each_tokens_adapter`, FP8 `wo_a` (3) | not runnable here* | not runnable here* |
| `test_deepseek_v4_swa_visible.py` (stubs V4.1's `wo_a`) | 35 passed | n/a |
| `test_compressor_kv_cache.py` (V4.1 compressor) | 149 passed, 26 failed | n/a |

\* That H20 has no DeepGEMM `fp8_einsum` ("DeepGEMM backend is unavailable"). The error comes from the baseline call, before any LoRA code runs. CI's H200 `LoRA` step has DeepGEMM and runs these cases.

The 26 `test_compressor_kv_cache.py` failures are the NVFP4 cases (`cvt with .e2m1x2` is not supported on `sm_90a`). Unmodified `main` gives the same 149 passed and the same 26 failures on that GPU.

With the fix reverted, the bit-exact checks without LoRA still pass. Only the adapter checks fail, on the ~35% of tokens mapped to an adapter, which shows the adapters were being dropped.

`pre-commit` passes on the changed files (ruff, mypy, typos, test tethering).

I did not do an end-to-end serving run with a V4 checkpoint and an adapter on these modules. Without LoRA, every changed V4 projection is bit-identical to `main` (asserted above), and RopeQuant only turns off when `--enable-lora` is set, so serving without LoRA is unchanged.

## Details

**Root cause.**
- The compressor kv_score closures in `DeepseekV4Attention._run_parallel_input_projections` call `torch.mm(hidden_states, fused_wkv_wgate.weight.T, out_dtype=torch.float32)`.
- Every CUDA `_o_proj` passes `self.wo_a` to `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj`, which runs `fp8_einsum`/`torch.bmm` on `wo_a.weight`.
- Under LoRA, both modules are LoRA wrappers whose `weight` (and `weight_scale`) resolve to the base layer, so these GEMMs never see the adapter. Nothing raises an error.

**Compressor.**
- `DeepseekV4CompressorKVScoreLinear` is a `MergedColumnParallelLinear` whose forward is that FP32 GEMM. It moved unchanged from `deepseek_v41/compressor.py` to `deepseek_v4/compressor.py`. V4's closures now call the layer.
- `DeepseekV4CompressorKVScoreWithLoRA`, added in #57245, matches the layer by class name and adds the adapter delta.
- CPU keeps the plain layer:
  - Its packed GEMM frees the raw weight (`dispatch_cpu_unquantized_gemm(remove_weight=True)`).
  - CPU attention calls the layer and upcasts the result itself.
  - The CPU V4 model does not declare `SupportsLoRA`.

**`wo_a`.**
- `DeepseekV4GroupedWoA` is the `ColumnParallelLinear` `wo_a`, plus two methods:
  - `grouped_forward`, which wraps the unchanged `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj`.
  - `grouped_input`, which returns the BF16 inverse-rotated groups.
- The class moved from `deepseek_v41/common/grouped_wo_a.py` to `deepseek_v4/common/grouped_wo_a.py`. Only the docstring and one import path differ, and V4.1's `fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant` already re-exports V4's.
- The three V4 CUDA `_o_proj`s call `wo_a.grouped_forward(...)` and then `wo_b`.
- `DeepseekV4GroupedWoAWithLoRA`, added in #57245, adds each group's delta:
  - LoRA-A is shared.
  - Group `g` uses LoRA-B rows `g*o_lora_rank:(g+1)*o_lora_rank`, each kept as its own buffer.
  - Under fully sharded LoRA, every rank keeps the full LoRA-A.
- This PR changes only the wrapper's type-only import.
- `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj` keeps its signature and behavior.

**Sharing with V4.1.**
- V4.1 already imports many pieces from V4: attention helpers, ops and model classes. Its `attention.py` and `compressor.py` now also import these two layers, and `deepseek_v41/common/grouped_wo_a.py` is deleted.
- Both LoRA wrappers match by class name, so they serve both models.

**Compatibility.**
- Both layers are plain subclasses. Nothing outside `vllm/lora` checks `type(...) is ColumnParallelLinear`/`MergedColumnParallelLinear`.
- The quant methods' `is_bmm` handling and #64827's `fp8_einsum` warmup read `wo_a` attributes, which the wrapper forwards.
- ROCm keeps reading `.weight` directly (fused compressor GEMM, mono decode, FP8 `wo_a`). Neither the AMD nor the CPU V4 model declares `SupportsLoRA`.
- XPU declares `SupportsLoRA` and picks up the compressor fix through the shared closures. Its `_o_proj` still reads `wo_a.bmm_weight` directly, so its `wo_a` adapters are still dropped. That is left for a follow-up.

**Tests.**
- The new V4 tests construct the real layers, LoRA wrappers and punica wrapper. They call the real `_run_parallel_input_projections` and the three backends' `_o_proj`.
- They check only V4's call sites. With an adapter set, V4's output must match the LoRA layer's own output. Without one, it must match the raw GEMM bit for bit.
- The wrapper's own math is covered by the existing V4.1 tests on the same layers: per-group LoRA-B, FP8 `wo_a`, the pointer cache, `reset_lora` and fully sharded LoRA.
- A `SimpleNamespace` stands in for the attention module, because building a real `DeepseekV4Attention` needs a full V4 config and GPU backends.
- The tests run in the H200 `LoRA` step and are skipped on its AMD mirror. That step doesn't watch `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/`, so a later V4-only change won't rerun them.

**Not a duplicate.**
- No open PR addresses this. I searched "deepseek v4 lora", "fused_wkv_wgate", "wo_a lora", "grouped_wo_a", "RopeQuant lora" and "pointer cache lora".
- #57245 (DeepSeek-V4.1 LoRA, merged) added the LoRA wrappers and V4.1-local copies of these layers. This PR applies them to V4 and removes the copies.
- #64827 (DeepGEMM warmup for the V4 o_proj) does not touch `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj` or the call sites.
- #44847 edits a different function in `o_proj.py`.

---

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Support n > 1 choices
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Support `n > 1` on `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/completions` in the Rust frontend, following Python's parallel sampling: render and tokenize the prompt once, then submit one engine request per sample. Today the Rust frontend rejects any `n > 1` with `400 Only n=1 is supported.`

Supersedes inactive vllm-project/vllm#58914, which fans out by calling `chat()`/`generate()` `n` times in the server and so renders the prompt (multimodal processing included) `n` times.

## Claims

- Chat and completions accept `n > 1`, streaming and non-streaming. Each choice carries its `index`; usage counts the prompt once and sums completion and reasoning tokens across choices.
- Like Python's `ParentRequest`, the prompt is rendered once, child requests use IDs `{index}_{request_id}` and `seed + index` when seeded, and the caller's external request ID stays on every child, so an abort or a client disconnect reaches every sample.
- `n` is validated like Python's `SamplingParams`: at least 1, at most `VLLM_MAX_N_SEQUENCES` (16384 by default; the chat DTO's old cap of 10 is gone), and 1 under greedy sampling, with Python's error messages.
- Metrics follow Python: `vllm:request_params_n` and `vllm:request_max_num_generation_tokens` are observed once per request, the other request histograms per sample, and per-request metrics in the response only for `n = 1`.
- `n = 1` takes the same path and is unchanged on the wire. `/inference/v1/generate` and gRPC still accept only `n = 1`; the render routes forward `n` into the rendered generate request, so `n > 1` keeps failing there explicitly instead of being dropped.

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root on this branch:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2550 tests run: 2550 passed, 13 skipped
```

The first commit also passes clippy and nextest on its own (2549 passed, 13 skipped).

New route tests against the mock engine (`rust/src/server/src/routes/tests.rs`):

- `chat_completions_n_returns_one_choice_per_seeded_sample`: child IDs and seeds `7`/`8` under one external ID; choices `hi`/`stop` and `yo`/`length` at indices 0/1; usage 22 + 5; the request-level histograms observed once (`n = 2`, max 3), the per-sample generation histogram twice.
- `chat_completions_stream_n_indexes_chunks_and_sends_one_usage_chunk` and `completions_stream_n_indexes_chunks_and_sends_one_usage_chunk`.
- `completions_n_returns_one_choice_per_sample`, with `seed: -1`: both children stay unseeded.
- `n_is_checked_like_python_sampling_params`: Python's messages for `n = 0`, `n > 16384`, and greedy sampling.
- `n_limit_follows_max_n_sequences_option`: the configured limit on chat, completions and both render routes; CLI tests cover the default, the env var, `--args-json` and an invalid value.
- `render_forwards_n_to_the_generate_request_check`: the render routes keep `n` and the generate route still rejects `n > 1`.

Red-green: on `main`, every new test except the render one fails (`n > 1` is rejected); the render test passes on `main` too and pins that removing the old check keeps the explicit error. With targeted reverts: dropping `seed + index` fails the seeded test, offsetting `-1` fails the completions test, yielding every per-choice usage chunk fails both stream tests, dropping the greedy check fails the validation test, a `< 1e-5` greedy threshold fails the tiny-temperature cases, observing the request-level histograms per sample fails the metrics assertions, and dropping `n` in render fails the render test.

Not run end to end on GPU in this PR. `test_completion.py::test_parallel_*` and the `n` cases in `test_chat.py` remain deselected in the Rust frontend CI step; `test_parallel_streaming` asserts at most `max_tokens` chunks per choice, while Rust sends the finish reason in a separate final chunk, so a length-limited choice gets one extra chunk.

## Details

The fan-out happens where Python does it, and each layer above returns one stream per sample instead of pushing a choice index through every stream type:

- `vllm-llm`: `generate_n(request, n)` is the required generation method of the `Llm` trait, and `generate` a provided method calling `generate_n(.., 1)`, since how `n` is carried out (child IDs, routing, request-level metrics) belongs to the implementation. `EngineCoreLlm::generate_n` submits the `n` child engine requests like `ParentRequest`. Seeds wrap on overflow, and `-1`, Python's unseeded sentinel, stays `-1` on every child (Python normalizes it to `None` before the fan-out). A shared `ParallelSamplingStats` observes the request-level histograms once, when the last child finishes (max over the children). `n = 1` submits the request unchanged.
- `vllm-text`: `TextLlm::generate_n` lowers once and decodes each child stream. It owns the greedy rule, checked against the resolved temperature (after generation-config defaults). Python first raises a positive temperature below 0.01 to 0.01, so only `temperature = 0` is greedy. Submission goes through the existing `submit` step, which now takes `n`, so the `--skip-tokenizer-init` structured-output check covers every sample.
- `vllm-chat`: `ChatLlm::chat_n` renders once and builds one output processor per sample, since parsers are stateful; the output grammar is built once and applied to the shared request.
- `vllm-server`: the routes resolve `n` like Python's `_verify_num_sequences`, run the existing per-choice chunk stream or collector for each sample, and merge. Streamed chunks interleave as the samples produce them, stamped with their choice index; the per-choice final usage chunks fold into one (`Usage::add_choice`); non-streaming responses append the choices in index order, with prompt-level fields from the first choice.
- `VLLM_MAX_N_SEQUENCES` is read once at startup through a hidden `--max-n-sequences` argument bound to the env var (and to the `--args-json` env fallbacks), parsed like Python's `int()`, and carried in `ApiServerOptions` and `RenderConfig`. An invalid value fails startup, where Python fails each request.

Ownership and layering: the fan-out (IDs, seeds, request-level metrics) sits in `vllm-llm`'s `EngineCoreLlm`, the `Llm` implementation that mirrors `AsyncLLM`; the greedy rule in `vllm-text`, which owns `SamplingParams` semantics; per-sample parsing in `vllm-chat`; wire DTO checks and response merging in `vllm-server`. `n` is passed as an argument rather than added to the shared request types, since only the fan-out and the greedy rule read it. The `n` range check stays in request lowering, which is configuration-free and shared with the render routes, separate from the configured upper limit.

Behavior notes:

- Chunk order across choices follows arrival; Python sends every choice's role chunk before any content chunk. Clients key on `index`, so this is not a wire contract.

Not a duplicate: the only open PR implementing `n` in the Rust frontend is vllm-project/vllm#58914, inactive since 2026-10-12 and built on a different design (see Overview); searched open PRs for `n choices`, `parallel sampling`, `n > 1` and `Only n=1`. The open beam-search PRs (vllm-project/vllm#47705, vllm-project/vllm#64862) cover a different feature. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this change; the human submitter reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Model] Fix Ling3 SwiGLU clamping
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

While investigating an accuracy issue during training–inference alignment for Ling RL, we found that routed experts applied the SwiGLU gate limit before SiLU, whereas the training/reference implementation applies it after SiLU. This mismatch can affect RL accuracy through inconsistent training and rollout computations, even though its impact is not obvious in standalone inference evaluations.

Use the existing `swiglustep` activation for Ling layers with a configured limit and forward that limit through the common MoE activation paths.

## Claims

- For limited Ling routed experts, compute `clamp(SiLU(gate), max=L) * clamp(up, -L, L)` instead of `SiLU(clamp(gate, max=L)) * clamp(up, -L, L)`.
- Honor the configured limit in both standard and masked `SWIGLUSTEP` activation paths.
- Keep unlimited Ling layers on `silu` and retain the default `SWIGLUSTEP` limit of `7.0` when no limit is supplied.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm][Kimi-K3] Refresh derived weight copies after in-place weight writes
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

This adds an opt-in module hook, `refresh_derived_weights()`, plus a walker in `weight_utils.py`. The walker is called from three shared paths that overwrite `state_dict()` tensors in place without the per-layer post-load hook:
- `SparseNCCLWeightTransferEngine.finish_weight_update`;
- the kernel-format branch of `reload_weights`;
- `ElasticEPScalingExecutor.prepare_new_worker`.

It does nothing unless a module defines the hook. Today only the Kimi-K3 ROCm KDA layer and MLA wrapper do, and the elastic-EP call has no model that reaches it yet. The PR also makes the Kimi-K3 ROCm `_w_fold` rebuild write in place.

Kimi-K3 on ROCm derives three tensors from its weights and keeps them outside `state_dict()`:
- `decode_conv1d_weight`, read by the AITER Gluon and HIP fused decode kernels;
- `decode_norm_weight`, read by the HIP kernel only;
- `_w_fold`, a plain attribute read by the fused decode-query GEMM.

The KDA copies (the first two) go stale on all three paths. `_w_fold` goes stale on the kernel-format reload and on elastic EP. On sparse NCCL it is rebuilt, but as a new tensor that CUDA graphs captured earlier do not read.

Related (all merged):
- #60110 added `_w_fold`.
- #61207 stages the KDA copies at load.
- #64158 builds `_w_fold` from the root model's hook.
- #64357 runs the model-level hook after every load, checkpoint-format reload and sparse NCCL update, but not after a kernel-format reload.

## Claims

The kernel-format reload claim is covered by the updated unit test. The sparse NCCL, elastic-EP and `_w_fold` claims come from reading the code (see Validation).

- **Kernel-format `reload_weights(..., is_checkpoint_format=False)`:** the Kimi-K3 ROCm KDA decode copies are re-staged from the reloaded weights, at the same addresses. On main they keep the values staged at load, while prefill reads the reloaded weights.
- **Sparse NCCL weight updates:** the same holds for an update that writes `conv1d.weight` or `o_norm.weight`.
- **Elastic-EP scale-up:** new ranks re-derive these tensors from the weights received from their peer, instead of keeping values computed from the dummy load. This is defensive for Kimi-K3. It does not set `num_moe_layers`, so EPLB never registers it and an elastic-EP scale-up cannot complete on it today (it fails at the `model.expert_weights` and `model_states` lookups).
- **`_w_fold`:** rebuilt in place. On main, layerwise reload and sparse NCCL assign a new `_w_fold`, so CUDA graphs captured before the rebuild keep the old, freed tensor's address.
- **Other models:** no change. Only modules that define `refresh_derived_weights()` are called.

## Validation

All runs used one MI355X (gfx950) with image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-3966924d566340e971a6da313e790d05492aa505`, with this branch's `vllm/` and `tests/` over the installed package. The image is 193 commits behind the base 5a233286c6; `csrc/kimi_k3` did not change in between.

`test_decode_weights_staged_after_loading` builds a real `KimiK3DeltaAttention`, then reloads every parameter with new values through `reload_weights(..., is_checkpoint_format=False)`. It checks that the staged copies match the reloaded weights and that no buffer moved.

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_decode.py tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_qb_uk_fold.py` | 45 passed |
| `test_decode_weights_staged_after_loading` on the base (every changed `vllm/` file from main, new test kept) | 2 failed, 2 passed |
| `pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py` | 82 passed, 17 skipped, 1 xpassed, 2 failed. The same 2 fail on the base: the NVFP4A16 `DeepSeek-V3-debug` cases of `test_reload_weights`, whose engine fails to start on this ROCm image. |
| `VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION=1 pytest tests/distributed/test_weight_transfer.py` (4 GPUs) | 114 passed, 26 skipped, 3 failed. The same 3 fail on the base: the `*_weight_transfer_between_processes` tests, whose Ray actors hit `invalid device ordinal` with two visible GPUs. |

On the base, both fp32-state cases fail after the reload, on `decode_conv1d_weight`. The bf16-state cases allocate no copies.

```
tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_decode.py:446: in test_decode_weights_staged_after_loading
tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_decode.py:424: in check_staged
E   AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not equal!
E   Mismatched elements: 18432 / 18432 (100.0%)
```

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>` (ruff 0.14.0, mypy): clean.

CI: `:amd: (MI355) Kimi K3` runs `pytest -v -s models/kimi_k3 --ignore=models/kimi_k3/test_prefix_cache.py` on this PR. The B200 step skips this ROCm-only file.

Not validated:
- **End to end:** no serving or RL run of Kimi-K3 on any of the three paths.
- **Call sites without a test:** the sparse NCCL and elastic-EP call sites. Both elastic-EP scale-up tests, `tests/distributed/test_elastic_ep.py` and `tests/v1/distributed/test_external_lb_dp.py::test_external_lb_elastic_ep_scale_up`, use DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, which has no module with the hook.
- **The in-place `_w_fold` rebuild:** no existing Kimi-K3 test builds a real MLA wrapper with `_fold_qb_uk` enabled (AITER MLA, fp8 KV cache, unquantized `q_b_proj`, no DCP or PCP), and adding one is a larger setup than this fix.

## Details

**How it was found.** By reading the code while reviewing #63612. It was not observed in a serving or RL run.

**Root cause.**
- The KDA copies are staged only in the layer's `process_weights_after_loading`. `_w_fold` is built only from the Kimi-K3 model-level hook.
- The kernel-format branch of `reload_weights` copies parameters and runs neither hook.
- Sparse NCCL ends with `finalize_model_weights`, which reaches the MLA wrappers through the model hook but not the KDA layers.
- Elastic EP builds new ranks with `load_dummy_weights=True` (`elastic_execute.py:273`), so both hooks derive these tensors from dummy weights. `batch_transfer_weights` then receives only `model.state_dict()` from a peer (`:97`) and runs no post-load pass.

**Change.**
- **The walker:** `weight_utils.refresh_derived_weights(model)` calls `refresh_derived_weights()` on every module that defines it, under `no_grad`.
- **The hook contract** (in the docstring): idempotent; reads only non-expert `state_dict()` tensors, since elastic EP moves routed experts later; no collectives; writes in place.
- **Callers:**
  - `prepare_new_worker`, after the transfer and `torch.accelerator.synchronize()`, under the worker's vLLM config;
  - `finish_weight_update`, after `finalize_model_weights`;
  - the kernel-format branch of `reload_weights`, after the copy loop.
- **`KimiK3DeltaAttention`:** the existing copy body moves into `refresh_derived_weights()`. `process_weights_after_loading` keeps the IPC weight-cache guard and calls it.
- **`KimiK3MultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper`:** `process_weights_after_loading()` and `refresh_derived_weights()` both rebuild `_w_fold`, which is copied in place once it exists.
- **Precedent:** `refresh_quantized_lm_heads` (`layers/quantization/online/lm_head.py:157`) re-derives copies in place after a weight reload, for the same CUDA-graph reason.

**Alternatives considered.**
- **Re-stage the KDA copies from the Kimi-K3 model hook (`amd/linear.py:1174`).** Sparse NCCL already runs that hook, so this fixes sparse NCCL with no core change. But the kernel-format reload runs no hook, and the elastic-EP receiver runs none, so a core call is needed anyway.
- **Refresh from the weight loader, as #63612 does for its GLM layer.** This covers writes that go through `load_weights`, such as sparse NCCL. It misses the kernel-format `param.copy_` and the elastic-EP `state_dict()` copy. #61207 also moved Kimi-K3's staging out of the loaders because dummy loads skip them.
- **Register the buffers as persistent, so `state_dict()` carries them.** This covers elastic EP only. It changes the key set of every saved Kimi-K3 `sharded_state` checkpoint ("Missing keys" on load), makes that key set depend on the decode backend picked at runtime, and does not cover `_w_fold`.
- **Re-run `finalize_model_weights` or the per-layer hooks on new elastic ranks.** Model-level hooks are not idempotent on already-processed weights in general: DeepSeek-V4 AMD preshuffles in its hook.

**Trade-offs and limits.**
- On sparse NCCL, `_w_fold` is now built twice per update (model hook, then the walker). That is one extra `_w_fold` build per MLA layer: `kv_b_proj` dequant, an einsum and a concat, then an in-place copy.
- The same pattern is left for follow-ups:
  - the Kimi-K3 NVIDIA KDA buffers, which only the weight loaders fill, so they are uninitialized after a dummy load;
  - `GateLinear._bf16x3_weight` for fp32-router models on gfx950;
  - #63612's GLM-5.3-Flash decode copy, a model that does reach elastic EP. Its layer could implement this hook.

**Duplicate check.**
- I searched open and closed PRs for `refresh_derived_weights`, `decode_conv1d_weight`, `_w_fold` and elastic-EP buffer staleness, and found the PRs listed above.
- #63612 refreshes its own layer's copy from its weight loader. No PR covers kernel-format reloads or elastic EP, or adds a hook that every in-place path calls.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Run DSpark's fused Markov sampling on gfx950 with --monokernel
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

This PR runs #60731's `fused_markov` DSpark sampler (one launch per draft position) on gfx950 (MI355X) with `--monokernel`, for steps of up to 5 requests. Today it runs only on gfx942, so gfx950 runs vLLM's loop of about 51 kernels per decode step at k=6. On MI355X, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP4 c1 decode steps get 2.4% faster at equal GSM8K and AL. It interacts with #63181, #63486 and #61311 (see Details).

## Claims

- With `--monokernel` on gfx950, a DSpark decode step's Markov sampling takes k+1 = 7 launches instead of about 51. Measured with the torch profiler, TP4, 2 rounds:
  - GPU kernels per decode step go from 365-366 to 321 (net -44 to -46);
  - the PR runs 7.00-7.01 `_markov_*` kernels per step.
- On gfx950 the fused launches take steps of at most 5 requests (`MAX_ROWS_GFX950`). From 6 on, vLLM's loop is faster there. Both archs launch the step kernel at 4 warps.
- On MI355X, `main` 335dd77b09 vs this PR (c128b8ba44):
  - Workload: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash `--monokernel`, DSpark k=6, AV off, synthetic AL 3.87, random 32k in / 1k out, `--ignore-eos`. Step = ITL p50.
  - Runs: 4 fresh servers per arm in ABBA order, each with 3 runs of 32 prompts. TP2 runs Engram on the host.

  | Config | `main` | PR | Delta | Spread across servers (`main` / PR) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | TP4 c1 | 5.372 ms | 5.245 ms | **-127 us (-2.36%)** | 0.39% / 0.44% |
  | TP4 c2 | 6.637 ms | 6.498 ms | **-139 us (-2.10%)** | 1.02% / 0.41% |
  | TP4 c4 | 8.614 ms | 8.530 ms | **-84 us (-0.98%)** | 0.91% / 0.49% |
  | TP4 c8 | 13.053 ms | 13.056 ms | +3 us (+0.02%): 8-row steps take vLLM's loop | 0.64% / 1.06% |
  | TP2 c1 | 6.434 ms | 6.288 ms | **-146 us (-2.27%)** | 0.52% / 1.01% |
- GSM8K-1319 and AL are unchanged (6 passes per arm):

  | Parallel requests | `main` GSM8K / AL | PR GSM8K / AL |
  |---|---|---|
  | 8 | 0.9189 / 3.576 | 0.9156 / 3.576 |
  | 4 | 0.9151 / 3.584 | 0.9151 / 3.581 |

  - At 8 parallel requests most steps have 8 rows, so both arms run the loop. At 4, every step takes the fused launches.
  - Numerics change only in the draft, as on gfx942: a 1-bf16-ULP bias difference can change a draft token, and rejection sampling keeps the target distribution.
- Unchanged: runs without `--monokernel`, other archs and every existing fallback (greedy drafts, AV, more than 8 requests, ...). No new flag or env var. No CI config change.
- gfx942 is unchanged by construction: there `monokernel_cdna3_or_4()` is true exactly when `enabled()` is, and the step kernel keeps 4 warps and `MAX_ROWS` = 8. Nothing was rerun on gfx942.

## Validation

All runs are at c128b8ba44 on MI355X. The current head, 9751254a4e, is rebased onto newer `main`. Its only code change since then is the gate refactor below: one check replaces the two wrappers, and it tests the same condition. The `main` arm is `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-335dd77b09161c5d63139b4e7ae51bb9928305b1`, built from this PR's base. The PR arm is that image plus this PR's `ops/__init__.py` and `ops/fused_markov.py`. The tests run in the image with `--noconftest`, because the image lacks `tblib`.

- [x] `tests/kernels/models/amd/test_dsv41_gfx942_fused_markov.py` on gfx950 at 4 warps: 6 passed. With `main`'s code: 6 failed (`assert fused_markov.sample_sequential(...)` is False, because the gate is gfx942-only).
- [x] `tests/kernels/models/amd/test_dsv41_gfx942_decode_meta.py` on gfx950 (#63885's kernel test, whose gate now shares the check): 3 passed.
- [x] `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py`: 82 passed.
  - With `main`'s code, 80 passed and 2 failed:
    ```
    E       assert False is True
    ```

- [x] TP4 c1/c2/c4/c8: 4 rounds, with `main` and PR running at once on the two GPU halves. One half ran (main, PR, PR, main) and the other (PR, main, main, PR).
  - Per round, c1 is 2.04-2.75% faster with the PR, c2 1.34-2.70% faster, and c4 0.60-1.43% faster.

**Microbench (the basis for the 5-row cap and for 4 warps).**
- It times one decode step's Markov sampling at k=6: all 6 draft positions, which is 7 launches fused and the whole loop on `main`.
- Shapes: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's head (vocab 129280, rank 256), random bf16 weights.
- Hardware: one MI355X GPU, graph-replayed with the MALL flushed.
- Values: median of 9 rounds of 200 replays, in us per decode step.

| Rows | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| vLLM's loop (`main`) | 225 | 286 | 339 | 355 | 1127 | 275 | 283 | 289 |
| fused, 4 warps (this PR; gfx950 takes 1-5) | 120 | 178 | 228 | 281 | 337 | 394 | 447 | 500 |
| fused, 8 warps (an earlier revision) | 120 | 177 | 240 | 290 | 347 | 403 | 457 | 514 |

- `rocm_unquantized_gemm` runs the loop's Markov GEMV on wvSplitK only for `0 < n <= 5`. From 6 rows it takes the generic GEMM, and the loop is cheaper there than the fused launches, whose cost grows by about 54 us per row.


**Bench.**
- Each server starts fresh and warms up with 4 prompts at 32k/256 and c2.
- Then 3 runs of each c in {1, 2, 4, 8} (TP2: c1 only), each with 32 prompts and seed 100+c.


**Design.**
- TP4: one server per GPU half (GPUs 0-3 and 4-7). Over 4 rounds, the halves ran (main, PR, PR, main) and (PR, main, main, PR).
- TP2: 4 servers at a time: (main, PR, PR, main), then (PR, main, main, PR).
- Every server's log was checked. Each PR server logs `DSpark fused Markov sampling: 6 steps, vocabulary 129280, rank 256, 505 blocks`, and no `main` server does.

| TP4 round | c1 `main` / PR | c2 `main` / PR | c4 `main` / PR | c8 `main` / PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5.381 / 5.234 (-2.75%) | 6.667 / 6.487 (-2.70%) | 8.616 / 8.557 (-0.68%) | 13.002 / 13.110 (+0.84%) |

| 4 | 5.368 / 5.239 (-2.40%) | 6.649 / 6.485 (-2.46%) | 8.618 / 8.515 (-1.20%) | 13.070 / 13.082 (+0.09%) |

**GSM8K** runs on separate block-rejection servers, because the perf servers force a synthetic AL.
- The client is an out-of-tree script over `/v1/completions`, using sglang `few_shot_gsm8k`'s prompt and scoring: 8-shot, temperature 0, at most 512 tokens.
- Each server runs one cold pass and two passes with a per-request `cache_salt`.
- Per pass at 8 parallel:

  - PR: 0.9189 0.9090 0.9166 0.9151 0.9121 0.9219
- Per pass at 4 parallel:
  - `main`: 0.9105 0.9143 0.9166 0.9128 0.9196 0.9166

**Launch count.**

- For each TP rank, it divides the rank's GPU kernels in the window by its decode steps. All 4 ranks give the same rate.

Per decode step, the PR removes:
- 6 each of argmax, gather, `_gumbel_sample_kernel` and the Markov GEMV (`wvSplitK`, two variants);
- 7 embedding and index lookups;
- about 8.5 copies and about 12 adds.

It adds 6 `_markov_step_kernel` and 1 `_markov_last_kernel`.

**Compile-only, gfx950** (step kernel at 4 warps, BLOCK 256, STEP 0 and 1, 1, 2, 4 and 8 rows; the kernel is unchanged since): 266-342 VGPRs+AGPRs, with no VGPR spills or scratch.
</details>

## Details

**Why:** #60731 was the gfx942 port, so it gated all of its helpers on `ops.enabled()`, which is gfx942-only. `fused_markov` is plain Triton on vLLM's own Gumbel helpers, with nothing gfx942-specific.

**Change:**
- `fused_markov` runs under `ops.monokernel_cdna3_or_4()`: `--monokernel` + ROCm + `get_cdna_version() in (3, 4)`, the same CDNA versions as the mono layer.
  - `swa_decode_meta` (#63885) uses the same check, in place of its `swa_decode_meta_enabled()`.
  - The other helpers keep `ops.enabled()`.
- `_why_not` caps CDNA4 (gfx950) at `MAX_ROWS_GFX950` = 5 rows. A larger step takes vLLM's loop, as a step of more than `MAX_ROWS` = 8 already does on gfx942. Under FULL CUDA graphs, the choice is made at capture for each padded batch size.
- Both archs launch the step kernel at 4 warps. `BLOCK` is unchanged.
- No speculator, model-runner or CPU-GPU sync changes.
- Tests:
  - `test_dspark_draft_model_samples_with_fused_markov` now drives the real gate with stub kernels in 4 cases. With `--monokernel`, the fused launches take a 5-row step on gfx950 and an 8-row step on gfx942. vLLM's loop takes a 6-row step on gfx950, and any step without the flag.
  - The gfx942 kernel test clears the new check's cache.
  - No new test or test file.

**CI coverage:** there is no `.buildkite` change.
- The gate test runs in the existing MI355 "Basic Models (Other)" job.
- The kernel test runs only in the MI300 gfx942 kernels job.
- No CI job runs the fused launch on gfx950. It was run by hand at this head: 6 passed.

**Limitations:**
- The kernel test compares the fused launches with vLLM's loop at 1 and 2 requests and k=5 only.
- 3-5-row steps on gfx950 were timed by the microbench and ran end to end at c4 and in GSM8K. Outputs at those row counts are compared only through GSM8K and AL.
- AV on: no effect, because a step with the acceptance estimator or the confidence head falls back to the loop.
- `use_fp64_gumbel` is untested on either arch, as before this PR.

**Related PRs:**
- **#63181:** a separate fusion of the same loop: a Markov GEMV and a sample epilogue, 2 launches per draft position.
  - With both merged, this hook runs first. So #63181's path runs without `--monokernel`, on steps that `fused_markov` declines, and on gfx950 steps of 6-8 requests.
  - Its head predates `main`'s `DraftLogitsCache` and conflicts with `main`. The head-to-head waits for its rebase.
- **#63885** (merged: SWA decode metadata in one launch on gfx950) added `swa_decode_meta_enabled()`. This PR replaces it with `monokernel_cdna3_or_4()`, which both helpers use.
- **#63486** and **#61311** move or delete the test files and the MI300 CI job that runs them, and make the kernel test gfx942-only.
  - #61311 also renames `ops._monokernel` and `record_monokernel` to `_specialized_decode` and `record_specialized_decode`. The shared check and both tests use those names.
  - Whichever lands first, this PR follows: it widens that skip to gfx950 and, after #61311, renames the flag.
- **#61869:** a CUDA-only fused Markov sampler. It does not reach ROCm.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Skip the top-k -1 fill on the rows vLLM's decode top-k writes
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The paged MXFP4 sparse indexer (gfx950, #58671) fills the step's top-k rows with -1 before its top-k kernels run. On decode rows that go to vLLM's `top_k_per_row_decode` (gfx950 k = 512 path: #56743), the fill is dead: that kernel writes all k entries of every row. This PR skips the fill on those rows, as the gfx942 indexer already does (#60731), and adds a GPU test for the mixed and padded steps the skip also covers.

## Claims

- **Same output as main.** Below 128 rows and below k = 2048, every path of `top_k_per_row_decode` stores all k slots of each row, with -1 past a short row's end, so the skipped -1 would always be overwritten. On the gather path, `_remap_compact_topk` then rewrites every slot. This write-all property was checked on MI355X at k = 32, 512 and 1024, rather than by diffing outputs against main:
  - A sentinel sweep of the kernel, called as `_topk` calls it, found no unwritten slot in 480 of 480 cases (240 shapes, each with two data distributions).
  - With the fill removed from every row, the indexer's GPU tests still pass, except the 6 cases with trailing padding rows. Those fail only on the padding rows, after their decode and prefill rows have passed.
- **8 fewer kernels per decode step (measured), all inside the decode graph.** That is one per index layer of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. `FillFunctor<int>` drops from 17 to 9 per decode step at both c1 and c2. Total kernels per step drop by exactly 8, and the `topKPerRowDecode`, mono K1 and eager-fill counts do not change.
- **Gain: small.** A 2-round ABBA on a main nightly measured -13 us (-0.25%) per decode step at c1 and -7 us (-0.11%) at c2.
  - The gain has the same sign and size on both GPU halves: -13 / -14 us at c1, -8 / -7 us at c2.
  - The 8 removed fills took about 37 us of in-graph kernel time per step in the profile, so the end-to-end saving is about a third of that.
  - There is no regression.
- **Accuracy unchanged.** GSM8K-1319: 0.9191 vs 0.9183. Real AL: 3.579 vs 3.576. Both are means over 4 runs per arm. Per-question flips between main and this PR (mean 66.9 questions) are within the flips between two runs of the same code (main 72.8, PR 63.2).
- **Unchanged elsewhere.** These rows keep the fill:
  - rows that aiter's top-k takes (128+ decode rows, which is about 19+ requests at DSpark k = 6, or k >= 2048);
  - steps without decode rows;
  - rows after the decode rows (padding, prefill).

## Validation

**CPU, on 9fc85b7dda** (this PR's first commit, rebased on main 434eadcbf8; same diff as the earlier 517b6d3f44). It ran in a CPU-only container on the nightly below.
- [x] `tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer_plan.py`: 8 passed. That is the new `test_topk_fill_skips_the_rows_vllms_topk_writes` (4 cases) plus 4 existing tests.
- [x] The test fails without the change, and against each of these mutants (output below):
  - main's behaviour (fill from row 0): fails `[7-512-7]`
  - no kernel gate: fails `[128-512-0]` and `[7-2048-0]`
  - a `<= 128` / `<= 2048` gate: fails `[128-512-0]` and `[7-2048-0]`
  - a decode step that skips the whole fill: fails `[7-512-7]`
- [x] `pre-commit run --files` passed on both commits (ruff, mypy, typos, test tethering). No kernel source changed.

**GPU: MI355X, main = `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-edad8b03c5285a1c12e7e4f83c1af709b319a01b`.** The GPU runs were done against main a6c3635e36, which that nightly is 63 commits behind. Main is now 434eadcbf8.
- **Same as main in the image (sha-checked against a6c3635e36):** the ops file; the MXFP4 and base indexer metadata builders; `deepseek_v41/amd/mono_decode.py`; `deepseek_v41/attention.py`; `backends/utils.py`; `breakable_cudagraph.py`.
- **Changed on main since then,** none of it on this skip's path:
  - #63047 sizes the base builder's (`mla/indexer.py`) expanded decode block table by decode tokens. The decode-row order and `decode_row_lens` are unchanged.
  - #60229 captures adaptive-verification FULL graphs with padding rows. Those rows have length 0, so vLLM's top-k writes them as all -1.
  - #64101 lets mono decode run at TP8. It calls the same op the same way.
- **Same as main in git:** the top-k kernel (`csrc/sampler.cu`) and the three test files are unchanged between edad8b03c5 and main. The image ships neither, and the tests ran from this PR's head.
- **Two nearby files differ,** neither on this op's path: a fused-shared-expert guard in `deepseek_v41/amd/model.py`, and one DBO-only capture line in `v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py`.
- **PR arm:** the same image plus this PR's ops file.
- **Commits tested:** the unit tests were re-run on the current head, f3dc96acdb: plan test 8 passed, indexer GPU test 42 passed on both arms. The sweep, profile, ABBA and GSM8K ran on 4eddaa283f, which differs from the head only in comments.

- [x] **Plan test:** 8 passed.
- [x] **`tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer.py`:** 42 passed. That includes the new `test_decode_rows_skip_the_fill_in_mixed_and_padded_steps`: 9 cases (decode rows + 3 padding rows, mixed decode + prefill, and both) at k = 32 / 512 / 1024.
  - It also passes 42/42 with main's ops file.
  - With the fill removed from every row, exactly its 6 padded cases fail. They fail on the padding-row check, after the dense layer's decode and prefill rows have passed.
- [x] **`tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py -k gfx950`:** 22 passed. No CI step runs these on gfx950.
- [x] **Sentinel sweep of `top_k_per_row_decode`:** 480/480 cases clean. Two corrupted-output controls each fail 480/480. Details are below.
- [x] **Profile, main vs this PR, c1 and c2:** 8 fewer `FillFunctor<int>` per decode-graph replay, all in-graph. Table below.
- [x] **ABBA at c1/c2:** 2 rounds with the GPU halves swapped. Table below.
- [x] **GSM8K-1319 and real AL:** 2 swapped rounds, cold and cache-salted passes, with per-question flips. Table below.
- [ ] **DeepSeek-V4 end to end:** not run, because there is no V4 checkpoint on the test node.
  - **CI that reaches this op:** with AITER on and the indexer dtype left at `auto`, #63669 picks MXFP4, so these DeepSeek-V4-Flash jobs run through this op:
    - `:amd: (MI355) LM Eval Large Models FP8` (DeepSeek-V4-Flash-MXFP4, TP4);
    - the nightly `:amd: (MI355) [Nightly] LM Eval Large Models` (DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4, TP8);
    - AMD CI's optional `:amd: (MI355) DSv4-Flash Disaggregated DP EP`.

    This PR's files trigger only the last one, and it needs `/amd-ci run` and an Unblock.
  - **CI that does not:** the DSpark DeepSeek-V4 GSM8K configs pin `indexer_kv_dtype=fp8`, so they never reach this op.
  - **Coverage of V4's k:** any `index_topk` below 2048 takes the same skip. DeepSeek-V4-Flash's is 512, the same as V4.1, and V4-Pro's is 1024 (`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/mono/dims.py`). The new test and the sweep cover both.

**Profile.** The table is per decode step, over 440-462 one-request (7-row) steps and 258-336 two-request (14-row) steps of the profiled window, on ranks 0 and 3.
- Counts are the per-step mode, identical on both ranks.
- Fill time is the per-step median: 36.1-36.2 us on rank 0, 37.5-37.6 us on rank 3.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `FillFunctor<int>` per step | 17 (8 in-graph, 9 eager) | 9 (0 in-graph, 9 eager) |
| In-graph fill time per step | 36.1-37.6 us | 0 |
| Kernels per step, 7-row / 14-row | 410 / 416 | 402 / 408 |
| `topKPerRowDecode` / mono K1 per step | 12 / 40 | 12 / 40 |

All 8 removed fills run inside the FULL decode graph (via `hipGraphLaunch`), each right after the layer's `_q_rope_mxfp4_quant` kernel.

**Perf.** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on one MI355X node: TP4 `--monokernel`, DSpark k = 6, AV off, random 32k in / 1k out with `--ignore-eos`, synthetic AL 3.87.
- Decode step = ITL p50, mean of 3 runs of 32 prompts per point.
- The profile and GSM8K servers used block rejection instead. The fill count and fill time per step do not depend on acceptance, because every decode step verifies 7 rows per request.

| conc | main | this PR | ABBA change | per round (P1 / P2) | same half (GPUs 0-3 / 4-7) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5.446 ms | 5.432 ms | -13 us (-0.25%) | -0.54% / +0.05% | -13 / -14 us |
| 2 | 6.649 ms | 6.642 ms | -7 us (-0.11%) | -0.44% / +0.23% | -8 / -7 us |

- GPUs 4-7 run about 0.3% faster than GPUs 0-3, which is why the two rounds differ. The swap cancels that.
- This PR is faster on both halves, by less than the ~37 us of fill time the profile removes. With 3 runs per point (spread up to 24 us), read the result as a small gain with no sign of a regression.
- An earlier unswapped A/B on a stack image showed -63 us at c1. That is more than the fills can account for, so it was drift.

**Accuracy.** GSM8K-1319, 8-shot, greedy, 8 in parallel. AL is taken from cold and cache-salted passes only.

| arm | runs | GSM8K | AL |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 4 | 0.9183 (0.9143-0.9212) | 3.576 (3.569-3.583) |
| this PR | 4 | 0.9191 (0.9143-0.9212) | 3.579 (3.568-3.594) |

Per-question correctness flips have these means:
- main vs PR: 66.9 (56-77, 16 pairs);
- main vs main: 72.8 (65-81, 6 pairs);
- PR vs PR: 63.2 (56-67, 6 pairs).

Greedy text identity is not reproducible on this stack even between two runs of one arm, so it is not used.

<details>
<summary>Setup, commands and test output</summary>

**CPU.** The CPU run overlays the given ops file onto the vLLM in the image. A stub `amdsmi` reports gfx950, and the container runs with `--network none` and no `/dev/kfd`.

```text
$ pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer_plan.py     # this PR
8 passed, 14 warnings in 17.39s
# fill from row 0 (main's behaviour)
FAILED tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer_plan.py::test_topk_fill_skips_the_rows_vllms_topk_writes[7-512-7]

# no kernel gate
FAILED ...::test_topk_fill_skips_the_rows_vllms_topk_writes[128-512-0]

# <= 128 / <= 2048 gate
FAILED ...::test_topk_fill_skips_the_rows_vllms_topk_writes[128-512-0]

# main's ops file
E   ImportError: cannot import name '_fill_topk_rows' from 'vllm.v1.attention.ops.rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer'
```

**GPU unit tests, one MI355X each.**

```text
plan test, PR                       8 passed
indexer GPU test, PR                42 passed
indexer GPU test, main's ops file   42 passed
indexer GPU test, no fill at all    6 failed, 36 passed   (exactly [decode-3-*] and [mixed-3-*], on the padding-row check)
test_top_k_per_row.py -k gfx950     22 passed, 640 deselected
sentinel sweep                      SWEEP OK: 480/480 cases clean
sweep, corrupted outputs            SWEEP FAILED: 0/480 cases clean (each of 2 controls)
```

**Sentinel sweep.** The output is pre-filled with -777. The kernel is then called as `_topk` calls it: `torch.ops._C.top_k_per_row_decode(logits, 1, lengths, out, rows, logits.stride(0), logits.stride(1), k)`, with fp32 logits and 1-D int32 lengths.
- Parameters:
  - k: 512 and 1024.
  - Rows: 1, 7, 14, 32, 33, 60, 64, 65, 100 and 127.
  - Widths: 4096, 12287, 12288, 16385, 65537, 199999, 200000, 262145, 524288 and 1048576.
  - Row lengths: 0, 1, k-1, k, k+1, the full width, and random.
  - Data: randn, and a tie-heavy integer distribution.
  - Logits: contiguous, plus a strided view at two widths.
- This reaches every gfx950 k = 512 config below 128 rows (one block; split + merge for <= 32 rows above 16K, and for <= 128 rows above 64K). For k = 1024 it reaches the insertion, radix, split and device-length-aware paths.
- For each row of length L and n = min(k, L), it checks:
  - no -777 is left;
  - there are exactly n distinct indices in [0, L);
  - each index's logit is >= the n-th largest;
  - exactly k - n slots hold -1.
- The two controls each fail 480/480:
  - one leaves one -777 slot;
  - the other turns a -1 slot into a stale index. That index is in range wherever the row is not empty, and the checker catches it as a duplicate.

**Servers.** Each arm is one TP4 server per GPU half (GPUs 0-3 and 4-7). The perf rounds used synthetic AL 3.87. The accuracy and profile rounds used `"rejection_sample_method":"block"`, without the synthetic AL.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=True \
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --monokernel \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --moe-backend aiter --block-size 128 --max-model-len 1048576 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":6,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.87,"enable_adaptive_verification":false}'
```

**Perf client.** It runs for c = 1 and 2, 3 times each, after a 4-prompt warm-up (32k/256 at conc 2). P1 put main on GPUs 0-3 and this PR on 4-7. P2 swapped them.

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend openai --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 32768 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos \
  --max-concurrency $c --num-prompts 32 --seed $((100 + c)) \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,99
```

**Accuracy.** The test is GSM8K-1319, 8-shot, greedy, at 8 in parallel, on two rounds with the GPU halves swapped. Each server ran one cold pass, then one pass with a per-request `cache_salt`, so no prefix-cache reuse. Warm repeat passes lower DSpark AL on main and are not used. AL = 1 + Δ`vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_total` / Δ`vllm:spec_decode_num_drafts_total`, read from `/metrics`.

**Profile.** `--profiler-config '{"profiler":"torch",...}'` was set on the first accuracy round's servers. After their GSM8K passes, the window was c1 with 2 prompts and c2 with 4 prompts, 32k in / 256 out.
- Steps are delimited by the mono K1 kernel for 7 rows or 14 rows. The 7-row steps include the c2 window's single-request steps.
- A fill counts as in-graph when its runtime call is `hipGraphLaunch`. Kineto records no grid or block for graph-replayed kernels, so the indexer fill is identified by the kernel just before it.
- Step times in a profiled run are inflated and are not used.

**Why every vLLM-kernel row is fully written** (`csrc/sampler.cu` on main):
- `topKPerRowJob` either takes the `rowLen <= topK` shortcut (indices, then -1 up to k) or ends in the final store loop over all k slots.
- gfx950 k = 512 (`topKPerRowDecode512DeviceLengthAware`): a row runs either in one block that stores directly, or in split blocks plus a merge launch. Both launches compute the same `activeBlocks`, so each row is written exactly once.
- The k = 1024 path and the generic insertion, radix and split+merge paths end in the same store loop.
- `rowEnd` is clamped to >= 0, so a padding row (length 0) is written as all -1.
- Rows are addressed at stride k. Both callers, DeepSeek-V4 and V4.1, allocate the buffer as `[max_num_batched_tokens, index_topk]`, so its width is k.

</details>

## Details

**Design.** `_vllm_topk(rows, k)` holds `_topk`'s dispatch condition (`rows < 128 and k < 2048`). Both entry points call `_fill_topk_rows`.
- When `_vllm_topk` holds for the decode rows, the fill starts after them. Otherwise it fills from row 0, as before.
- Decode rows lead the step (flattened). Padding requests have seq_len 0, so the kernel writes all -1 for their rows.
- Both decode paths write exactly `topk_buffer[:rows, :k]`.

**Gate and tradeoffs.**
- **Env-free and shape-only.** FULL graphs capture the same choice, and breakable graphs decide per step. No device tensor is read on the host.
- **In-graph.** At c1/c2 every decode step replays a FULL uniform-decode graph of 7/14 rows (`v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py`). Mono takes a layer only in NONE or FULL mode, and `eager_break_during_capture` passes the op through under FULL. So the op and main's 8 fills are captured in the graph, and the saving is in-graph GPU time only. Only mixed and prefill steps (breakable PIECEWISE) run the op as an eager break.
- **Scope.** #60731 requires a pure-decode, unpadded step. This gate also skips the decode rows of padded and mixed steps.
  - The new GPU test covers both: decode rows followed by prefill rows, and by padding rows, at k = 32, 512 and 1024.
  - The GSM8K runs at 8 in parallel also run mixed steps end to end.
  - The decode-only form (`metadata.prefill is None`) is a one-line change if reviewers prefer it.
- **Models.** The op serves DeepSeek-V4.1 and, on CDNA4 with AITER on, DeepSeek-V4 by default (#63669). DeepSeek-V4 decode takes the same skip whenever its `index_topk` is below 2048 (512 on V4-Flash, 1024 on V4-Pro). V4-Flash has 21 indexer layers, so its decode step should drop 21 fills rather than V4.1's 8. It has not been run end to end; see Validation.
- **Contract.** The skip relies on vLLM's kernel writing every slot. These tests check that:
  - `test_topk_matches_torch_on_both_kernels[8-4096-512]`: vLLM's kernel at k = 512, pre-filled with 7, with a row shorter than k.
  - The new mixed/padded test: the full op at k = 32 / 512 / 1024.
  - `test_top_k_per_row_decode_gfx950_k512_1d_seq_lens` and `_masked_graph_replay`, which pre-fill -777.

  The decode-layer tests run k = 32, the generic path. The shared predicate guards edits to `_vllm_topk` only; other edits to `_topk`'s aiter branch are caught only by these GPU tests. Rows taken by aiter's top-k keep the fill.

**Limitations.**
- **Small gain.** The profile removes ~37 us of in-graph kernel time per step. The end-to-end ABBA measured -13 us at c1 and -7 us at c2, on 2 rounds, one MI355X node and a main nightly.
- **No DeepSeek-V4 end-to-end run.**
- **CI coverage.** Default CI runs only the CPU plan test here: `:amd: (MI300) V1 Attention` and `:amd: (MI355 DPX) V1 Attention` are not optional and start once the PR is `ready`. The GPU indexer test runs only in AMD CI's optional `:amd: (MI355 DPX) Attention Kernels`, which needs `/amd-ci run` and an Unblock. No CI job runs `test_top_k_per_row.py` on gfx950.

<details>
<summary>Related PRs and sibling PRs</summary>

Related:
- #44527 dropped the ROCm FP8 indexer's fill for all rows, and #53906 restored it (`vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py:1393` on main). This PR keeps the fill on every row that the decode top-k does not write.
- #61985 (GLM-5/DSv3.2 on this indexer at k = 2048) keeps the fill under this gate. It has a trivial textual conflict in the plan test file.
- #50201 (top-k NaN hardening) is complementary.

This is one of six independent PRs against main from the same DeepSeek-V4.1 low-concurrency MI355X work. It shares no files with the others:
- #63885: build the SWA decode metadata in one launch on gfx950
- #63890: use AITER's all-gather for small TP all-gathers
- #63891: run DSpark's fused Markov sampling on gfx950 with --monokernel
- #63892: mono, batch TP4 K2's X8 copies, load its push's peer bases late
- #63893: mono, tuned K1 at TP4

</details>

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MiniMax-M3] Initialize the shard record in the indexer QKV layer
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Since #63752, MiniMax-M3 checkpoints fail to load:

```
AttributeError: 'MinimaxM3QKVParallelLinearWithIndexer' object has no attribute 'loaded_shard_ids'
```

#63752 added the per-shard loading record (`loaded_shard_ids`) in
`StackedColumnParallelLinear.__init__`. `MinimaxM3QKVParallelLinearWithIndexer` skips
`QKVParallelLinear.__init__` (it builds its own 5-group layout) by calling
`ColumnParallelLinear.__init__` directly, so it skipped the stacked init too.

Call `StackedColumnParallelLinear.__init__` instead. It sets up the record and forwards to
`ColumnParallelLinear.__init__` unchanged. The layer is also added to the shard-tracking tests.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_stacked_shard_tracking.py`
- E2E: `vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash -pp 2` on 2x B300, then a few chat requests.

## Test Result

- Shard-tracking tests: 9 passed. The new test fails on main with the `AttributeError` above.
- E2E: the server starts (it fails on main during weight loading) and answers correctly, e.g. "What is the capital of France? Answer in one word." → "Paris"; "Translate to German: The weather is nice today." → "Das Wetter ist heute schön."
