commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Serve gfx942 MLA verify past 4 tokens with a Triton kernel
commits.pr_body:
- Route causal verify longer than 4 tokens on CDNA3 (no DCP) to a new Triton verify kernel in `rocm_aiter_mla.py`; shorter verify, decode, prefill, DCP and gfx950 keep their current paths.
- Add `decode_attention_fwd_verify` to `triton_decode_attention.py`: one program reads each KV tile once for a block of a request's (token, head) rows, with a per-row causal limit, int64 page offsets and FP8 dequant. Its variants are compiled before serving, so ngram drafts of any length never JIT mid-request.
- Undo the FP8 V-scale drop of AITER's qlen 2-4 FP8 decode kernel (ROCm/aiter#6732), found by a one-time probe, so a fixed AITER turns the correction off by itself.
- Apply the per-TP head override of `test_mla_backends.py` on ROCm as well (it was XPU only), so ROCm CI tests real per-rank head counts instead of 128 heads at every TP.
- Below page size 8 with bf16, read the block table one tile ahead instead of two: above 2 GiB of KV, Triton's global-load variant of the kernel otherwise spills VGPRs (2.1-3.1x slower at `--block-size 1`).
- Add an op test for the new kernel (bf16 and FP8, pages 1 and 16, ragged, padded and varlen rows).

On MI300X, MTP or ngram with 4 or more draft tokens fails at startup: AITER's persistent bf16 MLA decode only has kernels up to 4 query tokens, and its non-persistent kernels are not a safe fallback. They return wrong results at 32 heads, ignore the causal mask at 64/128 heads, and at 16 heads (what padded ranks such as TP2 of a 16-head model use today) read the wrong KV pages once the cache passes 4 GiB (ROCm/aiter#6733). That last case is silent: DeepSeek-V2-Lite at TP2 with k=7 drops to GSM8K 0.004 once serving fills the cache past 4 GiB, and goes back to 0.605 with this PR. Raising an error instead (as #57642 does) would leave MTP 4+ unusable on MI300 and break the gfx942 DCP verify routes that work today. This fixes item 1 of #55609 and needs no AITER change to be correct.

**Still open on the AITER side (not blocking this PR, but blocking a fully green `test_mla_backends.py` on MI300):**
- ROCm/aiter#6731: the persistent `_ps` decode kernel returns wrong output in about 1 of 1000 calls (a race). ROCm/aiter#6277 (open) brings it to 6 bad calls in 250k but not to zero. In 30 runs of the whole file on this branch it shows up as an occasional `ROCM_AITER_MLA` mismatch on unchanged decode paths.
- ROCm/aiter#6735, fixed by ROCm/aiter#6748 (rounds CK forward attention to nearest): `test_chunked_context_backend_correctness[...glm...]` fails on main and on this branch because CK's FMHA forward truncates bf16; it passes 100/100 seeds with that change.
- ROCm/aiter#6732, ROCm/aiter#6733: the FP8 V-scale and the non-persistent kernel bugs worked around here.

**Results** (MI300X, AITER v0.1.25, DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, ngram drafts; `vllm bench serve`, mean of 2 runs, output tok/s):

| config | workload | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| TP1, no spec | InstructCoder c1 / c32 | 281 / 2046 | 280 / 2001 |
| TP1, no spec | random 1k/256 c1 / c32 | 259 / 3202 | 258 / 3100 |
| TP1, k=3 | InstructCoder c1 / c32 | 306 / 2507 | 315 / 2669 |
| TP1, k=7 | InstructCoder c1 / c32 | startup fails | 339 / 2700 |
| TP1, k=7 | random 1k/256 c1 / c32 | startup fails | 325 / 3201 |
| TP2, k=7 | InstructCoder c1 / c32 | 356 / 3042 | 370 / 3264 |
| TP2, k=7 | random 1k/256 c1 / c32 | 324 / 3557 | 369 / 3766 |

The c32 differences without spec decode are within this host's run-to-run noise (the same path runs on both). GSM8K 5-shot (lm_eval, 1319) is 0.647-0.663 for every config on both branches, and the TP2 k=7 0.004 above is the >4 GiB case.

**Against the per-token row-view** (what gfx942 DCP verify uses: one row per draft token through the generic split-KV kernel). MI300X, AITER v0.1.27, DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, ngram k=7, TP1, one server at a time on the same GPU, output tok/s:

| | InstructCoder c1 / c32 | random 1k/256 c1 / c32 |
|---|---|---|
| this PR | 426 / 3864 | 490 / 4606 |
| row-view, launch config and splits tuned for gfx942 | 400 / 3520 | 454 / 4086 |
| row-view, as it ships | 290 / 3385 | 313 / 3511 |

Per layer, with both kernels in HIP graphs on identical inputs and a production-size KV pool, row-view is 1.8-4.6x slower as it ships and 1.44x slower on geomean when tuned (0.96-2.4x across 16-128 heads and batch 1-64). The c1 gap over tuned row-view (6-8%) is outside this host's noise; at c32 this PR is ahead in every round run, but by less than the c32 run-to-run spread. TP2 and k=5 show the same ordering, and GSM8K is 0.648-0.668 on every arm.

Tests: `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_decode_attention.py -k verify` (48 passed; 10/10 runs with the page-size fix), `tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py`, and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py` 30 times: every run passes all spec-decode and verify cases (634 passed). The two remaining failures are both AITER-side and listed above: `test_chunked_context_backend_correctness[...auto-glm...]` fails in all 30 runs (max diff 0.031, identical on `TRITON_MLA`, the CK prefill), and 8 of 30 runs have one FP8 `large_decode` (qlen 1, unchanged decode path) `ROCM_AITER_MLA` mismatch of 0.16-0.39 from the persistent-kernel race. On main the 16 `spec_decode_medium` cases fail every run with `cannot get heuristic kernel ... qseqlen:8`.

commits.pr_title: [Core] Cheapen the spin while waiting for model output
commits.pr_body:
#65466 waits for a step's output by looping on future.poll(), which runs several Python calls with the GIL held before each sched_yield(). This delays the engine's input and output threads, and costs some throughput and tail latency, even when no inputs are handled during the wait.

Between polls, spin directly on the response queue's flags and the input queue instead, so that an iteration costs about 1us rather than 4us. Inputs are still handled as they arrive, so requests still reach the scheduler about as early as with #65466 (median queue wait about 25us, compared with 5-7ms before it).

For a remote reader, move the sleep on its socket into this new wait, so that readable() is non-blocking again and a loop iteration sleeps only once.

Qwen3-0.6B on GB200, MP executor, Rust frontend. Medians, before #65466 -> #65466 -> this change:

TP=1, 8 repeats, arrivals (128/8 tokens, 256 concurrent):
- 3,224 -> 3,133 -> 3,183 req/s; TTFT p99 58.8 -> 65.1 -> 59.7ms

TP=4, 3 repeats:
- decode (32/512, 256 concurrent): 81,670 -> 74,830 -> 81,500 tok/s
- single request (32/256): 685 -> 590 -> 700 tok/s

TP=4, 6 repeats, before #65466 -> this change:
- arrivals: 2,839 -> 2,869 req/s
- Poisson at 2,014 req/s: TTFT p99 47.0 -> 43.1ms; ITL p99 10.7 -> 10.3ms

commits.pr_title: [CI] Consolidate per-version model labels into vendor/family labels
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The repo currently tracks a mix of vendor/family labels (`deepseek`, `qwen`, `minimax`, `kimi`, …) and per-model-version labels (`DSv4`, `DSv4.1`, `k3`, `Qwen3.5+`). Every new model iteration requires new label automation, which has become diminishing returns. This consolidates labeling onto vendor/family labels (matching what SGLang does for new-model tracking):

- **Drop the `DSv4` / `DSv4.1` rules** — `DSv4` mentions in titles now fold into the `deepseek` vendor label. The existing `deepseek` file rules already cover the `vllm/models/deepseek_v4*/` trees, so no coverage is lost.
- **Drop the `k3` launch-triage rule** — `K3` mentions now fold into the `kimi` family label (the rule was already marked "retire after ramp-down").
- Same consolidation in the `issue_autolabel` workflow for issues.

`mrv1-only` / `mrv2` are Model Runner V1/V2 (engine internals), not model versions — left untouched. `Qwen3.5+` has no automation; it is a manual label only.

## Post-merge action for a maintainer

Delete the now-unused labels from repo settings: `DSv4`, `DSv4.1`, `k3`, `Qwen3.5+`.

## Test Plan

- Both YAML files parse; the workflow's embedded JS passes `node --check`.
- Simulated the matcher logic against sample titles: `DSv4 serving crash` → `deepseek`, `Deepseek V4.1 MTP regression` → `deepseek`, `K3 MTP acceptance rate low` → `kimi`, `Kimi K3 reasoning parser bug` → `kimi`.

commits.pr_title: [CI][Kernels] Make the MiniMax-M3 decode top-k test deterministic
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix the flaky `(L4) Attention Kernels` failure on main: `tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py::test_decode_index_topk_correctness[0-4-4]` fails with `assert {0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 7} == {0, 1, 4, 5, 6, 7}`. It has failed 17 times since build [99886](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/99886), with no related kernel or test change.

**Root cause.** The decode indexer computes scores with `tl.dot` on fp32 inputs, which runs at TF32 precision on L4. The reference uses a true-FP32 `einsum`. The test draws unseeded `randn` inputs, so whenever two blocks score within TF32 rounding of each other at the top-6 boundary, the two sides pick different blocks. The `[2-4-4]` sibling case, which takes the same `q_len=4` path, passes, so this isn't a kernel bug. The test just picks up whatever RNG state earlier tests in the shard left behind.

**Fix.**
- Draw the test's inputs from a local `torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(0)`, so they no longer depend on the global RNG state that earlier tests in the shard leave behind.
- Round `idx_q` and `index_kv_cache` to bf16-representable values. A product of two such values is exact in TF32, so the kernel and the reference compute identical products; the only remaining difference is fp32 accumulation order. The assertion stays a strict set-equality check.

Not a duplicate: there are no open PRs for this test. #52847 changes the decode index tile, not this test.

## Test Plan

- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` / `py_compile` pass locally.
- I have no GPU locally, so the test hasn't been run on GPU yet. The step should go green on this PR's L4 CI.

## Test Result

Pending CI.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Mono: tuned K1/K2 for the TP2 compress-ratio-2 layers on MI355X
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Faster K1/K2 for the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash mono decode layer on gfx950 (MI355X), applied only to the compress-ratio-2 target layers at TP2. A static build flag, `MonoBuild.tuned`, selects the new paths; their outputs are bit-identical to main's, and every other build (ratio 0/1, TP4, DSpark draft, gfx942, FFN launch) compiles to the same MLIR as on main.

1. **Tuned builds of the ratio-2 layers**: the `MonoBuild.tuned` gate with its own scratch; unsigned index math in the MoE stages; polled ready flags replicated on separate lines; independent loads issued ahead of waits.
2. **Down stage**: two-task down CTAs pipeline their rounds through LDS; their shared-expert down rows are offloaded to the next one-task CTAs.
3. **FFN seam and attention hand-offs**: a shorter seam -> norm -> router chain, whole-sector attention partials, per-tile `wo_a` ready flags.

Each commit builds and is bit-exact on its own. Related: #61482 (moves these kernels to `vllm/models/common/amd/mono/`).

**Rebased** onto main 8977b13a1c, which includes #63576 (K2's combine awaits `krdy` before reading `klen` in index-source launches) and #63689 (vLLM's scale code for zero and subnormal MXFP8 groups). Both fixes apply to the tuned builds as well: the tuned paths share `stage_combine` and its `krdy` wait, and quantize with the same `vllm_mx_code` / `mx_code`. No conflicts; the diff is unchanged.

**Result vs main:** ratio-2 layer K1+K2 8.6-18.1% faster (M = 1..48), index-source launches included; E2E TPOT p50 −3.3% (c32) and −3.7% (c4).

## Validation

8x MI355X, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-5d35ce39` (AITER 0.1.26, FlyDSL 0.4.0; no kernel or build changes between it and the base commit); only the Python tree differs between arms.

**Repo tests**

```bash
pytest -v tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py \
  tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py
```

| GPUs | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | 80 passed, 2 skipped (gfx942 only) | 80 passed, 2 skipped (gfx942 only) |
| 2 | 78 passed, 4 skipped (2 need 4 GPUs) | 78 passed, 4 skipped (2 need 4 GPUs) |

The numerics test also checks the tuned layer bit for bit against a `generic=True` runner at 12/36/48 rows.

**Correctness vs main**: 115/115 cases bit-identical at TP2 (92 on tuned builds; all K1+K2 outputs and the SWA cache, hashed per rank, index-source and no-fold launches included). The MLIR of every non-tuned build is byte-identical to main's (168/168 gfx950, 76/76 gfx942).

**Layer microbench** (TP2, ratio 2, K1+K2 µs per layer, cold L2, max over ranks, median of 11 fresh runs on 3 GPU pairs):

| M | 1 | 6 | 12 | 18 | 24 | 36 | 48 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 89.1 | 134.4 | 194.1 | 238.2 | 292.8 | 402.1 | 472.2 |
| this PR | 73.0 | 118.6 | 173.0 | 208.3 | 259.1 | 360.2 | 431.8 |
| change | −18.1% | −11.7% | −10.9% | −12.6% | −11.5% | −10.4% | −8.6% |

Weighted by the widths served at c32 / c4: −10.7% / −11.6%. Index-source launches (the ratio-2 layers that feed the indexer, which now wait on `krdy`): −8.9% to −17.3%, weighted −10.9% / −11.4% (7 runs); the `krdy` wait itself costs < 0.6% on main and on this PR.

**E2E** (TP2 + MTP, agentic-coding trace, 1 h per run, CI server arguments; main and this PR on two lanes at once, swapped in a second wave; mean of the two waves vs main; measured before the rebase, same kernel code):

| vs main | c32 | c4 |
|---|---|---|
| TPOT p50 | **−3.31%** | **−3.74%** |
| TPOT p90 | −1.22% | −6.84% |
| interactivity p50 | +3.49% | +3.78% |
| interactivity p90 | +1.16% | +7.59% |
| output tok/s/GPU | +0.53% | −0.66% |
| per-request ITL ratio | 0.973 / 0.976 | 0.970 / 0.960 |

MTP acceptance length 3.51 in every run; TTFT within run-to-run noise.

## Details

**Where it applies**: gfx950, TP 2, compress ratio 2, the target's routing (384 experts, top-6) and SWA window. The gate is static per build; no new flag or env var.

**Tradeoff**: tuned builds lay out their scratch differently, so the runner keys scratch by (width, tuned): up to ~20 MB per tuned width per rank. Peer memory is unchanged.

**Not covered**: gfx942 and DSpark draft builds were not run on GPU (MLIR identical to main's); TP4 is not tuned.

commits.pr_title: [MM] Support mm_device_do_normalize for Gemma 4
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Closes #65573. Adds `mm_device_do_normalize` support to Gemma 4, following #64487 (Gemma 3). No other PR covers it.

Gemma 4's processor only rescales by 1/255, so with the flag on it sends raw `uint8` patches and the model rescales them on the device. That's 4× fewer pixel bytes than `float32`: 7.7 MB → 1.9 MB for a 280-token image.

## Changes

- `gemma4_mm.py`: set the flag, build the input norm, and apply it in one helper before `patch_embedder` for images, video and the encoder CUDA graph. Patches are channel-last, so it normalizes them as `(pixels, 3)` into the model dtype. Capture buffers are `uint8` with the flag on.
- `test_video_cache_is_independent_of_image_kwargs` pins the flag off. Its per-request `rescale_factor` does nothing once the processor stops rescaling, as with the other models that support the flag.
- `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration` (encoder-free, its own image path) opts out with `supports_mm_device_do_normalize = False`; supporting it can follow.
- PPL test entry for Gemma 4 E2B, as requested.
- Docs table entry.

## Validation

- New `test_mm_device_do_normalize`: raw `uint8` image and video pixels, normalized on device, equal the CPU path. It fails without this change.
- New `test_embed_patches_normalizes_channel_last_patches`: different per-channel mean/std land on the right pixels.
- CPU with dummy weights on a shrunk model: flag on vs off gives bit-identical logprobs for one image, two images and a video.
- PPL test (`generation_ppl_test/gemma.py`, Gemma 4 E2B added next to Gemma 3; `hf_ppl` 71.009 measured with Transformers on an L40), RTX A6000, bf16, at 171213e: flag off and on both give 70.973 (−0.05%); with `cudagraph_mm_encoder` 70.918 (−0.13%) off and 70.757 (−0.36%) on. 4 passed.
- `test_gemma4.py`: 43 passed. `test_common.py -k gemma-4-E2B`: 3 passed. pre-commit passed.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][EC Connector] Make control-plane ZMQ heartbeats take effect
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The EC CPU connector's consumer sets ZMTP heartbeats on its DEALER only after `make_zmq_socket` has connected it, so libzmq never runs them. A producer that freezes or becomes unreachable is therefore never reported to `_on_peer_down`. This PR sets the options before the socket connects.

## Claims

- A producer that stops responding without closing TCP (frozen, host down, network partition) is reported within `HEARTBEAT_IVL + HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT` = 6 s. On main it is never reported.
- A killed producer was already reported, because TCP closes. A busy producer is not reported.
- No new option, and `make_zmq_socket` is unchanged.

## Validation

**New test** `test_control.py::test_zmq_client_transport_reports_frozen_peer`: a subprocess runs a ZMQ ROUTER that takes one request and never replies. The test connects through `ZmqClientTransport`, sends a request, `SIGSTOP`s the subprocess, and waits 5 s for `poll_dead()`. Heartbeats are patched to 100 ms / 500 ms.

```
pytest tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_control.py -k frozen
main:     FAILED  AssertionError: frozen producer never reported
this PR:  1 passed in 0.8 s (5/5 runs)
```

**Real constants** (2 s / 4 s), same setup:

| Producer | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `SIGSTOP` | no event in 11 s | reported after 6.00 s |
| Pure-Python loop holding the GIL for 12 s | no event | no event |

**EC unit tests** in a Linux CPU container: `pytest tests/v1/ec_connector/unit` gives 406 passed on main and 407 passed with this PR, with 36 skipped on both. The extra pass is the new test. Two `test_ec_transfer_params.py` cases time out on both because the container cannot reach the Hugging Face Hub. With Hub access they pass on both. `pre-commit` passes.

The new test is marked `cpu_test`, so the CPU "V1 Others" step runs it. The rest of `test_control.py` runs only in the V1 KV Connectors step, which is disabled.

## Details

**Root cause:** `ZmqClientTransport.connect()` calls `make_zmq_socket(..., bind=False)`, which connects, and only then sets `HEARTBEAT_IVL`, `HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT` and `HEARTBEAT_TTL`. libzmq copies socket options into a connection when it is created, and most options affect only later `bind()`/`connect()` calls (see `zmq_setsockopt`). The connection therefore runs without heartbeats, and the `EVENT_DISCONNECTED` monitor fires only when TCP closes.

**Fix:** set the three options as defaults on the transport's own `zmq.Context`. pyzmq applies context defaults when `make_zmq_socket` creates the socket, before it connects. This keeps `make_zmq_socket`'s other DEALER settings and leaves its signature alone. #65575 fixes the same pitfall for the Mooncake KV connector by adding heartbeat arguments to `make_zmq_socket`.

No open PR touches `ec_connector/cpu/control/zmq.py`. I searched open PRs for EC connector, heartbeat, and `ec_connector/cpu`.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Keep lazy SimpleCPUOffload stores at the GPU eviction end
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Lazy SimpleCPUOffload should offload the blocks the allocator will evict next, but two behaviors move it away from them. This PR fixes both: stored blocks go back to the front of the GPU free queue, and every walk starts from the head of the queue instead of a saved cursor.

Includes the two commits of #59383 by @obendidi, rebased onto main with authorship kept, plus the walk change. Builds on #64229.

## Claims

- Lazy stores return GPU blocks to the eviction end (from #59383).
- The lazy walk starts at the head of the free queue on every step, so it no longer offloads blocks far from eviction.
- With sliding-window groups that are not prefix-cacheable (DeepSeek-V4.1) and a contended CPU tier, the walk change is what lowers recomputed blocks; #59383 alone does not help there. The simulation below went from 67.5% to 59.7% recomputed blocks with 32 such blocks per cached block.
- No change to eager mode. Net -3 lines outside tests (+17/-20).

## Validation

Tests, on CPU:

```bash
pytest tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_kv_events.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_metrics.py
```

Result: 152 passed. `pre-commit` passes on the changed files.

`test_lazy_walk_does_not_offload_past_eviction_window` fails before the walk change: the second walk offloads the blocks past `target_free`. `test_lazy_store_returns_blocks_to_eviction_end` comes from #59383.

Simulation: the real `SimpleCPUOffloadScheduler` and `BlockPool` replaying one multi-turn session trace per row, with only the requests and store completions simulated. Each cell is the share of prompt blocks recomputed, averaged over 2 seeds (lower is better). The CPU tier is 2x the GPU pool and the working set is about 2.7x the CPU tier. SWA blocks are taken from the same free queue and freed on the next step. The 32 row uses twice the pool and half the per-step budget of the others, so that the SWA blocks fit, and runs long enough to reach steady state.

| Uncached SWA blocks per cached block | main | #59383 only | walk from head only | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 74.8% | 55.8% | 74.5% | 55.7% |
| 8 | 64.7% | 66.5% | 60.0% | 57.6% |
| 32 | 67.5% | 70.5% | 62.6% | 59.7% |

Per request, #59383 alone also writes 1.8x (8 SWA) to 2.1x (32 SWA) as many blocks to the CPU tier as this PR. When the CPU tier holds the whole working set (8 SWA), all four variants recompute 4.0%.

Not validated:

- No E2E serving run was done for this PR, so these are block-level hit rates and not a throughput measurement. The pool sizes and session shape are assumptions.
- `tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_integration.py` has no passing result: its 2 non-optional tests need a GPU. They failed at engine startup on a GPU without enough free memory, and also fail without a GPU, as `test_chunked_local_partial_gpu_hit` does on main. They need a run in CI or on a free GPU.

## Details

Root cause: the cursor is only reset when its block leaves the free queue. Uncached SWA blocks are freed to the front of the queue and reused there, so the block under the cursor is often neither stored nor reallocated, and the walk resumes past it. In the simulation with SWA groups, about 99% of walks with only #59383 applied resumed from the cursor, against 72% without SWA. The walk then misses the blocks #59383 returned to the front and keeps offloading fresher blocks, which turns over the CPU tier.

Why not just #59383: it is sufficient without such groups (first row), but on DeepSeek-V4.1-style configurations it needs the walk change. The two are combined here so they can be reviewed and merged together. If #59383 merges first, this PR reduces to the walk commit.

Tradeoffs: a walk now revisits blocks already on CPU near the head, but it is still bounded by `target_free`, the same bound as before. One simulated case favors #59383 alone: without SWA groups and with an 8-step store latency, it recomputes 67.2% against 70.8% here. With 8 SWA blocks and the same latency, this PR is better (65.6% against 58.7%).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Declare 64-token kernel blocks for SM120 sparse backends
commits.pr_body:
### Summary
On SM120, the DSV41 sparse-MLA backends declare only `[128]`-token kernel blocks (`get_supported_kernel_block_sizes` returns `[64 if family(90) else 128]` / `[128]`), so serving with `--block-size 64` dies in block-size negotiation:

```
ValueError: No common block size for 64 (FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41: [128]; DEEPSEEK_V41_INDEXER: [128])
```

This declares `[64]` on SM12x for the two sites (indexer backend, sparse MLA backend, FlashInfer sparse backend), mirroring the existing SM90 branch. The SWA/backend selection is untouched.

The approach is @aagallo's (described in #59203); this PR adds the validated matrix below.

### Matrix validation (8x RTX PRO 6000, SM120, TP8)
Stack: vLLM `0.31.1rc1.dev158+gab905a885` + FlashInfer `0.7.1rc5`, `--block-size 64 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}'`, DeepGEMM switched between PR14 head (`40592bd`) and the current pin (`1e1842a`):

| vLLM tree | DeepGEMM | result |
|---|---|---|
| stock | `1e1842a` | fails negotiation (error above) |
| this PR (uniform `[64]`) | `40592bd` | serves, 17x19=323 |
| this PR (uniform `[64]`) | `1e1842a` | serves, 17x19=323 |
| per-layer variant (`[64,128]` + `64*max(1,cr)` specs) | `40592bd` | serves, 17x19=323 |
| per-layer variant | `1e1842a` | serves, 17x19=323 |

All four patched cells boot in ~90-160 s and answer correctly; zero failures. An earlier `attention.hpp:484` observed with uniform-64 on an older stack (0.30.1rc1.dev738 + FlashInfer main @c11f8ba + DeepGEMM 6901431) does not reproduce on current main with either DeepGEMM build — details in #59203.

Pairs naturally with #57292 (fail-fast when FlashInfer lacks runtime page sizes).

Addresses the SM120 serving failure in #59203.

### Test Plan
- [x] 5-cell matrix above (serve + correctness per cell)
- [x] pre-commit / CI

---

## Requirements & validation (added after review)

**FlashInfer requirement: `flashinfer-python >= 0.7.1rc5` (runtime page sizes).** Measured end to end on 8x RTX PRO 6000 (SM120):
- pinned `0.7.0.post1` + this PR: does **not** serve — fails in ~110 s with `page_block_size=32 is unsupported; decode kernels are instantiated only for page_block_size=64` (64-token kernel blocks give ratio-2 layers 32-token compressed pages; the pin has no runtime page sizes). Stock fails on the pin as well.
- `0.7.1rc5` + this PR: serves at default and `--block-size 64`; `--block-size 128` does not serve on this stack in either declaration form (see matrix below), so the PR buys default-64 — the only geometry that serves on the default BLHNC layout.

Landing order per review discussion: after the FlashInfer bump (#60948), or together with the #57292 guard.

**Matrix (stock / A=[64] / C=[64,128] x default / 64 / 128, GSM8K n=100):** stock fails both ways (assertions upthread); A and C serve at default and 64 (GSM8K 89-91%, no variant-dependent degradation); 128 fails under both declarations (A: BLHNC layout guard; C: FlashInfer `block_kv == 32 or block_kv == 64`). Decode throughput of the four servable configs is within <1% at c1/c4.

**No unit test, by review:** an earlier revision added `tests/v1/attention/test_dsv41_indexer_block_sizes.py`, but it pinned kernel-support values that will drift (and the block size is asserted in C++ at kernel launch, so a black-box version would need a real kernel anyway). Per review it was removed and each SM12x `[64]` now carries a short inline comment naming the failure it avoids (#59203).

**Revalidation on the final form** — 8x RTX PRO 6000 96 GB (SM120), vLLM 0.33.0 with these two declarations, fp8 KV, no explicit `--block-size`: negotiation reports `Setting kv cache block size to 64 for FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41/DEEPSEEK_SPARSE_SWA/DEEPSEEK_V41_INDEXER/CompressorBackend`; READY in ~7.5 min (cold JIT); KV cache 2,397,337 tokens at 32,768 max-model-len; 4/4 short-answer probes correct and greedy output byte-identical across 3 runs.

Coordinated with #56509 (same failure, overlapping declarations).

commits.pr_title: [Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] DeepGEMM FP8 MegaMoE with fused shared experts
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Run GLM-5.3-Flash's MoE layers with DeepGEMM's FP8xFP8 MegaMoE (routed and shared experts in one kernel that also dispatches and combines across the EP group), using the official FP8 checkpoint. Enabled by `--kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}'` with `--tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size N --enable-expert-parallel`.

Related: #55275 (BF16 / MXFP4 MegaMoE for GLM, open), #54049 (FlashInfer NVFP4 mega kernel).

## Claims

- On the AgentX replay at concurrency 96, DEP4 with MegaMoE gives 1.6x the output throughput of DEP4 on the generic MoE path.
- Against TP4 it is about level on throughput (+6%, one run each) and has about a fifth of the TTFT.
- It prefills 1.8x faster than DEP4 generic and 2.5x faster than TP4.
- AIME 2026 Pass@1 matches the generic MoE path (0.934 vs 0.939 with a 131K output cap) and is 0.977 with the 1M context.
- A weight reload, in layerwise or direct mode, restores byte-identical weights at the same addresses.
- No change for any other `moe_backend`.

## Validation

4x B200, nightly `8cbd5d03` with this change applied, MTP 5 with acceptance fixed by `synthetic_acceptance_length` 3.61. The three arms ran on the same node and in the same container, one run each; they differ only in parallel layout and `moe_backend`.

AgentX replay (InferenceX-pinned aiperf, `semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126`), concurrency 96, 1 hour:

| metric | TP4 | DEP4, generic MoE | DEP4, MegaMoE |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| output tok/s | 3,152 | 2,063 | **3,332** |
| input tok/s | 380,126 | 234,727 | **399,297** |
| total tok/s | 383,278 | 236,790 | **402,628** |
| requests completed (errors) | 11,372 (4) | 8,143 (1) | 11,986 (5) |
| TTFT avg / p50 / p99 | 3.93 / 2.19 / 23.8 s | 2.36 / 1.47 / 17.3 s | **0.81 / 0.49 / 5.99 s** |
| ITL avg | 18.3 ms | 45.6 ms | 19.5 ms |
| output tok/s per user | 64.0 | 26.2 | 64.1 |
| prefix cache hit | 93.9% | 92.4% | 94.0% |
| of which GPU / host reload | 6.2% / 87.7% | 50.9% / 41.5% | 71.2% / 22.8% |
| preemptions | 35 | 53 | 2 |

`vllm bench serve`, random prompts, concurrency 128, on the same servers:

| workload (in/out) | metric | TP4 | DEP4, generic MoE | DEP4, MegaMoE |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 8192 / 1 | total tok/s | 46,334 | 63,900 | **115,081** |
| | mean TTFT | 20.8 s | 15.2 s | 8.4 s |
| 1024 / 1024 | output tok/s | 7,895 | 8,478 | **11,691** |
| | mean TTFT | 4.31 s | 1.86 s | 0.85 s |

Accuracy:

| eval | TP4 | DEP4, generic MoE | DEP4, MegaMoE |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GSM8K, lm-eval 5-shot, 1,319 questions | 0.9757 ± 0.0042 | – | 0.9735 ± 0.0044 |
| AIME 2026 Pass@1, 30 problems x 32 samples | – | 0.939 ± 0.006 | 0.934 ± 0.006 |

GSM8K ran on nightly `43b4aaea` (TP4) and the servers above (MegaMoE). AIME ran on nightly `df3bd094` with this branch, both arms in the same container (MTP 3, fp8 KV, 131K output cap) with DeepInfer's `eval/aime` prompt and rule-based judge, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95; the generic arm runs `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` on the checkpoint's own scales. With the full 1M context MegaMoE reaches **0.977 ± 0.005**; the remaining loss is mostly problem 15 (0.72), where 12 of 32 samples never stop and loop until the context is full.

Weight reload, 4x B200, nightly `e0d00e4b8e` with this branch, DEP4, MTP 3. The experts are zeroed before each reload, which breaks every greedy output; all results are compared with the cold start:

| metric | layerwise | direct |
|---|---:|---:|
| target reload time | 41.6 s | 37.3 s |
| parameters and buffers differing (5,900 across ranks) | 0 | 0 |
| parameters and buffers moved | 0 | 0 |
| greedy outputs matching (4 short prompts) | 4/4 | 4/4 |

The same holds for a second reload, a reload of the MTP drafter, and an update that sends expert weights and block scales in separate `load_weights` calls. Long prompts (about 14K tokens) already vary between identical runs without a reload, on both MoE backends, so they are not compared. No real NCCL or IPC trainer was run.

Unit tests: `pytest tests/models/glm5next/test_mega_moe.py`, 5 passed.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 PYTHONHASHSEED=42 vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --max-num-seqs 96 \
  --language-model-only --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5,"rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.61}' \
  --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":true,"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_capture_sizes":[6,12,18,24,30,36,48,60,72,96,120,144,192,240,288,384,480,576,768,1020,1536,2046,3072,4092,6144,8190]}' \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 8190 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.97 \
  --prefix-match-unit 16 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":300000000000,"enable_cross_layers_blocks":"true","lazy_offload":false}}'

vllm-router --port 8000 --worker-urls http://127.0.0.1:8001 --intra-node-data-parallel-size 4 --policy consistent_hash

aiperf profile --scenario agentx --url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --model zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --concurrency 96 --benchmark-duration 3600 \
  --public-dataset semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126
```

AIME 2026:

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --language-model-only --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --reasoning-parser glm47 \
  --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}' \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92
```

The client sends DeepInfer's `eval/aime` prompts (`build_records`) to `/v1/chat/completions` with `temperature=1.0, top_p=0.95`, 32 samples per problem, and scores `reasoning + "</think>" + content` with its `score_rollout`. Samples were drawn with a 131K output cap first; the 82 that hit it were continued from their own text to the 1M context, which samples the same distribution as the larger cap.

The baselines drop `moe_backend` (DEP4, generic) or use `--tensor-parallel-size 4` alone with `--intra-node-data-parallel-size 1` on the router (TP4). The generic path picked `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` for the FP8 experts. The random-prompt rows were measured on the same servers before the replay with `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --max-concurrency 128`.
</details>

## Details

- The checkpoint's experts are block FP8 (E4M3, one float32 scale per 128x128 block). DeepGEMM's SM100 MegaMoE feeds scales to the block-scaled MMA and needs UE8M0 scales per row and 32 columns, so the routed and shared expert weights are requantized once at load (`requant_block_fp8_to_ue8m0`).
- This requantization is lossy: about 2.4% relative L2 per weight tensor and about 3.9% on one MoE layer's output (layer 15, real weights, random inputs). The generic TRTLLM path uses the checkpoint's scales as they are. The GSM8K gap above is within one standard error.
- Routing stays outside the kernel: `fused_topk_bias` (sigmoid, score correction bias), with `routed_scaling_factor` folded into the top-k weights. DeepGEMM's Mega Gate only supports `sqrtsoftplus`.
- `Glm5NextMegaMoEExperts` subclasses `DeepGemmMegaMoEExperts`, which is unchanged, with the `MEGA_MOE_MXFP8` format. E4M3 shards load straight into the kernel layout; their float32 block scales are staged in `*_weight_scale_inv`, and the model's `process_weights_after_loading` calls `requantize_block_fp8()`, which rounds every newly loaded shard to UE8M0 1x32 scales in place (main model, multimodal wrapper and MTP drafter).
- A weight update may send an expert weight and its block scale in separate `load_weights` calls; by the end of the load both must be in, or `requantize_block_fp8()` raises.
- Reload and weight transfer finish with that hook (#64357, and direct mode from #64336), so the kernel tensors keep their storage. The derived UE8M0 scales are marked `weight_loader_numel = 0`, so a layerwise reload replays a layer as soon as its checkpoint tensors are in.
- The block-FP8 shared expert is fused the same way: the experts own its weights and the model builds no shared MLP.
- `--prefix-match-unit` matters for this model independently of this PR: the KDA state page makes the KV block 8,960 tokens under DEP4, and without the flag prefix hits land on whole blocks.
- Limitations: `tensor_parallel_size=1` only; SM100 only; no sharded RDT or sparse NCCL updates. Under DEP4 each rank holds 8.8M KV tokens.

---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Attention] Keep FlashInfer TRTLLM prefill query offsets in a persistent buffer
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix an illegal memory access / segfault during CUDA graph replay of the standalone draft-model prefill on Blackwell (SM100), reported in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60989#issuecomment-6620438731.

Since #60989, the standalone draft model (`method: "draft_model"`) captures FULL CUDA graphs for its prefill. That prefill is a uniform batch of `num_speculative_tokens + 2` tokens per request, because it adds a correction token. That is one token more than FlashInfer's `reorder_batch_threshold` (`1 + num_speculative_tokens`). The builder therefore classifies every request as a prefill and, on SM100, takes the TRTLLM prefill path.

On that path, `build()` allocated `cum_seq_lens_q` as a new tensor (`qo_indptr[prefill_start:] - qo_indptr[prefill_start]`). Attention metadata is built outside the graph, so a FULL graph keeps the address that tensor had at capture time. The tensor is freed after capture and its memory is reused. At replay, the attention kernel reads query offsets from that reused memory. The result is wrong drafts or, for large batches, `CUDA error: an illegal memory access` or a segfault in `cuGraphLaunch`.

This PR writes the offsets into a persistent buffer owned by the builder, the same way `paged_kv_indptr` already works, so every build updates the memory the graph reads. The other tensors on this path (`seq_lens`, `block_tables`, `cum_seq_lens_kv`) are already views of persistent buffers.

Not covered here: with an FP8 KV cache and a non-FP8 query, the same path also makes a contiguous copy of `block_tables` on each build, which would have the same problem under a FULL graph. That configuration was not tested, so this PR leaves it alone.

## Test Plan

- New unit test `tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_trtllm_prefill_cudagraph.py`. It builds TRTLLM prefill metadata twice, for uniform batches wider than the reorder threshold, and checks that `cum_seq_lens_q` holds the right offsets and stays at the same address.
- End to end on 1x GB200 with model runner V2:

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
  --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "draft_model", "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}'

python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-questions 1319 \
  --max-concurrency 256 --max-tokens 256 --temperature 0 --seed 0
# and again with --max-concurrency 32
```

## Test Result

- Unit test: passes with this PR. On main it fails with `cum_seq_lens_q moved between builds`.
- GSM8K end to end (1319 questions, greedy decoding; target Qwen/Qwen3-8B, draft Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B, K=3):

| Setup | C256 | C32 | Mean accepted tokens per draft |
|---|---|---|---|
| Uniform decode graphs up to 256 requests (as in #63406), without this fix | crash (illegal memory access) | n/a | n/a |
| Same, with this fix | 0.886 | 0.886 | 2.44 |
| `cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE`, attention runs eagerly (reference) | 0.886 | 0.886 | 2.44 |
| main, with this fix | 0.886 | 0.886 | 2.44 |

On main without this fix, the crash is intermittent: graphs there stop at about 200 requests, so a crash depends on what the freed memory holds. With the fix, accuracy and acceptance match the PIECEWISE reference, which shows the replayed draft prefill now reads the correct query offsets.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Let ci-selector decide csrc/ changes on CUDA
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Any change under `csrc/` (except `csrc/cpu/` and `csrc/rocm/`) matches `run_all_patterns`, so the pipeline runs every step and ci-selector never sees it. That was ~12% of PR NVIDIA GPU time in the week after the selector rollout.

ci-selector can now decide these on CUDA: each full CI run records which kernels every job launches, and the image build's kernel source map ties each kernel back to its `csrc/` file (headers and `torch_bindings.cpp` / `ops.h` narrow by op name since ci-infra#823). A replay of the 25 builds that ran everything because of `csrc/` between Oct 17 and Oct 22:

| | run all | ci-selector (with ci-infra#823) |
|---|---|---|
| estimated NVIDIA GPU-hours | 1,322 | 804 (−39%) |

None of the failures in those 25 builds was on a step the selector would have skipped (four flagged: a known `model-executor` flake, a network-unreachable error, a test-asset server 500, and a DeepEP SIGSEGV that also failed on unrelated main builds). Kernels with no recording yet and host-only dispatch files with no kernels fail open to a broad selection.

This moves `csrc/` from `run_all_patterns` to `amd_run_all_patterns`:

- **CUDA**: ci-selector decides `csrc/` changes.
- **AMD**: unchanged. AMD is not selected by ci-selector yet, so a `csrc/` change still runs every non-optional AMD step (ROCm compiles these sources through HIPify). `csrc/cpu/` and `csrc/rocm/` stay excluded, as today.
- `cmake/` and `CMakeLists.txt` still run everything; the selector cannot narrow them yet.

**Merge after vllm-project/ci-infra#892**, which adds `amd_run_all_patterns` to the generator. Without it the new key is ignored and AMD would also stop running everything on `csrc/`. vllm-project/ci-infra#891 (a selector run-all decline runs every step instead of the old rules) is related but independent.

## Test Plan

ci-infra#892's generator functions on this config:

| change | run all | AMD run all | AMD steps that run |
|---|---|---|---|
| `csrc/attention/attention_kernels.cu` | no (was yes) | yes | 169 / 169 non-optional |
| `csrc/rocm/attention.cu` | no | no | 19 (unchanged) |
| `csrc/cpu/foo.cpp` | no | no | 13 (unchanged) |
| `cmake/utils.cmake` | yes | – | all (unchanged) |

commits.pr_title: [CI][DSv4.1] Give the MXFP8 linear test stub a params_dtype
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix `:nvidia: (4xB200) DeepSeek-V4.1 NVIDIA Kernels` (nightly). It has failed 12 times in a row since #64111 merged ([latest: 99485](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/99485#01a1a039-4070-49ba-bf82-733112dd7dba)):

```
FAILED models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_kernels.py::test_engram_wkv_prefetch_matches_inline[False]
FAILED models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_kernels.py::test_engram_wkv_prefetch_matches_inline[True]
AttributeError: '_Mxfp8Linear' object has no attribute 'params_dtype'
```

**Root cause:** #64111 changed `FlashInferCutedslMxfp8LinearKernel.apply_weights` (`vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/mxfp8/flashinfer.py`) to take the output dtype of unquantized inputs from `layer.params_dtype` instead of `x.dtype`. Real vLLM linear layers always set `params_dtype`, but the hand-built `_Mxfp8Linear` stand-in in this test did not.

**Why #64111's CI didn't catch it:** the step is `optional: true` (nightly only), so it never runs on PRs, and its source triggers don't include `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/mxfp8/`.

**Fix:** set `params_dtype = torch.bfloat16` on the stand-in, as a real linear layer would. The test feeds bf16 inputs, so the kernel's output dtype is the same as before #64111.

**Not a duplicate:** no open PR touches this test or stub.

## Test Plan

Not run locally (needs B200 GPUs). The step is nightly-only, so it will be confirmed by the next nightly after merge, or by a selected-step run of `dsv41-nvidia-kernels-4xb200` on this PR.

## Notes

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][UMBP] Copy every KV cache layout's per-head runs
commits.pr_body:
- Split each layer's page into per-head runs in `data.py`, using the allocator's `compute_layout_strides`.
- Register the same runs in the `embedded.py` bulk path, falling back to per-range copies for a group whose stride doesn't match.
- Fail at startup instead of corrupting KV when a page is split and `kv_cache_layout` is unset.
- Round-trip all 6 layouts through the bulk and range paths in `test_umbp_embedded.py`.

UMBP took `cache.stride(0)` as the block stride and copied one contiguous page per layer, both on the range path in `data.py` and on the bulk path in `_register_load_layouts`, as noted in the review of #61794. Under LHBNC, the default with `ROCM_AITER_FA` and `VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1`, K and V are head planes spanning every block, so the engine fails at init with `KV region bytes (65536) exceed its stride (32768)`, and under BHLNC heads of different layers interleave inside a block row, so UMBP silently restores the wrong KV. `pytest -q v1/kv_connector/unit/test_umbp_embedded.py -k every_kv_cache_layout` gives 4 failures without the fix and 12 passed with it. On MI350X with Qwen3-0.6B, 16 greedy tokens after a 192-token UMBP hit now match recompute under BHLNC (`TRITON_ATTN` with `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BHLNC`) and under AITER shuffle-KV, and stay identical under the default layouts; the batch-invariant tests in `test_mori_token_e2e.py` likewise fail without the fix and pass with it under `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BHLNC` and `LHBNC`. Batch invariance rules out `ROCM_AITER_FA`, so those tests run on `TRITON_ATTN`, and AITER shuffle-KV is covered only by the greedy check above. Other layouts and MLA keep the single-span copy, and refusing LHBNC and BHLNC instead would make UMBP unusable with AITER shuffle-KV, since forcing LBHNC trips the shuffle decode path. LHBNC and BHLNC now issue one bulk range per head instead of one per layer, which I haven't benchmarked yet, and no open PR touches UMBP layout handling.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Shard Multimodal Models (Extended Generation 1) automatically, with spawned engines
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Enrolls Multimodal Models (Extended Generation 1) and its AMD mirror in `automatic_shard`, and sets `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn` on the step.

Without spawn, sharding this step fails. In #65211's first build ([99300](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/99300)), the only sharded run of this step without spawn, one of four shards ran `test_pixtral.py::test_chat_consolidated` and its engine core died with `CUDA error: initialization error` while starting. vLLM forks the engine unless `torch.cuda.is_initialized()` says CUDA is already up (`_maybe_force_spawn` in `vllm/utils/system_utils.py`). On main the step runs as one job, and an engine start early in the run (Granite Speech) finds CUDA up and switches the whole pytest process to spawn, so later engines never fork. That shard had no such test: after one engine test, only CPU unit tests ran (Moondream3 MoE, which sets up vLLM's distributed state, Nemotron Parse MTP, Pixtral's own unit tests) before Pixtral forked its engine. One of them sets up CUDA in a way torch doesn't report. Setting spawn on the step makes every engine start the way the later ones already do on main, in any shard order.

## Claims

| Job | Plan |
|---|---|
| `multi-modal-models-extended-generation-1` | 5 shards |
| its AMD mirror | 4 shards |

- Each shard stays under the 20-minute target; the planned extra machine time is the repeated job setup (a few percent).
- The step passes on recent nightlies as one job.

## Validation

- The sharding harness (each shard's commands run against a mock test tree, as a PR build and as main with the OTel wrapper) shows every test runs exactly once, base and mirror.
- The generated pipeline carries `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn` on both the NVIDIA step and the AMD mirror.
- `split_check.py` finds no step whose jobs each run the whole suite.
- On the head rebased onto current main, PR build [100034](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/100034) ran the step as 5 shards and scoped build [100043](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/100043) ran the AMD mirror as 4 shards; all passed, with no automatic retries, each shard well under the 20-minute target. Each command's passed and skipped counts match main's latest nightly on both platforms. (Earlier builds 99363 and 99365 ran the previous 4 + 3 plan; it grew with main's timings.)
- Machine time is within noise of main's one-job nightly: above it in 100034 and below it in 100043, and the earlier builds swung the same way, so it depends more on the hosts the shards land on than on sharding. The extra per shard is the repeated job setup, plus spawn starting each engine in a fresh interpreter.

## Details

- **Why spawn on the step, not a test fix.** Which earlier test sets up CUDA unseen isn't pinned down, and any future test could do the same. Spawn is what most of this step already runs under on main.
- **Timeouts unchanged.** `timeout_in_minutes` stays per job.

commits.pr_title: [XPU][Perf] Reuse GDN metadata across KV cache groups on XPU
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Let XPU use the existing Model Runner V2 path that reuses GDN attention metadata across KV cache groups (#58762). Both the reuse path and the aligned state index precompute it depends on in mamba `align` mode were limited to CUDA; this PR allows XPU in both checks.

## Claims

- On XPU, hybrid GDN models (Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.6 family) build GDN metadata once per KV cache spec per step and re-gather state indices for the other groups via `update_block_table()`, as on CUDA. With 3 GDN KV cache groups, 2 of 3 metadata builds per step are replaced.
- Outputs are unchanged.

## Validation

Intel Arc Pro B70, MTP with `num_speculative_tokens=3`, eager mode, prefix caching on (mamba `align` mode), greedy decoding with `logprobs=1`. GDN metadata calls were counted inside the workers; baseline is unmodified main.

| Model | Config | GDN `build()` calls (baseline → this PR) | `update_block_table()` calls | Outputs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B | TP=1, bf16, B1+B8 | 819 → 273 | 0 → 546 | tokens and logprobs identical across 5 processes |
| Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 | TP=2, B1+B8, per worker | 2133 → 711 | 0 → 1422 | tokens identical across 4 processes; B8 logprobs identical; B1 max logprob difference 0.093, baseline-vs-baseline 0.075 |

Throughput on Qwen3.5-0.8B (128 input / 64 output tokens, median of 5 runs per process, A-B-B-A process order):

| Batch | Baseline (A1 / A2) | This PR (B1 / B2) | Paired change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 183.5 / 181.1 tok/s | 189.4 / 192.1 tok/s | +3.2% / +6.1% |
| 8 | 1329.9 / 1342.0 tok/s | 1404.9 / 1399.1 tok/s | +5.7% / +4.3% |

Run-to-run variation within a process was up to 5%. On Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 the throughput difference was within run-to-run noise.

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_utils.py
# 70 passed, 36 skipped (existing CUDA-only cases)
```

Changed-file pre-commit (including mypy) passed.

## Details

`GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder.supports_update_block_table` required `device.type == "cuda"`. In mamba `align` mode, `update_block_table()` reads the indices produced by `MambaSpecDecodeGPUContext.compute_aligned_state_indices()`, which asserted `seq_lens.is_cuda`. Qwen3.5 uses `align` mode by default when prefix caching is enabled, so allowing XPU only in the first check fails at that assert. The precompute is a Triton kernel and runs unchanged on XPU; identical outputs above confirm the indices match the per-group build.

No new test is added: the existing builder tests that cover `update_block_table()` are device-independent and pass, and there is no existing unit test for the precompute numerics; the change only widens two device checks, and the end-to-end comparison above exercises both on XPU.

#58851 moves this sharing into the builder and drops the CUDA check for sharing itself, but keeps the aligned-index precompute CUDA-only. This PR is independent of it; the `compute_aligned_state_indices()` change is still needed for XPU in `align` mode either way.

Limitations: XPU only (no CUDA behavior change), eager mode only; graph mode was not exercised.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Test] Rotate KV into RHT domain in the INT4 unified attn test
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix the INT4 case of `test_triton_unified_attention_per_token_head_scale`. It filled the INT4 cache with unrotated K/V and compared the result against a reference that didn't match what `unified_attention_int4` computes. The test now writes the cache in the RHT domain, like `reshape_and_cache_int4`, so it actually checks the INT4 attention kernel.

Follow-up to #40835. Removes the Intel CI deselect of `[int4-16-128-num_heads0-seq_lens1]`. Downstream report: intel/intel-xpu-backend-for-triton#8358.

**Not a duplicate:** no open PR or issue fixes this test. #62113 edits the same test but keeps the INT4 reference as is and widens the Intel deselect to two INT4 cases. See Details for how the two PRs combine.

## Claims

- The kernel output and the reference now agree (correlation 1.0000 vs ≈ 0.00 before). The test no longer passes or fails depending on the RNG stream.
- INT4 uses the same `atol=rtol=5e-2` as INT8/FP8, down from 0.5. This also removes the Hopper-only `atol=1.1`.
- The Intel CI deselect for this case is removed.
- Test-only change. No kernel or runtime code is modified.

## Validation

**Test commands run:**

```bash
pytest -q tests/quantization/test_per_token_kv_cache.py
# plus a probe that reruns the INT4 attention test over 200 seeds
# (set_random_seed(seed)) and records corr(output_q, output_ref),
# max |output_q - output_ref|, and how many seeds fail atol=rtol=5e-2.
```

**Results:**

| Platform | Test | Case | corr(out_q, ref) | worst abs diff | seeds failing |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Intel BMG (Arc Pro B65, and a G21 board) | before | seq_lens0 | ≈ 0.00 | 0.94 | — |
| | before | seq_lens1 | ≈ 0.00 | 1.79 | fails with the default seed |
| | after, tol 5e-2 | seq_lens0 | 1.0000 | 0.006 | 0/200 |
| | after, tol 5e-2 | seq_lens1 | 1.0000 | 0.012 | 0/200 |
| NVIDIA RTX 3060 Ti (sm_86) | before, tol 0.5 | seq_lens1 | +0.004 | 1.89 | 62/200 |
| | after, tol 5e-2 | seq_lens0 | 1.0000 | 0.015 | 0/200 |
| | after, tol 5e-2 | seq_lens1 | 1.0000 | 0.021 | 0/200 |

- **BMG, `main` (e9cc6244a) with this PR:** all 82 tests in the file pass. Before the fix, `seq_lens1` fails: `Mismatched elements: 2 / 1024, Greatest absolute difference: 1.086 (up to 0.5 allowed), Greatest relative difference: 1.0`.
- **RTX 3060 Ti:** all INT4/INT8 cases pass before and after with the default seed. The FP8 cases fail both before and after with `fp8e4nv not supported in this architecture` (Ampere has no e4m3). This is unrelated to this PR.
- **BMG, this PR rebased on top of #62113:** all 94 tests pass, including the new `[(4, 128), (4, 97)]` INT4 case and both `seq_threshold_3D` values, with neither of #62113's two INT4 deselects. #62113 alone fails exactly the two INT4 cases it deselects.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `typos` pass.

**CI coverage:**
- The H200 MIG "Quantization" job runs this file, so CI covers the removed Hopper special case and the `hadacore` RHT path.
- The Intel quantization job now runs the formerly deselected case.

**Not validated locally:**
- Hopper and the `hadacore` path. On the RTX 3060 Ti the RHT ran through the Triton Hadamard kernel; the H200 job above covers both.
- ROCm.

## Details

**Root cause.** `reshape_and_cache_int4` stores `K_s = H·D·k` (RHT, with `H·H = d·I`, `D·D = I`). `unified_attention_int4` relies on that layout:
- it rotates `q' = H·D·q` and uses `softmax_scale / d`, so `q'·K_s / d = q·k`;
- it applies `D·H(·) / d` to the output, which undoes the rotation of V.

The test wrote unrotated `k`, `v` into the cache. As a result the kernel attended over `D·H·k / d` and `D·H·v / d`. Those entries have std ≈ 1/√128, so `output_q ≈ 0`, which is uncorrelated with `output_ref`.

The check `|out_q − ref| ≤ 0.5 + 0.5·|ref|` then reduces to roughly `|ref| ≤ 1`:
- kv_len 128 (`ref` std ≈ 0.15) almost always passes;
- kv_len 64/32 (`ref` std ≈ 0.25–0.3) fails on 1–2 elements whenever a `|ref|` tail exceeds 1.

That explains the reported abs diff just above 1.0 and relative diff of exactly 1.0. The failure is deterministic per seed but differs across platforms because their RNG streams differ, hence the Hopper `atol=1.1` and the Intel deselect.

**Fix.** Rotate K/V with `single_rht` (rounding through bf16, like `reshape_and_cache_int4`) before quantizing. Then inverse-rotate the dequantized reference back to the original domain, as `test_reshape_and_cache_per_token_head` and `test_per_token_head_round_trip_accuracy` already do. The original-domain values stay around N(0,1), so the reference attention is still meaningful.

**Tolerance.** The remaining error comes from bf16 rounding and accumulation order only. The worst case is 0.021 over 200 seeds on CUDA, 2.4× under 5e-2. CUDA's error is larger than XPU's because the Triton Hadamard path rotates in bf16. The reference divides by `head_size`, which equals `largest_power_of_2_divisor(head_size)` for the parametrized `head_size=128`, consistent with the rest of the file.

**Interaction with #62113.** The two PRs only conflict textually, on adjacent lines:
- the tolerance block, where #62113 appends an assert that should be kept;
- the Intel deselect line.

Whichever PR merges second should keep that assert and drop all `test_triton_unified_attention_per_token_head_scale[int4-*]` deselects.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Run test_depyf_integration in a spawned process
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`test_depyf_integration` forks its test process on CUDA, so it fails with `Cannot re-initialize CUDA in forked subprocess` whenever an earlier test in the same pytest session has initialized CUDA. This runs it in a spawned process instead, as ROCm already does. Needed before vllm-project/ci-infra#888 merges: that PR changes how PyTorch Fullgraph is sharded, and its new plan puts such a test first in the same session.

## Claims

- `test_depyf_integration` passes no matter which tests run before it in the session.
- No other test changes: one decorator argument.

## Validation

- **Without the fix:** staging build [99301](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/99301) (ci-infra#888's sharding plan): PyTorch Fullgraph shard 5/7 ran `test_clone_elimination.py`, then `test_depyf_integration` failed with `Cannot re-initialize CUDA in forked subprocess`.
- **With the fix:** staging build [99622](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/99622), same plan, same order on shard 5/7: all 7 shards passed. 42 passed / 1 skipped, the same counts and the same test IDs as a recent main build.
- On main today the test passes only because no CUDA-initializing test runs before it in its shard.

## Details

- **Root cause:** `create_new_process_for_each_test()` defaults to fork on CUDA (`tests/utils.py`). `test_clone_elimination.py` creates a CUDA tensor in the pytest process, so a forked child of that process can't initialize CUDA. The failure depends on test order, not on depyf.
- **Why spawn on the test, not on the step:** it fixes the test wherever it runs, and the same decorator argument is already used by the cudagraph and worker tests.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Run pip-compile pre-commit hooks only when requirements change
commits.pr_body:
### Summary
  - **Problem:** CI runs pre-commit with `--all-files`, so the 5 `pip-compile` hooks re-resolve every lockfile against PyPI and `download.pytorch.org` on every run, even when nothing in `requirements/` changed. When those indexes return a 502/503, pre-commit fails for changes that have nothing to do with dependencies.
- **Impact:** During a burst of 502s from `files.pythonhosted.org` (Aug 15–19), 57 PR pre-commit runs failed inside these hooks. Main went red 18 times from May to Sep for the same reason (see Examples).
- **Fix:** skip `pip-compile` in the `--all-files` run, and run it separately on only the files the commit changed. The hooks' existing `files:` filters then decide whether they need to run, so they only touch the network when requirements change.
- If `.pre-commit-config.yaml` changed, they still run on all files, because a uv bump or a hook-args edit can change the lockfiles without touching `requirements/` (as in #26591).


### Examples
- Jul 6, `pip-compile-xpu`, 503 from download.pytorch.org: [run 28826483690](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/28826483690)
- Jul 7, `pip-compile-xpu`, 503 from download.pytorch.org: [run 28834611183](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/28834611183)
- Jul 7, `pip-compile-xpu`, 503 from download.pytorch.org: [run 28840983587](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/28840983587)
- Jul 7, `pip-compile-xpu`, 503 from download.pytorch.org: [run 28901713650](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/28901713650)
- Jul 8, `pip-compile-xpu`, 503 from download.pytorch.org: [run 28977448720](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/28977448720)
- Aug 15, `pip-compile-cpu`, 502 from files.pythonhosted.org: [run 31888326977](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/31888326977)
- Aug 16, `pip-compile-xpu` and `pip-compile-docs`, 502 from files.pythonhosted.org: [run 31935561992](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/31935561992)
- Aug 16, `pip-compile-rocm`, 502 from files.pythonhosted.org: [run 31938637047](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/31938637047)
- Aug 17, `pip-compile`, `pip-compile-rocm` and `pip-compile-xpu`, 502 from files.pythonhosted.org: [run 32012766971](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/32012766971)
- Aug 17, `pip-compile`, `pip-compile-xpu`, `pip-compile-cpu` and `pip-compile-docs`, 502 from files.pythonhosted.org: [run 32021711554](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/32021711554)
- Aug 17, `pip-compile-cpu`, 502 from files.pythonhosted.org: [run 32047339080](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/32047339080)
- Aug 17, `pip-compile-cpu`, 502 from files.pythonhosted.org: [run 32073834879](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/32073834879)
- Aug 18, `pip-compile` and `pip-compile-rocm`, 502 from files.pythonhosted.org: [run 32170751177](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/32170751177)
- Aug 18, `pip-compile-cpu`, 502 from files.pythonhosted.org: [run 32172635973](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/32172635973)

- Aug 19, `pip-compile` and `pip-compile-xpu`, 502 from files.pythonhosted.org: [run 32208700153](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/32208700153)
- Sep 27, `pip-compile-xpu`, 503 from download.pytorch.org: [run 36288536065](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/36288536065)

### Tests
Real GitHub Actions runs on my fork. "Network blocked" means a dead proxy on the pip-compile step to simulate a 502 burst. Look at the `pip-compile (only if its inputs changed)` step: the jobs themselves are red because actionlint flags a line in the test harness, or because pre-commit hit a 504 while installing hook environments.

- Unrelated change, network blocked: 5x "(no files to check)", passes ([PR](https://github.com/tahsintunan/vllm/actions/runs/36866229364), [push](https://github.com/tahsintunan/vllm/actions/runs/36866206566))
- Control, old `--all-files` behavior with network blocked: all 5 fail with "Connection refused" ([run](https://github.com/tahsintunan/vllm/actions/runs/36866232937))
- Stale `requirements/test/xpu.in`: only `pip-compile-xpu` runs and fails with `+toolz` ([PR](https://github.com/tahsintunan/vllm/actions/runs/36866239120), [push](https://github.com/tahsintunan/vllm/actions/runs/36866207312))
- Same change, relocked: `pip-compile-xpu` passes ([run](https://github.com/tahsintunan/vllm/actions/runs/36866242360))
- `[tool.uv]`-only change in `pyproject.toml`: cuda, rocm, xpu, cpu fail with `+openai-harmony` ([PR](https://github.com/tahsintunan/vllm/actions/runs/36866255998), [push](https://github.com/tahsintunan/vllm/actions/runs/36866205342))
- Same change, relocked: all 5 pass ([run](https://github.com/tahsintunan/vllm/actions/runs/36866262605))
- `pyproject.toml` change outside `[tool.uv]`: all 5 run and pass ([run](https://github.com/tahsintunan/vllm/actions/runs/36866267518))
- Comment-only `.pre-commit-config.yaml` change: all 5 run and pass ([run](https://github.com/tahsintunan/vllm/actions/runs/36866248079))
- Ruff error plus stale lockfile: the main step fails on ruff, and the pip-compile step still runs and catches `+toolz` ([run](https://github.com/tahsintunan/vllm/actions/runs/36866273814))

commits.pr_title: [Mamba] Unify FI ReplaySSM STP/MTP/Prefix Caching Lifecycle
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Adds FlashInfer ReplaySSM prefix caching in `align` mode, including MTP, for Model Runners V1 and V2.
Replay rings remain inside Mamba pages.

- Preserves live state and cached prefixes across partial acceptance, preemption, and request reordering.
- Batches lifecycle work across cache groups and keeps V1 accepted-token counts on the GPU.
- Fixes Mamba page alignment and checkpoint publication before block release.

[Usage, MTP example, and supported configurations](https://github.com/askliar/vllm/blob/d9cd1fd1fcfc5a08d14ff29ba7439f76ad42d628/docs/features/automatic_prefix_caching.md#flashinfer-replayssm).

## Performance

### ReplaySSM OFF → ON

**Super 3, one GB300, TP1, V2, FP32 SSM state, CUDA graphs, no prefix caching.**
Uses the [paper workloads](https://github.com/Johnny-Liou/ReplaySSM/tree/73a9592e9d8a2268620e8883a82f5cec7442ed36/benchmarks/replayssm) with current FlashInfer.
Standard decoding generates 1,000 tokens from a short prompt. Natural MTP3 generates 256 tokens per GSM8K question.
Results average two repetitions per mode in OFF/ON/ON/OFF order.

| Workload | Batch | OFF output TPS | ON output TPS | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Natural MTP3 | 512 | 10,950 | 24,037 | **2.20×** |
| Natural MTP3 | 256 | 9,516 | 19,217 | **2.02×** |
| Standard decoding | 256 | 11,412 | 14,631 | **1.28×** |

Output TPS includes prefill and complete generation. MTP gains include higher admission:

| Workload | Peak concurrent decoding, OFF → ON | Per-request decode TPS, OFF → ON |
|---|---:|---:|
| MTP3, batch 512 | **219 → 512** | 61.99 → 59.93 |
| MTP3, batch 256 | **221 → 256** | 60.81 → 97.98 |
| Standard, batch 256 | 256 → 256 | 45.01 → 57.89 |

Concurrent decoding is measured from overlapping request timestamps. Per-request decode TPS is the reciprocal mean time per output token.
All 16 Super runs completed with zero preemptions.

### ReplaySSM OFF → ON with prefix caching

**Same TP1 paper workloads, with prefix caching enabled in both modes.**
Uses Super 3 on one GB300, V2, FP32 SSM state, stock FlashInfer, and normal CUDA graphs.
Each run seeds the exact prompt batch before timing. Results average two runs per mode in OFF/ON/ON/OFF order.

| Workload | Per-request decode TPS, OFF → ON | Decode change | Total output TPS, OFF → ON | Requests with prefix hits, OFF → ON |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| MTP3, batch 256 | 60.21 → **91.12** | **+51.3%** | 8,747 → **18,043** | 0 → **256** |
| Standard, batch 256 | 43.88 → **54.56** | **+24.3%** | 11,047 → **13,670** | 256 → 256 |
| MTP3, batch 512 | 60.83 → 57.15 | −6.1% | 10,266 → **20,384** | 0 → 0 |

- **Standard, batch 256:** both modes reuse 13 prompt tokens per request, with zero preemptions.
- **MTP3, batch 256:** ON reuses 19,683 prompt tokens per run with zero preemptions. OFF has no hits and 2–4 preemptions.
- **MTP3, batch 512:** neither mode records prefix hits. ON improves total throughput while decoding more requests together, but per-request decode slows.

Per-request decode TPS is the reciprocal mean time per output token. Total output TPS includes prefill and complete generation.
All 16 prefix-enabled runs completed. These results demonstrate prefix reuse at batch 256.
Gains include differences in cache retention and preemption.

### Prefix caching OFF → ON

**Super 3, four GB300 GPUs, TP4, V2, FP16 SSM state, concurrency one, CUDA graphs.**
ReplaySSM is enabled in both modes.
Workload: 51,200 shared tokens, then 20 turns with 2,048 new input tokens and 1,024 output tokens.
MTP uses three drafts and synthetic acceptance length 3.1151. Values average two repetitions per mode.

| Metric | Prefix OFF | Prefix ON | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| E2E output TPS | 304.76 | 518.88 | **+70.26%** |
| Decode TPS | 589.38 | 611.60 | **+3.77%** |
| Time to first token, mean repeat median | 1,658.9 ms | 249.8 ms | **−84.94%** |

Each ON run records **1,513,680 prefix-hit tokens**. Measurements include first-use checkpoint-store compilation.

### Comparison with main

Same TP4 workload, ReplaySSM enabled, prefix caching disabled.

| Comparison | Main | PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| STP decode TPS, identical saved tuning | 239.77 | 239.65 | −0.05% |
| MTP decode TPS | 577.02 | 587.76 | +1.86% |
| MTP E2E output TPS | 303.20 | 301.58 | −0.54% |

## Validation

Manual GB300 validation:

- **71 component tests passed**, with one expected missing-provider skip.
- **17 E2E test identities passed** across tested revisions, covering FP16 TP2 MTP, prefix reuse, preemption, and partial acceptance.
- **Hooks and DCO passed** on `d9cd1fd1fc`; [hosted pre-commit](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/40393393118).
- GPU tests are selected in dedicated CI jobs. Hosted GPU execution remains deferred.

**GSM8K:** Super 3, 1,319 questions, five shots, V2, TP2, FP16 SSM state, stochastic rounding, natural MTP5, and eager execution.
Both modes enable ReplaySSM. Each has zero invalid answers.

| Cache mode | Accuracy | Mean acceptance length | Prefix-hit tokens |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `none` | 93.33% | 4.254 | 0 |
| `align` | 92.80% | 4.266 | 861,972 |

<details>
<summary>Benchmark setup</summary>

Runtime source: `00cf5cb2ab`, based on main `74340c7300`. Head `d9cd1fd1fc` adds documentation only.
Stock FlashInfer: Python `0.7.2.post1`, cubin/JIT cache `0.7.2`, with version checking disabled and no provider patches.
The TP1 runs use BF16 inputs, FP8 E4M3 KV cache, replay window 16, and FlashInfer autotuning.
The TP1 cache modes are `none` without prefix caching and `align` with prefix caching.
The prefix-enabled runs use `prefix_match_unit=1` and chunked prefill to reuse the original short prompts.
GB300 power limit is 1400 W. The paper uses Triton on B300 at 1100 W.

</details>

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Scheduler] Respect disabled chunked prefill for multimodal requests
commits.pr_body:
## Overview
Fix partial prefill of multimodal pooling requests when chunked prefill is disabled. Bidirectional MEAN-pooling models can crash under async encoder-cache pressure or an explicit long-prefill threshold.


## Claims
- Defer the whole request when encoder limits would force partial prefill, releasing acquired cache references and restoring the compute budget.
- Ignore `long_prefill_token_threshold` when chunked prefill is disabled.
- Add scheduler and real-model regression coverage for both triggers.


## Validation
Reproduced with real weights for `nvidia/llama-nemotron-embed-vl-1b-v2`, using Model Runner V2. Both cases queue two distinct images with chunked prefill disabled:

- **Encoder-cache pressure:** async scheduling, a 384-token budget/cache, and 256 tokens per image. The second request fits the next step's token budget while the first image still occupies the encoder cache.
- **Prefill threshold:** synchronous scheduling with `long_prefill_token_threshold=128`, which incorrectly splits the queued prompts.

With the unchanged upstream scheduler (`c7a7607519`), both cases raise `RuntimeError: partial prefill is not supported with MEAN pooling`. With this fix, both complete and every batched embedding matches its individually processed reference with cosine similarity ≥0.999.

Focused regressions, **2 passed each**:
```bash
python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  -k encoder_cache_pressure_respects_disabled_chunked_prefill -v

python -m pytest \
  tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_llama_nemotron_vl.py \
  -k test_image_embeddings_without_chunked_prefill -v
```

## Details
The scheduler checks the token budget before scheduling encoder inputs. Encoder-cache exhaustion can subsequently shorten the request to the text before an image, violating disabled chunked prefill. Async scheduling exposes this when an earlier batch still holds encoder-cache references. An explicit long-prefill threshold provides a separate path to partial prefill under synchronous scheduling.

The encoder check lives in `_try_schedule_encoder_inputs`. The threshold is applied only when chunked prefill is enabled.

Open-PR searches found no equivalent fix. Related work: [#63033](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63033) adds a PaliGemma-specific whole-prompt guard; [#61733](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61733) rejects permanently oversized prompts at admission. Neither covers these two triggers.

commits.pr_title: [Build] Marlin: drop SM12x-specific cubins and rely on compute_80 PTX
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Part of #65560.

Revert the SM12x-specific cubins that #40923 added for the fp16/bf16 Marlin and Marlin-MoE kernels, and go back to building them as `8.0+PTX` only. On SM12x the driver JIT-compiles the existing PTX (compute_80 for fp16, compute_90 for bf16), which on current main is correct and runs at the same speed.

## Claims

- #40923's premise (Marlin-MoE gives wrong output on SM12x without native cubins) does not reproduce on current main: Marlin kernel tests and an end-to-end Marlin-MoE eval through the PTX JIT match the native-cubin build on GB10 (SM121).
- Removes the sm_120 SASS for every fp16/bf16 Marlin and Marlin-MoE kernel from multi-arch builds (with `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="8.0;9.0;12.0"`: `_C_stable_libtorch` 74.6 → 70.0 MB, `_moe_C_stable_libtorch` 35.0 → 29.0 MB, −10.6 MB total; compile time for these two targets 656 s → 593 s).
- Cost: a one-time PTX JIT on SM12x, about +5–9 s on a cold driver JIT cache (`~/.nv/ComputeCache`); nothing once the cache is warm.

## Validation

All on DGX Spark (GB10, SM121), CUDA 13.0, built with `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=12.1`. Confirmed with `cuobjdump` that the PR build has no sm_120 SASS for the fp16/bf16 Marlin kernels (only sm_80/sm_90 SASS + compute_80/compute_90 PTX), so every test below goes through the JIT.

| Check | main (native sm_120) | this PR (PTX JIT) |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/kernels/quantization/test_marlin_gemm.py` | 520 passed, 2 failed | 522 passed |
| `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py -k marlin` | 305 passed, 6 skipped | 305 passed, 6 skipped |
| gpt-oss-20b, `--moe-backend marlin`, GSM8K (100 q) | 0.36, 1395 tok/s | 0.33, 1400 tok/s |
| Startup to `/health`, cold JIT cache, Qwen2.5-3B-GPTQ-Int4 | 90.6 s / 89.1 s | 97.8 s |
| Startup to `/health`, cold JIT cache, gpt-oss-20b Marlin MoE | 30.4 s / 26.3 s | 35.5 s |

The main column uses the precompiled main wheel. Its 2 dense failures were not investigated, and they did not occur with the PR build. The GSM8K gap is within noise for 100 questions. Output is coherent, not the gibberish described in #40923.

```bash
vllm serve openai/gpt-oss-20b --moe-backend marlin --max-model-len 8192
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-questions 100
```

## Details

- `MARLIN_ARCHS`, `MARLIN_BF16_ARCHS` and `MARLIN_MOE_ARCHS` go back to `8.0+PTX` (bf16 keeps `9.0+PTX` for the atomicAdd path). The CUDA < 13.0 `12.0a;12.1a` branches go too.
- The FP8-activation kernels (`MARLIN_FP8_ARCHS` / `MARLIN_MOE_FP8_ARCHS`) keep their 8.9/12.x targets: they use e4m3 MMA, which compute_80 PTX cannot express. #65542 removes Marlin's 8-bit activation paths entirely in favor of Humming; the two PRs are independent.
- A build that targets only SM12x gets bigger (sm_80 SASS + PTX instead of only sm_120 SASS: 46.0/27.0 MB vs 37.3/15.5 MB for `_C_stable_libtorch`/`_moe_C_stable_libtorch`). The release wheel targets many archs and already ships the sm_80 + PTX copy, so it only loses the sm_120 copy.

Not a duplicate: no open PR changes these arch lists (searched "marlin PTX sm120", "marlin 12.0f").
