commits.pr_title: [Kernel] Marlin: remove 8-bit (INT8/FP8) activation support, rely on Humming
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Part of #65560.

Remove INT8 and FP8 activation support (W4A8) from the dense and MoE Marlin kernels. Marlin becomes a 16-bit-activation kernel, and Humming covers 8-bit activations. Independent of #65540 (Marlin PTX-only build); this PR leaves the fp16/bf16 Marlin arch lists alone.

## Claims

- Removes Marlin's W4A8-INT8 (GPTQ/AWQ INT4) and W4A8-FP8 (GPTQ/AWQ INT4, MXFP4) paths: the sm89 FP8-activation kernels and their SM89/SM12x build targets, the INT8-activation instantiations, the 8-bit paths in both templates, the `marlin_int4_fp8_preprocess` op, `a_scales` on `marlin_gemm`/`moe_wna16_marlin_gemm`, and `is_a_8bit` on the repack ops. Net −2039 lines.
- `VLLM_MARLIN_INPUT_DTYPE` is removed, and setting it raises an error with a migration hint. The replacement is `--quantization humming` with `VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG='{"dtype":"int8"}'` (or `float8e4m3`), documented in `docs/features/quantization/README.md`.
- Compressed-tensors W4A8-FP8 checkpoints on SM89/SM12x, which previously fell back to Marlin, now select `HummingLinearKernel`.
- No change for FP8-weight Marlin (W8A16, MXFP8) or any 16-bit-activation format.

## Validation

DGX Spark (GB10, SM121), CUDA 13.0, `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=12.1` source build of this branch (kernel tests rerun after rebasing onto main without #65540, with native sm_120f Marlin cubins).

Kernel tests: `test_marlin_gemm.py` 254 passed, `test_moe.py -k marlin` 189 passed / 6 skipped, `test_marlin_tile_padding.py` 98 passed, `test_reload.py -k marlin` 6 passed, `test_marlin_vs_trtllm_mxint4.py` 1 passed. The counts dropped because the 8-bit-activation cases were removed. pre-commit (incl. mypy) passes.

GSM8K, `Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct-GPTQ-Int4`, 100 questions, 5-shot:

| Config | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| default (Marlin W4A16) | 0.62, 3348 tok/s | 0.60 / 0.62 (2 runs), 3364 tok/s |
| W4A8-INT8 (main: `VLLM_MARLIN_INPUT_DTYPE=int8`; PR: `--quantization humming` + `VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG='{"dtype":"int8"}'`) | 0.68, 3413 tok/s | 0.63, 4008 tok/s |
| W4A8-FP8 (same, `fp8` / `float8e4m3`) | 0.69, 3554 tok/s | 0.62, 3842 tok/s |

The 100-question accuracy gaps are within noise. On the full set (1319 questions, accuracy only):

| Config | main (Marlin) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| W4A16 | 0.622 | 0.622 (Marlin) |
| W4A8-INT8 | 0.625 | 0.644 (Humming) |
| W4A8-FP8 | 0.591 | 0.603 (Humming) |

I checked that the Humming runs actually quantize activations by reading the loaded layer config: `a_dtype=int8, as_dtype=float32`. Note that `--linear-backend humming` with the same env var does **not** quantize activations for GPTQ/AWQ (`a_dtype=float16`), which is why the docs point to `--quantization humming`. Setting `VLLM_MARLIN_INPUT_DTYPE` now fails at startup with: `ValueError: VLLM_MARLIN_INPUT_DTYPE has been removed. Marlin no longer supports 8-bit activations. Use --quantization humming and set the activation dtype with VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG, e.g. '{"dtype":"int8"}'.`

```bash
VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG='{"dtype":"int8"}' vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct-GPTQ-Int4 --quantization humming --max-model-len 8192
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-questions 100
```

## Details

- On main, the Marlin 8-bit path was already narrow. For linear layers it only worked with GPTQ symmetric INT4: AWQ + `VLLM_MARLIN_INPUT_DTYPE=int8` fails at load with "W8A8 is not supported by marlin kernel". FP8-weight + FP8-activation was plumbed in Python but never instantiated.
- Template changes are constant folding of `is_a_8bit == false`, so the 16-bit kernels compile to the same code. The `mma` helpers lose the k=32 path and the `k_size`/`idx` params, and the repack kernels lose their `is_a_8bit` template param.
- `MarlinLinearKernel.can_implement` rejects 1-byte activation types, so selection falls through to Humming. `ConchLinearKernel` now also rejects non-16-bit activations; it had no activation check and sits between Marlin and Humming in the CUDA list.
- `int_wna16` MoE conversion returns 8 entries instead of 10 (the INT8 input global scales are gone). Every in-tree caller is updated.
- Not validated: Humming W4A8 MoE end to end. Marlin MoE W4A8 was only reachable through the removed env var.
- Deprecation: `VLLM_MARLIN_INPUT_DTYPE` is removed without a deprecation cycle. Setting it is now a hard error, raised from `validate_environ` via a new `envs.removed_environment_variables` map, and the message points to `--quantization humming` with `VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG`. Without the error, a user who set it would silently fall back to W4A16. Covered in `tests/config/test_config_generation.py::test_unrecognized_env`.

Superseded open PRs that extend Marlin W4A8: #58326, #48926, #38066, #50096, #59895, #61405, #49039, #57091. No open PR removes these paths (searched "VLLM_MARLIN_INPUT_DTYPE", "marlin w4a8", "marlin int8/fp8 activation", "remove marlin").

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Model] Add Beam 1.0 support on ROCm
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview


ROCm follow-up to [#61978](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61978), which adds day-0 support for Reflection's [Beam 1.0](https://huggingface.co/reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B) and its [DFlash2 drafter](https://huggingface.co/reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-DFlash2).


EDIT: Since #61978 has been split into smaller PRs (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62042, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62052, and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62074), I've updated against main and now the PR diff isn't swamped by the changes from #61978.

This PR adds AMD-owned implementations under `vllm/models/beam/amd/` for both `BeamForCausalLM` and `DFlash2BeamDraftModel`. The NVIDIA implementation from #61978 is unchanged in the relative diff. Shared package dispatch selects the AMD classes on ROCm and the NVIDIA classes elsewhere.

## Claims

- Beam 1.0 BF16 loads and serves on 8x MI350X with TP8 and expert parallelism through the AMD model path.
- Beam's required FP32 activation, normalization, Q/K preprocessing, attention-output gate, and logit-softcap arithmetic is retained in AMD-local Triton kernels.
- The AMD target uses standard vLLM ROCm attention and KV-cache updates, linear layers, finalized MoE output, and RCCL collectives rather than NVIDIA direct-cache, CuTe/FlashInfer, or MNNVL fast paths.
- The AMD DFlash2 implementation loads the released 1.93B drafter, generates successfully, and delegates cache writes and cache-format handling to the selected ROCm attention backend.
- The change adds no HIP/C++ kernels and does not modify the scheduler, KV-cache manager, model runner, attention backends, or NVIDIA Beam implementation.
- Added recipe in line with https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/issues/1107

### Serving commands

Target only:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 16384 \
  --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 131072 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \
  --moe-backend triton \
  --reasoning-parser beam \
  --tool-call-parser beam \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

With DFlash2:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 16384 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \
  --moe-backend triton \
  --speculative-config '{
    "method": "dflash",
    "model": "reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-DFlash2",
    "num_speculative_tokens": 8
  }'
```

## Validation

**Setup:** 8x AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950), ROCm 10.1, PyTorch 2.13, TP8 with expert parallelism, Beam 1.0 BF16 and the BF16 DFlash2 drafter.

| Check | Target only | DFlash2 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Ruff checks and formatting | Passed | Passed |
| Current-source ROCm build | Passed | Passed |
| Full 501B checkpoint and drafter load | Passed | Passed |
| GSM8K, 1,319 questions, strict extraction | 1,202/1,319 (91.13% ± 0.78%) | 1,200/1,319 (90.98% ± 0.79%) |
| GSM8K, 1,319 questions, flexible extraction | 1,212/1,319 (91.89% ± 0.75%) | 1,212/1,319 (91.89% ± 0.75%) |

The GSM8K used 5-shot chat, greedy decoding, `max_gen_toks=1024`, TP8, and expert parallelism.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

```bash
lm_eval \
  --model vllm \
  --model_args pretrained=/path/to/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B,tensor_parallel_size=8,dtype=bfloat16,max_model_len=16384,gpu_memory_utilization=0.85,enable_expert_parallel=True \
  --tasks gsm8k \
  --num_fewshot 5 \
  --batch_size auto \
  --apply_chat_template \
  --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=1024
```

The lm-eval vLLM wrapper also accepts the top-level speculative aliases:

```text
spec_method=dflash,spec_model=/path/to/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-DFlash2,spec_tokens=8
```

```bash
vllm bench serve \
  --backend vllm \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
  --model beam \
  --tokenizer /path/to/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B \
  --dataset-name random \
  --num-prompts 10 \
  --random-input-len 8192 \
  --random-output-len 10 \
  --max-concurrency 10 \
  --request-rate inf \
  --ignore-eos \
  --temperature 0 \
  --seed 42
```

</details>

### Short concurrency sweep
On NVIDIA SPEED-Bench `throughput_8k` / `low_entropy`, with a fixed 1,024-token output, greedy decoding, 16 warmup requests per point, and `10 * concurrency` measured requests:

| Concurrency | Prompts | Target tok/s | DFlash2 tok/s | Speedup | Target TTFT | DFlash2 TTFT | Acceptance length |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 10 | 117.40 | 168.47 | 1.44x | 234.66 ms | 241.48 ms | 3.41 |
| 4 | 40 | 331.88 | 443.00 | 1.33x | 657.87 ms | 297.50 ms | 3.51 |
| 8 | 80 | 492.26 | 769.78 | 1.56x | 634.83 ms | 240.43 ms | 3.63 |
| 16 | 160 | 803.81 | 1,263.22 | 1.57x | 788.46 ms | 265.18 ms | 3.57 |

All 580 measured requests across both modes succeeded. DFlash2 token acceptance ranged from 30.13% to 32.83%. These are single runs without variability estimates.

<details>
<summary>SPEED-Bench run configuration</summary>

Both servers used the same target configuration:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve /path/to/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 16384 \
  --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 131072 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \
  --moe-backend triton \
  --served-model-name beam \
  --disable-log-requests
```

The DFlash2 server added:

```bash
--speculative-config '{
  "method": "dflash",
  "model": "/path/to/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-DFlash2",
  "num_speculative_tokens": 8
}'
```

Each server was reused across all four concurrency points. `vllm bench serve` issued its initial probe and 16 warmup requests before the measured requests at each point:

```bash
for concurrency in 1 4 8 16; do
  num_prompts=$((10 * concurrency))
  vllm bench serve \
    --backend vllm \
    --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
    --model beam \
    --tokenizer /path/to/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B \
    --dataset-name speed_bench \
    --dataset-path /path/to/prepared/speed-bench \
    --speed-bench-dataset-subset throughput_8k \
    --speed-bench-category low_entropy \
    --speed-bench-output-len 1024 \
    --num-prompts "${num_prompts}" \
    --num-warmups 16 \
    --max-concurrency "${concurrency}" \
    --request-rate inf \
    --ignore-eos \
    --temperature 0 \
    --seed 42
done
```

</details>

### Remaining validation

- [x] Accuracy benchmarks (with and without dflash2)
  - [X] GSM8k 
  - [x] GPQA-diamond
  - [x] AIME2025
- [X] Performance baseline using NVIDIA [speedbench](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/SPEED-Bench) 8k with low entropy and 1k fixed OSL
- [x] Same checks for gfx942

## Details

- **Vendor ownership:** All ROCm target and DFlash2 implementation code lives under `vllm/models/beam/amd/`. The relative diff does not modify `vllm/models/beam/nvidia/`.
- **Platform dispatch:** `vllm.models.beam` exports AMD target and draft classes on ROCm and NVIDIA classes on other platforms.
- **Target execution:** AMD attention uses ordinary backend-owned K/V cache updates. AMD projections use standard vLLM linear layers, MoE returns finalized output normally, and distributed reductions use standard RCCL paths.
- **DFlash2 cache handling:** AMD-local Triton computes context K normalization and RoPE. Cache layout, slot scattering, optional shuffling, and quantization are delegated to each ROCm attention backend's native cache-update API rather than hard-coded pointer arithmetic.
- **Numerics:** AMD-local Triton kernels retain Beam's required FP32 operations and intermediate BF16 rounding boundaries.
- **HIP launch compatibility:** AMD kernels omit CUDA-only Triton launch options such as `enable_reflect_ftz` and `launch_pdl`.
- **Footprint:** 1,968 additions and 2 deletions across 12 Beam model files; no core execution or NVIDIA implementation changes.

AI assistance was used. The submitter should review every changed line and this description before converting the PR from draft.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Keep the HiSparse FlashInfer all-reduce backend on lazy workspace creation
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

#65201 forces the `trtllm` FlashInfer all-reduce backend under HiSparse to avoid the MNNVL fused AR+RMSNorm race (#64327). The override was skipped when the shared workspace was created lazily outside the vLLM config context. HiSparse servers then still came up on `mnnvl` and crashed with `CUDA error: unspecified launch failure`. Related: #56699.

## Claims

- HiSparse servers on main now get the `trtllm` all-reduce workspace without needing `VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND`.
- Fixes the asynchronous `CUDA error: unspecified launch failure` (driver 719) under HiSparse multi-turn agentic load. It surfaces at the next event sync, e.g. `_finish_mirror_phase` or `async_utils.get_output`.

## Validation

Hardware: 4×B200, TP4. Main = 70eaf457c3. PR = 70eaf457c3 + this diff (since merged with current main; the touched file is unchanged there). Both arms ran an identical environment shim on `PYTHONPATH`: the kernel fix from #61463 (merged since), an `os.memfd_create` polyfill for the container's Python build, and logging probes. Nothing else differs.

Server:

```bash
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=skip
vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 --revision c8917e4258572c405575855ff53effe58c17a38e \
  --tokenizer-revision c8917e4258572c405575855ff53effe58c17a38e --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --block-size 64 \
  --max-model-len 98304 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 256 --seed 0 \
  --enable-prompt-tokens-details --no-enable-extensible-kv-cache --served-model-name zai-org/GLM-5.3 \
  --port 8000 --attention-config '{"hisparse_config":{}}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":160}}'
```

Client (evalscope 1.14.1, `swe_smith` multi-turn dataset JSON):

```bash
evalscope perf --url http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions --api openai --model zai-org/GLM-5.3 \
```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][CUDA] Use CUDA memory accounting for integrated GPUs on WSL
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix model startup on NVIDIA integrated GPUs under WSL by using CUDA-reported free memory rather than WSL guest RAM availability.

## Claims

- Apply the CUDA-on-WSL exception in the shared `device_memory_info()` helper, covering memory snapshots and extensible KV-cache sizing.
- Preserve native Linux UMA accounting, discrete GPUs, and non-CUDA platforms.
- Extend the existing helper regression test and explicitly select the native environment in the reclaimable-memory sizing test.

## Validation

Original hardware validation was performed by the human submitter using upstream vLLM containers with and without the patch on an ASUS ProArt P16 RTX Spark laptop, Ubuntu under WSL, 128 GB memory with a 64 GB GPU carveout.

| Model/configuration | Upstream without patch | With patch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4`, FP8 KV cache, 262144 context, utilization 0.8, DFlash2 | Startup fails with “not enough free RAM” | Server starts successfully |

<details>
<summary>Hardware reproduction command supplied by the submitter</summary>

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 \

  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model": "z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2", "num_speculative_tokens":8}' \
  --load-format safetensors \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

</details>


Current merge validation against upstream main `b43366fa4b8d4d1dea3b4036f877b428733d45dd` on 2026-11-04:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Memory snapshot and shared-helper regression tests | 14 passed, 1 GPU-only profiling test deselected |
| Existing measured KV-cache sizing tests | 2 passed, 21 unrelated tests deselected |
| Pre-commit on affected files | Passed |
| Python compilation and diff whitespace checks against upstream | Passed |

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/utils_/test_mem_utils.py -k 'memory_snapshot or device_memory_info' -q

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/utils/mem_utils.py tests/utils_/test_mem_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_extensible_kv_cache.py
```

<details>
<summary>Regression failure on current upstream, then success with the fix</summary>

The regression suite was copied to an unmodified upstream-main worktree at `b43366fa4b`. The baseline test copy uses `create=True` for the new `in_wsl` mock target, which upstream has not imported.

```text
# Run in /tmp/vllm-uma-wsl-base-20261104 with the same environment:
/home/eugr/Projects/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/utils_/test_mem_utils.py -k 'memory_snapshot or device_memory_info' -q

FAILED test_memory_snapshot_integrated_gpu_accounting[20-cuda-wsl]
AssertionError: assert 21474836480 == 42949672960
FAILED test_memory_snapshot_integrated_gpu_accounting[100-cuda-wsl]
AssertionError: assert 107374182400 == 42949672960
FAILED test_device_memory_info_integrated_gpu_accounting[True]
At index 0 diff: 107374182400 != 42949672960
```

</details>

The existing Buildkite `utils_` and `v1/worker` steps select these tests. WSL hardware is not covered by those CI lanes; the original hardware startup comparison above validates the affected deployment outside CI. This merge was checked locally with the established precompiled test environment and mocked hardware memory reports; GPU profiling and a fresh WSL model run were not performed. No accuracy or throughput changes are claimed.

## Details

The integrated-GPU correction normally replaces CUDA free memory with `psutil.virtual_memory().available` to include reclaimable native Linux system memory. Under WSL, guest RAM does not represent CUDA's allocation budget, particularly with a GPU memory carveout, so this substitution can reject a model that fits.

Upstream [#65413](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65413) extracted the correction into `device_memory_info()`. This PR retains that refactor and applies the existing cached CUDA+WSL condition in the shared helper. Native UMA behavior and the helper's callers remain intact. No options, dependencies, explicit synchronization, or transfers are added.

Duplicate-work searches before opening found no other open fix for `WSL UMA` or `WSL psutil`. The native UMA and ROCm accounting changes discussed in [#54776](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54776), [#49760](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49760), and [#46932](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46932) address different behavior. commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Reject push handshakes between different P/D block sizes
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

NixlPushConnector now rejects P/D peers with different block sizes at the handshake, so their requests fail at once instead of stalling or crashing D.

## Claims

- A P/D pair that differs in kernel block size or kernel blocks per logical block is rejected at the handshake, and D keeps serving.
- Pull and equal-block-size push are unchanged.

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py
```

`test_push_handshake_rejects_different_block_sizes` covers the new check. Of the two tests of the removed PP-only check, `test_layer_handshake_rejects_unsupported_geometry` keeps only its TP case, and `test_packed_mla_rejects_unequal_block_sizes_before_peer_registration` is removed: the new check does not depend on packed MLA or PP and runs before any registration.

CPU, this PR at `32bad14c7d` on main `8530a778f7`: the new test's 3 cases fail without this PR and pass with it. Other NIXL unit tests are unchanged.

GB10, main `8530a778f7` without and with this PR at `1675f70e48`: both P/D pairs that stall or crash D on main are rejected at D's handshake and D keeps serving; 64/64 push is bitwise equal to main's push.

<details>
<summary>GB10 runs</summary>

Qwen3-0.6B, NixlPushConnector, P and D on one GPU, greedy, `--enforce-eager`, code prompts (2 per rejected pair, 6 for 64/64).

| P / D | backend | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16 / 64 | FLASH_ATTN | P's handshake fails with `Local block size 16 is not divisible by remote block size 64 or vice versa.`; both requests still pending at the 150 s client timeout | D's handshake raises `NixlPushConnector requires identical P/D block sizes. Kernel block size and kernel blocks per logical block: local (64, 1), remote engine … (16, 1).`; both requests fail at once |
| 128 / 64, both with 64-token kernel blocks | FLASHINFER | D's EngineCore dies with `IndexError: tuple index out of range` in `get_transfer_results` | rejected the same way (local (64, 1), remote (64, 2)) |
| 64 / 64 | FLASH_ATTN | 6/6 served | 6/6 outputs, logprobs bitwise equal to main's push |

In both rejected cases D's `/health` stays 200 and a direct completion sent to D succeeds.

</details>

## Details

NixlPushConnector cannot convert or re-pair blocks when P and D differ in kernel block size or kernel blocks per logical block, and D registers P for notifications without checking either. On main, for such a pair:

1. D handshakes with P and sends `PUSH_REG` with its block ids.
2. P handshakes with D and WRITEs into those blocks. Depending on the sizes, P's handshake fails or P writes misaligned blocks.
3. D waits for a WRITE that never comes, or its receive fails on the block-size-ratio assert or on empty push block ids.

This PR rejects such peers in `NixlPushConnectorWorker._validate_remote_parallel_config`, which `_nixl_handshake` runs for P's and both of D's handshakes (registration and heartbeat) before registering the peer, so the request fails like any failed handshake. It replaces the PP-only block-size check in `add_remote_agent` and removes push's `block_size_ratio > 1` branch in `_xfer_blocks`, which can no longer run.

No open PR rejects push peers with different block sizes.

commits.pr_title: [MiniMax-M3] Support sequence parallelism with pipeline parallelism
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

MiniMax-M3 enables model-level sequence parallelism (SP) for TP + EP + MegaMoE (#64659), keeping the residual stream sharded by token across TP ranks, but only when pipeline parallelism (PP) is off. This PR keeps SP on under PP, handling stage boundaries the same way as DeepSeek-V4.1: non-last stages all-gather the token shards before returning `IntermediateTensors`, and the next stage re-shards them on entry. No other open PR enables this combination.

## Claims

- MiniMax-M3 with MegaMoE, TP > 1 and PP > 1 now runs the same SP path as PP = 1.
- PP2 and PP4 reproduce PP1's prompt logprobs exactly; GSM8K matches PP1 with and without DSpark.
- Throughput at PP2 × TP2 is unchanged: for each workload, the runs with and without this PR overlap.
- PP = 1 and non-MegaMoE backends are unchanged.

## Validation

`MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` on B300, TP2 + EP + MegaMoE.

**Prompt logprobs.** Six fixed prompts via `/v1/completions` with `prompt_logprobs: 0` (405 scored positions). PP2 and PP4 with this PR match PP1 at every position (max |Δ| = 0).

**GSM8K** (1319 questions, chat, thinking disabled):

| Config | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| PP1 × TP2 (SP on) | 0.958 | unchanged |
| PP2 × TP2 | 0.957 (SP off) | 0.960 |
| PP1 × TP2 + DSpark (SP on) | 0.957 | unchanged |
| PP2 × TP2 + DSpark | 0.962 (SP off) | 0.951, 0.957 |

DSpark draft acceptance (`num_speculative_tokens=7`): 0.524 at PP1; 0.521 and 0.523 at PP2 with this PR; 0.526 at PP2 on main.

**Throughput**, PP2 × TP2, output tok/s of two interleaved runs per arm:

| Workload (in/out, concurrency) | main (SP off) | This PR (SP on) |
|---|---|---|
| decode 512/512, c64 | 2013, 2005 | 2007, 1994 |
| mixed 2048/256, c64 | 1654, 1660 | 1576, 1659 |
| prefill 8192/16, c8 | 97.6, 98.0 | 97.8, 100.5 |

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash --trust-remote-code --max-model-len 16384 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 64 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --enable-expert-parallel --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --pipeline-parallel-size 2
# DSpark rows add:
#   --speculative-config '{"method": "dspark", "num_speculative_tokens": 7, "attention_backend": "FLASHINFER_TS", "kv_cache_dtype": "fp8", "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic", "rejection_sample_method": "block"}'

python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --max-concurrency 64 \
  --use-chat-completions --max-tokens 1024 \
  --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}'

vllm bench serve --model MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 512 --num-prompts 512 \
  --max-concurrency 64 --ignore-eos --seed 1

curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model": "...", "prompt": "...", "max_tokens": 1, "temperature": 0, "prompt_logprobs": 0}'
```
</details>

## Details

PP transport sends 1/TP of each `IntermediateTensors` entry from every TP rank and all-gathers it on the receiver, so stage outputs must cover all tokens and be identical across TP ranks. The change:

- Drop `pipeline_parallel_size == 1` from `_use_sequence_parallel`.
- On entry to a non-first stage, shard the received `residual` together with `hidden_states`.
- At a non-last stage exit, pack `hidden_states`, `residual` and the aux hidden states into one tensor and all-gather it once. On the last rank, aux states received from earlier stages are already full and are appended after the local gather, as before.
- Build the dense MLP's `down_proj` with `reduce_results=False` under SP. With PP > 1 the decoder layer asks each FFN to reduce its own output, but under SP the dense MLP already reduce-scatters the `down_proj` output, so an extra all-reduce would sum it twice.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to investigate, implement and validate this change. The submitter reviewed every changed line and the validation results.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][DCP] Sparse indexer: key only significant bits in the DCP top-k merge
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Since #61149 (DeepGEMM 2026-09-30), the SM100 MQA logits of the sparse indexer are BF16. Under DCP they are upcast to FP32 before the top-k, so the low 16 bits of every candidate score that reaches the DCP top-k merge are zero. The merge selector, `StableTopKFromGatheredCandidatesKernel`, radix-sorts the 64-bit key `score << 32 | ~token_id` in 11-bit passes. BF16 scores almost always tie at the top-k boundary. The radix then also walks the 16 zero score bits and the constant high bits of the token id, and each of those passes funnels every remaining candidate into a single histogram bin.

This PR packs only the bits that carry information into the key: the 16 high score bits when the logits were BF16, and the token-id bits that positions below `max_model_len` need. The selected set is unchanged.

## Claims

- Removes the DCP top-k merge cost that #61149 added. It applies to every DSA model with a sparse indexer under DCP on SM100 (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x).
  - With BF16 scores, the selector costs 1.6-1.7x what it costs with FP32 scores.
  - With this PR it is back to the FP32 cost. Per call at top-2048 on GB300:
    - DCP4: 16.7 → 10.6 us (FP32: 10.4), and 21.0 → 11.5 us on concentrated scores;
    - DCP8: 24.8 → 14.5 us (FP32: 14.3), and 32.2 → 19.0 us.
- GLM-5.3, TP4 DCP4 on one GB300 node, 60k-token prompts, 4 runs per variant on 2 nodes:
  - the selector goes from 21.0 to 14.2 us per call in decode (21 calls per step);
  - c1 TPOT p50 drops from 13.55 to 13.44 ms (-0.8%);
  - c2 TPOT p50 drops from 17.77 to 17.65 ms;
  - c8 ITL p50 drops from 19.30 to 19.13 ms.
- No behavior change:
  - The selection uses the same total order: score at the precision it was computed in, then the smaller token id.
  - Main and this PR select the same set:
    - in unit tests with forced boundary ties;
    - on 28.4M rows merged in GLM-5.3 runs and checked against main's selector. 97% of the rows with more than 2048 candidates had a tie at the boundary.
  - FP32 logits keep 32 score bits.
  - GSM8K is within run-to-run noise.

## Validation

### Serving: GLM-5.3 (`zai-org/GLM-5.3`, FP8)

Setup:
- TP4 + DCP4 on one GB300 node (4 GPUs), model runner V2, default DCP backend (`a2a`);
- `--attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`;
- `--max-model-len 65536 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 64 --no-enable-prefix-caching`;
- `-cc.cudagraph_mode=FULL_DECODE_ONLY`: decode steps replay full CUDA graphs. With the default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, `main` itself did not start on this setup: the ranks diverged during PIECEWISE capture. That is unrelated to this PR.
- `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 60000 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos`, with 6 prompts at c1, 12 at c2 and 24 at c8.

Method:
- Two Slurm jobs on two nodes. Each job runs four servers on the same node: `main, PR, main, PR` and `PR, main, PR, main`.
- Values are the means over the 4 runs of each variant. The per-run spread of c1 TPOT p50 is 0.01-0.03 ms.
- `main` is 803bc13cf9.

| | c1 main | c1 this PR | c2 main | c2 this PR | c8 main | c8 this PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TPOT p50 (ms) | 13.55 | **13.44** | 17.77 | **17.65** | 52.52 | **51.91** |
| TPOT p99 (ms) | 13.65 | **13.47** | 20.65 | **20.46** | 61.50 | **61.07** |
| ITL p50 (ms) | 13.64 | **13.51** | 15.09 | **14.95** | 19.30 | **19.13** |
| TTFT p50 (ms) | 6673 | **6609** | 10059 | **9997** | 16284 | 16405 |
| output tok/s | 49.84 | **50.29** | 72.41 | **72.96** | 116.53 | **117.29** |

- Per run, c1 TPOT p50 is 13.55-13.56 ms on `main` and 13.43-13.46 ms with this PR.
- At c8, TPOT includes the steps that carry 8192-token prefill chunks of the other 60k-token prompts, so it varies by ±1 ms between runs. ITL p50 is the plain decode step: 19.23-19.42 ms on `main` and 19.04-19.21 ms with this PR.
- c8 TTFT depends on how the prefills interleave and is within its run-to-run spread (14.6-17.3 s).

GLM-5.3 has 21 sparse-indexer layers per step (`index_topk_freq=4`). Models with an indexer in every layer, like DeepSeek-V3.2, or DCP8 with 2x the candidates, save proportionally more per step.

### Kernel time in the model (torch profiler)

Same setup, 60k-token prompts, 8192 candidates per row (4 ranks × top-2048). The table gives the median per call on ranks 0 and 2 (they agree within 0.1 us). Each decode trace covers 29-40 steps (609-840 selector calls).

| | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| merge selector (`StableTopKFromGatheredCandidatesKernel`), decode c1 (1 row) | 19.4 us | **13.8 us** |
| merge selector, decode c8 (8 rows) | 21.0 us | **14.2 us** |
| merge selector per decode step (21 calls), c1 / c8 | 409 / 441 us | **290 / 298 us** |
| merge selector, first 8192-token prefill chunk (8192 rows) | 649 us | **449 us** |
| local top-k `cooperative_topk` (control), c1 / c8 | 9.6 / 9.9 us | 9.7 / 9.9 us |

The per-step saving (119 us at c1, 143 us at c8) matches the measured TPOT/ITL gain. The prefill-chunk saving is where the ~1% lower c1 TTFT comes from: every prefill chunk runs the merge in each of the 21 indexer layers.

### Microbenchmark

All-gather selector alone on one GB300, top-2048, ids drawn from a 64k context (16 id bits). us per call, CUDA graph of 100 launches. "Wide" scores are N(0, 3²). "Narrow" scores are 60 + N(0, 4²): they are more concentrated, so more of them tie at BF16 precision. "set == ref" checks the selection against an FP64 reference.

| DCP | rows | scores | main | this PR | set == ref |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---|
| 4 | 1 | FP32 wide | 10.4 | **9.3** | yes |
| 4 | 1 | BF16 wide | 16.7 | **10.6** | yes |
| 4 | 1 | BF16 narrow | 21.0 | **11.5** | yes |
| 4 | 8 | BF16 narrow | 20.6 | **11.9** | yes |
| 8 | 1 | FP32 wide | 14.3 | **12.7** | yes |
| 8 | 1 | BF16 wide | 24.8 | **14.5** | yes |
| 8 | 1 | BF16 narrow | 32.2 | **19.0** | yes |
| 8 | 8 | BF16 narrow | 32.7 | **19.1** | yes |

FP32 logits keep 32 score bits and gain a little from the shorter id field.

### Correctness

- Selection on real model data:
  - A check-only build of this PR (not part of the diff) re-ran `main`'s selector (64-bit key) on the same gathered candidates after every DCP merge and compared the selected sets. It ran in eager mode, so it could sync.
  - Workload: GLM-5.3 TP4 DCP4, serving the greedy prompts below (up to 51k tokens), 200 GSM8K questions and 8 random 60k-token requests at c8. Prefill chunks and decode steps are both covered.
  - Two runs, counted on DCP rank 0: 28.4M merged rows.
    - 24.3M of them had more than 2048 valid candidates.
    - 23.7M (97%) had a tie at the top-k boundary.
    - **0 rows differed from `main`'s selection.**
  - The same check on GLM-5.3-Flash (`zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, kpool indexer, top-512 pools out of 2048 candidates), TP4 DCP4 with `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 64`, covered the long greedy prompts and 4 random 60k-token requests at c8.
    - It checked 4.65M rows: 4.45M had more than 512 candidates, and 4.23M had a tie at the boundary.
    - **0 mismatches.**
- GSM8K (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, 1319 questions, 5-shot, completions, max concurrency 64), same setup as above:

| | runs | accuracy |
|---|---|---|
| main | 3 | 90.8, 91.4, 91.4 |
| this PR | 2 | 91.8, 91.6 |

- Greedy (`temperature=0`), sequential at c1, 38 prompts: 34 short ones (128 tokens each) and 4 real-text prompts of 8k, 20k, 38k and 51k tokens (256 tokens each). This setup is not deterministic run to run, even on `main`:
  - `main`, the same server queried twice: 11/38 and 16/38 outputs differ;
  - `main` across server restarts: 14/38 and 15/38;
  - this PR, the same server twice: 12/38;
  - this PR vs `main`: 11/38, 13/38 and 16/38.

  Most of the differing prompts are short ones. There every valid candidate is selected, so this PR cannot change their result. The outputs diverge after a common prefix, as numerical noise does. So greedy identity cannot separate the two here. The check on real model data above can.

### Tests

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
```

| | this PR | main |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py` (GB300) | 117 passed (incl. 3 new) | 114 passed |
| `pre-commit` (ruff-check, ruff-format, typos, mypy, ...) | all hooks pass | |

New test `test_cutedsl_gathered_select_compact_keys_match_reference[16384|131072|1048576]`:
- BF16-valued scores: random, 64 distinct values (so the boundary tie spans hundreds of ids), all negative, padding mixed in, and all tied;
- token ids up to `num_positions - 1`;
- it checks that the default 64-bit key and the compact key (`score_bits=16`, `id_bits=dcp_topk_id_bits(num_positions)`) both select the FP64 reference set.

The server logs show no CuTeDSL JIT compilation during inference with this PR (`jit_monitor_mode=warn`), on GLM-5.3 and on GLM-5.3-Flash (kpool, `max_model_len // 4` id bits). So the new warm-up keys match the runtime keys.

## Details

**Root cause.**
- #61149 made the SM100 MQA logits (`fp8_fp4_mqa_logits`, `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits`) BF16. `sparse_attn_indexer` upcasts them (`as_fp32_logits`) whenever DCP is on.
- `StableTopKFromGatheredCandidatesKernel` builds `score_key << 32 | ~token_id` and runs up to 6 radix passes (11 bits each, the last one 9). It stops at the first pass whose threshold bin fits.
- With FP32 scores, the first 1-2 passes usually resolve the boundary. A BF16 score is complete after the first 16 key bits (passes 1-2), and it often ties at the boundary. The radix then continues:
  - pass 3 sees the 10 low score bits, which are all zero, plus the top id bit;
  - pass 4 sees id bits 30-20, which are constant because ids are below `max_model_len` (16 bits for a 64k context);
  - only passes 5-6 separate the tied candidates.
  - In the passes that separate nothing, every remaining candidate falls into one histogram bin, and the shared-memory atomics serialize on it.

**Fix.**
- `CompileKey` gains `score_bits` and `id_bits`.
- The key is `score_key >> (32 - score_bits)` followed by the low `id_bits` of `~token_id`, packed at the top of the 64-bit word. With BF16 logits and a 64k context, that is 32 bits and 3 passes.
- Padding keys stay 0 and still decode to -1.
- The order is unchanged:
  - the dropped score bits are zero for upcast BF16 values;
  - `~id & mask` preserves the order of ids below `2**id_bits`.
- `sparse_attn_indexer` (DSA) and the GLM-5.3-Flash kpool indexer pass the following:
  - `score_bits=16` when the raw logits are BF16;
  - `id_bits` from `max_model_len`, or `max_pool_len` for kpool pool ids.
  - On a DCP rank whose prefill chunk is empty (no logits to inspect), `score_bits` follows the platform. That keeps it on the warmed-up key. 32 bits would also select correctly.
- Warm-up compiles the SM100 key: 16 score bits, and id bits for `max_model_len // index_kpool`.
- The last radix pass can now be narrower than the 512-thread block. For example, a 30-bit key gives passes of 11, 11 and 8 bits. The bin scan now covers whole block slices; bins at or above `num_bins` stay zero.

**Scope.**
- Only DCP > 1 with BF16 indexer logits (SM100) changes speed. FP32 logits keep 32 score bits.
- DCP = 1 does not run the merge.
- No new host syncs: `score_bits` comes from the logits dtype and the platform, and `id_bits` from `max_model_len`. All three are host-side metadata.
- No new CI step: the new test runs in the existing B200 "V1 Attention" step (`pytest v1/attention`), which has CuTeDSL.

## Why this is not a duplicate

- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search` with "dcp topk", "top-k merge", "indexer dcp", "radix select bf16", "61149", "StableTopKFromGatheredCandidates", "dcp_indexer_cutedsl", "dcp top-k" and "sparse indexer bf16 logits" found no PR that changes the merge selector's key:
  - #47348 (CuTeDSL DCP top-k merge optimizations, before BF16 logits) and #50010 / #50366 (consumer-direct and owner-sharded top-k) restructure the exchange. They do not touch the key layout.
  - #63200, #62172 and #62240 make the local (non-DCP) top-k read BF16 logits. Under DCP, the upcast and this merge stay as they are.
  - #59367 bounds the merge's scratch memory and also edits `_merge_dcp_topk_global`. The changes are independent, and a rebase conflict would be trivial.
- No upstream issue covers it.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to investigate the regression, write the change and its test, and run the benchmarks and evals above. The submitter reviewed every changed line and the measurements.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Don't validate model-built dummy inputs against mm limits
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes engine startup for Pixtral (+ other models with the same problem) when a modality is embedding-only (`--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"<modality>": 0}'` with `--enable-mm-embeds`). This is the root cause of the failure observed in #65648.

## Claims

- Every model registered as of now obeys the contract that #32493 introduced.

## Validation

```shell
vllm serve mistralai/Pixtral-12B-2409 --tokenizer-mode mistral \
    --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 0}' --enable-mm-embeds
```

## Details

#32493 added embedding input for disabled modality. It introduced the following split:

- User inputs are checked against `--limit-mm-per-prompt` and `--enable-mm-embeds` once, in the renderer (`BaseRenderer` calling `info.parse_mm_data`).
- Data the processor builds or re-parses is parsed with `validate=False`. #32493 switched both call sites:
  - the dummy inputs used for profiling (`get_dummy_inputs`)
  - the cache-miss items in `_get_cache_missing_items`

The split is needed because `MultiModalBudget` profiles each embedding-only modality with `mm_counts={modality: 1}` while its limit is 0. A dummy input that gets validated can never pass that check.

4 models including Pixtral override `get_dummy_inputs` and call `self.info.parse_mm_data(dummy_mm_data)` with the default `validate=True`. This PR fixes the processor-side contract violation. Without it, any deployment of these models that relies on embedding-only modalities still crashes at startup, including KV/EC consumers that should receive embeddings.

commits.pr_title: [Model] Add Unlimited-OCR-2 DASH attention support
commits.pr_body:
Add native [Unlimited-OCR-2](https://huggingface.co/baidu/Unlimited-OCR-2) support with DASH sparse attention and page-aware RoPE.

- FlashAttention and FlashInfer for chunked prefill and decode, using Model Runner V2.
- R-SWA retains input KV and bounds output KV to 128 tokens; full decode graphs and opt-in segmented prefill graphs.
- Model-specific preprocessing, decoder construction and optional GPU page-count guard. Shared DeepSeek decoder and scheduler files match main.

<details>
<summary>Usage and limitations</summary>

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 python examples/generate/multimodal/vision_language_multi_image_offline.py \
    --model-type unlimited_ocr2 --num-images 2 --method generate
```

Use `"<PAGE><image>" * len(pages) + "Multi page parsing."` with images in page order, `temperature=0` and `skip_special_tokens=False`. `mm_processor_kwargs={"crop_mode": False}` selects a 1024-square global view. Invalid page/image sequences are rejected before worker execution.

FA is the default; select FI with `attention_config={"backend": "FLASHINFER"}`. The vision encoder falls back from FI to FA. `hf_overrides={"rswa_window": 0}` retains full output KV. Segmented prefill graphs require `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1` and `cudagraph_mode="FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"`; dynamic DASH routing, attention and KV writes remain eager breaks. Whole-prefill FULL graphs are unsupported.

The page-count guard is opt-in through `vllm.model_executor.models.unlimited_ocr2:PageCountGuardLogitsProcessor`; it respects existing sampling masks, preserving EOS when it is the only finite choice. Its `SamplingParams.extra_args` include `page_token_id`, `eos_token_id` and `max_page_tokens` (default 20000; 0 disables the cap).

V1, prefix caching, quantization, PP/CP, LoRA, speculative decoding and KV transfer are unsupported. Validated on GB200/BF16 with prebuilt extensions; clean-build validation remains pending.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Evaluation and validation</summary>

MPDocBench historical full run (before chunked-prefill changes): 420 documents / 3,135 pages, V2. Overall is **84.7407** with the published-client fallback budget and **84.8430** with available-context budgets (paper reference **84.5900**). The latter has no length stops or page-count mismatches. This uses a local evaluation adapter and does not establish identical paper deployment or unpublished per-PDF budgets. MarathonDocBench was cancelled.

The preceding `f5033fd` 4-document / 29-page FA check (B=4, 513-token chunks) retains byte-identical raw and Markdown predictions. Real-weight `pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_unlimited_ocr.py -k 'batched_pages and False' -x -q` passes all 6 FA/FI eager/decode/prefill-graph cases. No new throughput claim.

The [EOS-only guard review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64016#issuecomment-6523759526) is fixed: `allowed_token_ids=[EOS]` previously emitted `[0,0,0,0]`; it now emits exactly `[EOS]` and stops. CPU/GPU retain EOS when masking it would remove the last finite choice. GPU checks run within the existing kernel, stop at the first finite alternative, and perform no host readback. The same FA/FI eager/decode/prefill generation command above covers this case alongside normal OCR content.

Merged main `f1fd044b`. Prefill request metadata is prepared once from existing CPU buffers and shared across decoder layers. The mixed decode/prefill forward fails the CUDA-sync check before this change and passes afterwards with identical output.

**Open review issue:** the excess-marker raw-logit regression remains unresolved; its `atol=0.5, rtol=0` and source are unchanged. A zero-preemption control reproduces a 0.9375 difference at output 123 when comparing B=1 with B=2. A B=2/no-preemption vs B=2/preemption experiment passed FA/FI once, then failed FA with 0.875 on final confirmation, so that test rewrite was discarded. This establishes numerical sensitivity but does not rule out a simultaneous recomputation defect. Reconstructed pre-fix routing still fails (2.75). No passing preemption claim is made for this head. Reproducer: `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_unlimited_ocr.py -k excess_markers -x -q`.

CI compatibility: FA2/3 use paged segment addressing, reduced-layer test configs resize DASH metadata, and vision/cold-shape initialization avoid blocking transfers. On GB200, FA2 real OCR and all 12 FA4/FI eager/decode/prefill-graph generation cases (with/without crops), plus both encoder-pressure cases, pass with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. Hopper FA3 execution, ROCm and clean-build CI remain pending.

</details>

AI-assisted implementation. No duplicate model-support PR found; #57540 concerns generic n-gram sampling.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Run H100 fusion config sweeps and batch invariance nightly only
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Make three H100 steps nightly-only (`optional: true`) to relieve the saturated `mithril-h100-pool` queue: `fusion-e2e-config-sweep-h100`, `fusion-e2e-tp2-ar-rms-config-sweep-h100` and `batch-invariance-h100`. Their AMD mirrors keep running on PRs (`optional: false`, same pattern as `distributed.yaml` / `lora.yaml`).

## Claims

- Frees ~465 of the ~483 GPU-hours/week these steps used on the H100 pool (~10% of `ci`'s H100 GPU-hours). They now run once per nightly instead of on every selected PR and main build.
- No loss of per-PR coverage in either area apart from the H100-specific runs listed under Details.
- No change to AMD scheduling.

## Validation

Data from Oct 27 – Nov 3 2026, collected through the Buildkite REST API for the `ci` pipeline:

| step | GPUs | GPU-h / week | PR jobs passed | PR jobs failed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `batch-invariance-h100` | 1 | 226 | 585 | 0 |
| `fusion-e2e-tp2-ar-rms-config-sweep-h100` | 2 | 207 | 360 | 0 |
| `fusion-e2e-config-sweep-h100` | 1 | 50 | 360 | 0 |

The PR jobs that didn't pass were canceled or `waiting_failed`; none failed.

Generator behavior was checked locally against ci-infra `main` (`eb2d628f`) by loading the edited yaml with `step.parse_steps_from_yaml`, then evaluating `_step_should_run` and `_get_amd_mirror_effective_step` on a PR diff touching `vllm/compilation/` and `vllm/model_executor/determinism/`:
- NVIDIA steps: `optional=True`, so they don't run on a PR and do run with `NIGHTLY=1`.
- AMD mirrors: `optional=False`, so they still run on the PR.

When `ci-selector` is on, `pipeline_generator._selector_decision` removes optional keys from the selector's choice, as on every PR build today; recent decisions show `selector_optional_dropped` of ~148 keys per build. AMD keys stay on the path rules.

`pre-commit run --files .buildkite/test_areas/compile.yaml .buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml` passes.

## Details

Why these steps:
- The H100 pool's p90 queue wait was 46 min that week (p99 115 min), compared with 5–14 min on the H200-slice and B200 queues.
- Each of the three steps had 0 PR failures and has a sibling that still runs per-PR:
  - The fusion sweeps run the full config grid. `fusion-e2e-quick-h100` and `fusion-e2e-tp2-quick-h100` (plus `fusion-e2e-tp2-b200`) still cover fusion on PRs. The B200 sweep (`fusion-e2e-config-sweep-b200`) is already nightly.
  - `batch-invariance-b200` runs on PRs and its commands are a superset of the H100 step's.

What moves to nightly-only:
- **Hopper batch invariance.** The Qwen3-FP8 `FLASH_ATTN` needle test on H100 exercises FA3; on B200 the same test takes a different FlashAttention path.
- **Full H100 fusion sweeps.** Only the quick subsets keep running on H100 per PR.
- PRs can still run these steps through "Run more jobs" or a `ready-run-all-tests` label.
- A PR that edits one of these step definitions still runs it, through the selector's changed-steps rule.

Not in this PR: `replayssm-e2e` is 26.5% of `ci`'s H100 GPU-hours. Narrowing its `source_file_dependencies` would not help, because on 22 of 30 recent PR builds that ran it, `ci-selector` chose it itself (`added-by-coverage`). The remaining 8 were run-all, nightly or explicit builds. Reducing it needs a selector or test-size change, which will be a separate discussion.

Duplicate check: `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search` on "batch invariance nightly", "config sweep nightly", "fusion e2e sweep", "H100 nightly" and "batch-invariance-h100" returned no PR that changes these steps' scheduling.

commits.pr_title: [JIT][ROCm] Fully warmup GLM-5.3-Flash
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

It used to JIT several triton kernels during runtime. This PR
1. registers those kernels for warmup.
2. fixes a bug where even after registering for warmup, triton re-compiled during runtime on ROCm

#### **Explanation for the triton fix:**: 
- Triton on AMD specializes kernels on buffer size being below or above 2GiB, i.e int32 addressable. 
- When <2GiB, this allows the compiler to lower to buffer load/store intrinsics which require 32-bit offsets
- The warmup code previously assumed all buffers passed during warmup were <2GiB. 
- In `kpool_tail_seed_dispatch` we pass the kv cache which can be large. During warmup it specialized on a <2GiB KV cache, whereas at runtime it gets passed a larger KV cache and re-compiles _without_ buffer loads. See https://github.com/ROCm/triton/blob/0ec280cf80dd91e9a86887981a670f2d4541a32b/third_party/amd/backend/compiler.py#L76-L110 for details
- This PR removes that assumption and instead passes the real buffer size

## Claims

- No runtime compilation on GLM-5.3-Flash, i.e. doesn't crash with `--jit-monitor-mode error`

## Validation

Expect lots of runtime compilation on main, none on this branch
```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 \
VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 \
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --max-num-seqs 512 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 \
    --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
    --jit-monitor-mode warn
    --jit-monitor-verbose
```

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."},
      {"role": "user", "content": "Tell me a short joke. Think for 50 tokens before answeing"}
    ],
    "temperature": 0.7,
    "max_tokens": 100
  }'
```

### Main: 53 compile keys and runtime compilation

commits.pr_title: [Test][UMBP] Restore a Mamba2 hybrid end to end through UMBP
commits.pr_body:
- Add a Granite 4.0-H hybrid restore test to `test_mori_token_e2e.py`, run through embedded UMBP.
- Require bitwise-equal tokens and logprobs against a local GPU prefix hit, plus an exact external-hit count.
- Cover a prompt ending mid-block and one ending exactly on a block boundary.

No hybrid model restores through UMBP end to end today. The Nemotron-H GSM8K row never gets a prefix hit because its 1088-token hybrid block is longer than the prompts, so the Mamba boundary-state handoff is only covered with fake runtimes. Mamba hybrids have no batch-invariant kernels, so a cold run can't be the reference, and prompts go one at a time because async load timing changes the batch layout and batched hybrid outputs aren't bitwise stable. On MI350X with MORI v1.2.3.post1 built with UMBP, `pytest -v -s -rs v1/kv_connector/umbp_integration/test_mori_token_e2e.py -k hybrid` passed 10/10 in a loop and the whole file gave 3 passed, but every case fails once the restored Mamba pages are zeroed after the load. The MI355 UMBP integration group already runs this directory, so CI is unchanged. No open UMBP PR (#61795-#61798, #63002, #59276) restores a hybrid end to end, though #63830 and #63670 rework Mamba align mode and may need this test adjusted if they land first.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

commits.pr_title: [Core] Add cache-aware admission ordering
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Within a bounded look-ahead window over the waiting queue, admit requests whose prefix is
already resident in the KV cache ahead of requests that would have to compute theirs.

The problem is an interaction between strict FCFS admission and prefix caching: a cold
request admitted first allocates blocks, and under pressure that allocation evicts blocks
which a request further back in the queue still needs. The eviction turns a would-be cache
hit into recomputation, and the deeper the shared prefix, the more expensive the loss.
Looking a bounded distance ahead lets the scheduler admit the resident request first, so
the cold request's allocation no longer destroys reuse that was about to be collected.

Two new scheduler options, both off by default:

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--cache-aware-admission-window N` | 0 | Look-ahead depth over the waiting queue; 0 admits strictly in arrival order |
| `--cache-aware-admission-threshold F` | 0.0 | KV cache usage below which the window is not applied |

Deliberate limits on scope:

- Reordering is confined to the window, and within it to the slots held by plain
  `WAITING` requests with nothing computed. A request in a blocked status
  (`WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` and friends) or one already partially computed keeps its exact
  position, and nothing is moved past it. This is a reordering among peers, not a change
  in priority.
- It requires the `fcfs` policy. Positional reordering is meaningless in a priority heap —
  `PriorityRequestQueue.prepend_request` re-inserts by priority and ignores position — and
  it would also fight the user's explicit priorities. Under `priority` the feature is
  disabled at construction.
- It requires prefix caching, and is skipped on steps that defer prefill anyway.
- The threshold exists so operators can confine reordering to periods where there are
  evictions worth avoiding. It defaults to 0.0 (always apply) so that setting only the
  window has a visible effect rather than silently doing nothing on a roomy cache.

Scoring uses a new `KVCacheManager.get_num_cached_tokens`, which probes the cache without
taking references, allocating blocks, or emitting events, so it is safe to call for a
request that may not be scheduled. `get_computed_blocks` is unsuitable for this: it emits
`BlockStored` events under `kv_cache_report_mode="full"`, which would publish phantom
events for requests that were only scored.

Cost is one prefix-cache lookup per request in the window per step, plus one linear pass
over the waiting queue when the order actually changes.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

**#53571** (SLO-aware scheduling policy) is the closest existing work and deserves an
explicit comparison, since it also reorders waiting requests. It is keyed on TTFT targets
and prompt length, to stop short prompts queueing behind long prefills; this is keyed on
resident prefix length, to stop cold admissions evicting reusable blocks. Different
signal, different objective, and they could coexist.

The implementations diverge deliberately. #53571 adds a new `SchedulingPolicy` value,
which makes it mutually exclusive with `priority`. This is a bounded per-step re-sort
behind its own flag, so it composes with whatever policy is in force rather than replacing
it. If maintainers would prefer these unified under one policy mechanism, I am glad to
adapt.

Other adjacent open PRs, none overlapping:

- **#54327** (bounded prefix-aware filesystem cache eviction) concerns the KV-offload
  filesystem tier, not admission order.
- **#53772** and **#54348** rework promotion of blocked `skipped_waiting` requests. This
  PR pins non-`WAITING` requests in place, so it composes; the status filter is covered by
  the tests.
- **#45558** (priority-based preemption at `max_num_seqs`) preempts running requests; this
  never preempts.

Checks run (`gh` was not authenticated in my environment, so these were run against the
public search API; the equivalent `gh` invocations are):

```bash
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "cache-aware admission"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "prefix cache admission order"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "waiting queue reorder"
```

## Test Plan

Five new tests in `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`, built on a helper that seeds the
prefix cache with one request's prompt so a later request is genuinely warm:

- `test_cache_aware_admission_prefers_cached_prefix` — the warm request is admitted ahead
  of the cold one that arrived first.
- `test_cache_aware_admission_does_not_look_past_the_window` — a warm request outside the
  window keeps its place in arrival order.
- `test_cache_aware_admission_skipped_below_threshold` — below the usage threshold,
  admission stays in arrival order.
- `test_cache_aware_admission_requires_fcfs_and_prefix_caching[priority, no-caching]` —
  the feature is off under the `priority` policy and with prefix caching disabled.

`create_scheduler` gains `cache_aware_admission_window`, `cache_aware_admission_threshold`
and `policy` parameters.

## Test Result

All green. Commands and results:

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
       tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py               253 passed  (5 new)
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
       tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py \
       tests/v1/core/test_priority_preemption_bug.py      180 passed
```

Environment note: the host for these runs has no `torch`, so tests ran inside the
`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` image (vllm `0.28.1rc1.dev108+g1dc464d42`, torch 2.12.0,
Python 3.12) with this checkout's sources overlaid on the installed package, whose build
is a direct ancestor of this branch. This deviates from the `uv`/`.venv` workflow in
`AGENTS.md`; I intend to re-run under the standard workflow before merge.

A single pytest process over all of `tests/v1/core` is SIGKILLed partway through on this
machine, on `main` as well as on this branch, so the suite was run per-file. Each file
passes on its own.

## Serving results

Kimi-K3 FP4, 8x MI355X, a single engine with DCP=8, replaying an agentic-coding trace.
Interactivity is per-user output speed at the 90th percentile; higher is better.

### 1. Window in isolation (cadence held constant)

The claim attributable to *this* PR. Both arms pin `prefill_schedule_interval=29` and
`sched_stats=1`; the only difference is the admission window. Concurrency 52, 3628s and
3625s, same day a few hours apart.

| `cache_aware_admission_window` | p90 interactivity | tok/s/GPU | server prefix-cache hit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 12.56 | 7,983 | 90.7% |
| 16 | 12.80 (+1.96%) | 8,339 (+4.47%) | 91.5% (+0.8pp) |

A repeat at `window=16` under the identical configuration gives 12.77 and 8,459 tok/s/GPU,
so the direction reproduces. The gain is small and the arms are not repeated enough to put
a tight interval on it; I would describe it as a low-single-digit improvement in both
metrics, with the prefix-cache hit rate moving the way the mechanism predicts — that last
point is what makes the other two deltas credible rather than coincidental.

### 1b. Window in isolation, offload OFF, current nightly

A second measurement on a current nightly (`76c6f3f2`), under a deliberately
stripped-down configuration. Two differences from the table above matter and are not
incidental:

- **KV offload is OFF** (`offload=none`). The measurements above run with KV offload
  (LMCache in the deployed configuration). Offload changes how KV pressure builds, and
  this PR's threshold is defined against KV-cache usage — so the two setups do not
  exercise the window the same way.
- **The cadence option is ABSENT, not held constant.** `prefill_schedule_interval` is
  unset in both arms, so the only non-default scheduler flag in the treated arm is this
  PR's own.

`threshold=0.0`, so the window is always active. Kimi-K3 FP4, 8× MI355X, DCP=8,
`max_num_seqs = 2 × concurrency`, agentic-coding trace, 2029 s per arm.

| concurrency | `cache_aware_admission_window` | p90 interactivity | tok/s/GPU | server prefix-cache hit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 44 | 0 | 15.15 | 10,818 | 94.7% |
| 44 | 16 | 15.53 (+2.53%) | 10,821 (+0.03%) | 94.6% |
| 48 | 0 | 11.50 | 10,384 | 94.2% |
| 48 | 16 | 12.07 (+4.95%) | 10,279 (−1.01%) | 94.2% |

Two control arms run hours apart under identical settings agree to **0.11% on throughput
and 0.19% on p90**, so the interactivity gains are 13–26× the run-to-run noise while the
throughput deltas sit near it.

The interactivity gain is larger at the higher concurrency, where the waiting queue is
deeper (p90 depth 39 at conc 48 versus 34 at conc 44) and there is more for the window to
reorder. **Without offload the prefix-cache hit rate is already ~94%**, leaving little
headroom for the mechanism to improve it — which is likely why it is unchanged here,
against +0.8pp in the offload configuration above.

**Window size matters more than the earlier table suggests.** At `window=64` on this
same configuration, conc 44 loses 12.9% of throughput and 8.6% of p90 interactivity,
with prefix-cache hit falling 94.5% → 93.8% — the mechanism's own target metric
moving backwards. At `window=32` the gain is about half that of 16 (+1.38% p90). Size
the window to the *typical* queue burst, not the maximum, and verify rather than
assume.

### 2. Across concurrency, deployed configuration

The configuration actually deployed enables this PR's window together with
`prefill_schedule_interval` from #54627, against a baseline with both absent. These
figures are for the two options together, not for this change in isolation. LMCache KV
offload, 3600s measured window.

| concurrency | window / interval | baseline p90 interactivity | with both options |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 44 | 64 / 33 | 11.94 | 17.28 (+44.7%) |
| 48 | 64 / 33 | 11.32 | 16.33 (+44.3%) |
| 52 | 64 / 33 | 10.98 | 13.27 (+20.8%) |

Throughput over the same runs is close to unchanged, as expected for a change that
reorders admission rather than removing work: 9,617 to 9,390 tok/s/GPU at concurrency 44
(−2.4%), 10,537 to 10,103 at 48 (−4.1%), and 8,001 to 8,409 at 52 (+5.1%).

### 2b. How the benefit tracks with concurrency

Same two options, measured across the concurrency range rather than at one point.
Each concurrency runs in its own published configuration -- concurrency 44 and 48 use
DCP8 with KV offload and no speculative decoding, 14 and 1 use DCP1 with MTP -- so this
is the benefit in each deployment as it is actually run, not one configuration swept
across load.

| concurrency | baseline | with both options |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 48 | 11.32 | 16.33 (+44.3%) |
| 44 | 11.94 | 17.28 (+44.7%) |
| 14 | 46.65 | 46.79 (+0.3%) |
| 1 | 121.47 | 121.95 (+0.4%) |

The benefit is concentrated at high concurrency and disappears at low concurrency, which
is what both mechanisms predict. Admission ordering only matters when there is a waiting
queue to reorder, and a prefill cadence only matters when prefill and decode are
contending for the same steps. At concurrency 1 and 14 the queue is shallow or empty and
there is little for either option to act on, so the deltas sit at a few tenths of a
percent -- within run-to-run noise, and reported here to show the absence of an effect
rather than to claim one.

### 3. Window sizing

A same-day sweep varying **only** the window, with the prefill cadence and threshold
pinned across all three arms. Concurrency 52, ~3600s per arm.

| `cache_aware_admission_window` | p90 interactivity | tok/s/GPU | prefix-cache hit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 16 | 13.08 | 8,298 | 96.93% |
| 64 | 13.01 | 8,349 | 96.92% |
| 128 | 13.13 | 8,317 | 97.02% |

**The size is immaterial over an 8x range.** p90 spans 13.01-13.13 and throughput
8,298-8,349 — about 1%, inside run-to-run noise on this workload, with no monotonic
trend.

The mechanism explains why. Admission reorders scale 1,220 to 1,581 going from window 16
to 64 and then saturate: 128 gives 1,584, i.e. 0.2% more. This trace's waiting queue
averages about 20 deep and peaks near 70, so a window of 64 already spans it and widening
further has nothing left to reorder.

That also answers the cost question directly: since a larger window buys nothing
measurable, there is no reason to run one. Prefer the smallest window that spans the usual
queue depth. Combined with the threshold defaulting to 0.5, the per-step probe is bounded
both by width and by only running under pressure.

### Input-length coverage

ISL is a property of the agentic workload, not a knob. The trace is replayed
request-for-request, so ISL arrives as a heavy-tailed distribution and every run sweeps
that distribution rather than sitting at one length. Reporting a single "ISL"
number for an agentic trace would be misleading: the mean is roughly 120k tokens, but it
is pulled there by the tail, and the median request is only about 84k.

Per-run distributions, showing what each measurement actually covers:

| run | n | ISL mean | p50 | p75 | p90 | p95 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| conc 44 baseline | 2,462 | 117,173 | 84,644 | 135,675 | 241,476 | 340,419 |
| conc 44 both options | 2,377 | 118,084 | 84,302 | 136,698 | 245,376 | 343,461 |
| conc 48 baseline | 2,567 | 122,854 | 83,905 | 140,551 | 253,786 | 374,550 |
| conc 48 both options | 2,400 | 125,888 | 84,096 | 142,877 | 259,991 | 469,672 |

Three things follow from this that matter for reading the results above:

1. **Coverage.** Each arm spans roughly 84k at the median to 250k at p90, with the top 5%
   reaching 340k-470k. So the reported deltas are already integrated over a 3-5x span of
   input length, not measured at one point on it.
2. **Fairness.** The distributions are closely matched between the arms being compared —
   medians agree within 0.9% and p90s within 2.5% — so the A/B is not confounded by one
   arm drawing easier requests.
3. **Where the options should act.** Admission ordering and prefill cadence matter most
   where prefill work is large relative to a decode step, which is the upper half of this
   distribution. A fixed-ISL sweep at, say, 8k would sit far below the median and would
   not exercise the mechanism this PR targets.

Output lengths are short and similarly matched (median 278-301 tokens, p90 1,738-1,845),
which is what makes interactivity the metric of interest here rather than throughput.

If a fixed-ISL sweep would still be useful, that is a different experiment — synthetic
fixed-length requests rather than trace replay — and I am happy to run it; ISL is simply
not an independent variable in the measurement above.

An earlier revision of this section reported results against the `vllm-simple` KV offload
backend. That backend is no longer what we run.

No accuracy eval was run. Neither the model computation nor sampling is touched; the
change affects only the order in which waiting requests are admitted. Batch composition
does change, as with any scheduling change, so outputs are not bit-identical. I am happy
to run `tests/evals` or a gsm8k pass if reviewers would like that confirmed.

## AI assistance

AI assistance (Cursor) was used to write this change, its tests and this description. I
have reviewed every changed line and can defend the design.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][DSv4.1] Shard the Engram gate so TP ranks gather only the value slice
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

At TP > 1, each DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram layer all-gathers its whole `wkv` output (`[T, 6400]` per rank at TP4) before the fused post kernel. The gate only needs per-token sums over `dim`, so on gfx942 and gfx950 this PR shards `wkv` by `dim` slice. Each rank exchanges its value slice plus eight FP32 partial sums per token in one all-gather (`[T, 1296]`) and finishes the gate locally. CUDA, other ROCm GPUs, TP1 and sequence parallel keep the current path. Engram DP-sharded tables combine with it: DP sharding only changes the row lookup before `wkv`.

## Claims

* DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MI355X, TP4, 12-point sweep: mean TTFT −5.1% on average; long-context TTFT improves 5–8%.
* Per Engram layer at 16384 tokens, the exchange plus post kernel drops from 4.69 ms to 1.13 ms. Under CUDA graphs it is 1.1 µs slower at 1 token and faster from 2 tokens up.
* The math is unchanged apart from FP32 summation order across ranks. GSM8K and NIAH (32k, 64k) scores match `main` within run-to-run noise.
* One collective per Engram layer, as before, with 5× fewer bytes. No new streams or host synchronization.

## Validation

### End-to-end performance

<details>
<summary> Server and client commands </summary>

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 AITER_USE_FLYDSL_MOE_SORTING=1 \
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --async-scheduling --no-enable-log-requests --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --trust-remote-code --language-model-only --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --block-size 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --moe-backend aiter --monokernel
```

The 8k/1k, c=4 point; the others change the lengths, concurrency, prompts, warmups and seed:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.bench_serve --backend vllm --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --port 8000 --dataset-name random --random-range-ratio 0.8 --request-rate inf \
  --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --max-concurrency 4 --num-prompts 32 --warmup-requests 4 --seed 1
```

</details>

| ISL/OSL, concurrency, prompts | mean TTFT (ms), `main` → this PR |
| ----------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| 8k/1k, c=4, 32                | 136 → 130 (−4.5%)                |
| 8k/1k, c=8, 64                | 163 → 153 (−6.3%)                |
| 8k/1k, c=16, 96               | 242 → 227 (−6.3%)                |

| 128k/1k, c=4, 32              | 1,912 → 1,766 (−7.6%)            |
| 128k/1k, c=16, 96             | 3,864 → 3,587 (−7.2%)            |

TTFT improves at 11 of 12 points. Decode saves at most about 33 µs per step (two Engram layers, microbenchmark below), under 1% of TPOT, so TPOT and throughput are not claimed.

### Post-WKV microbenchmark

4 ranks on MI355X through vLLM's TP group, `hc_mult=4`, `dim=5120`. "Gathered" is the current path (all-gather of `[T, 6400]` along dim 1, its re-layout copy, `_fused_engram_post_wkv_kernel`); "sharded" is `RocmEngram._post_wkv`. CUDA-graph rows are the mean of 200 replays of 10 calls; two runs agree within 0.3 µs.

| Tokens | Gathered (µs) | Sharded (µs) | Mode       |
| ------ | ------------- | ------------ | ---------- |
| 1      | 14.3          | 15.4         | CUDA graph |
| 2      | 18.5          | 16.1         | CUDA graph |
| 8      | 24.0          | 16.8         | CUDA graph |
| 64     | 41.7          | 25.2         | CUDA graph |
| 512    | 168.5         | 53.7         | CUDA graph |
| 2048   | 628           | 171          | eager      |
| 16384  | 4,684         | 1,133        | eager      |

### End-to-end accuracy

Same server as the sweep, `lm_eval` 0.4.13. Greedy decoding at concurrency 32 is not batch-invariant, so `main` was run twice to show run-to-run noise.

| Task                           | main (run 1, run 2) | This PR |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------- | ------- |
| GSM8K 5-shot, flexible-extract | 92.27%, 92.80%      | 92.57%  |
| GSM8K 5-shot, strict-match     | 92.19%, 92.80%      | 92.49%  |
| NIAH niah_single_2, 32k        | 97.6%, 97.2%        | 97.4%   |
| NIAH niah_single_2, 64k        | 93.2%, 94.8%        | 95.2%   |

Per sample, against `main` run 1, `main` run 2 flips 67 GSM8K answers and 26/52 NIAH answers (32k/64k); this PR flips 78 and 21/50.

### Tests

`tests/kernels/test_engram.py`: 61 passed, 56 skipped (CUDA-only) on MI355X.

<details>
<summary>Command</summary>

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/test_engram.py
```

</details>

- `test_sharded_engram_loads_and_matches_tp1` builds `RocmEngram` on each simulated TP rank (TP 2 and 4), unquantized and with the model's `DeepseekV4FP8Config` (MXFP8, 32x32 block scales). It loads one fused checkpoint `wkv` through the model's weight loader and checks two things against a TP1 `Engram` loaded from the same checkpoint: each rank's `wkv` output is its column slice of every key and of the value, and `Engram.forward` matches after the exchange.
- `test_sharded_engram_post_wkv_matches_reference` checks the two kernels against the existing reference at TP 2 and 4, with and without a token mask, including `dim=5120` and an empty batch.

CI runs both in `:amd: (MI355) Miscellaneous Kernels`.

## Details

**Why.** In a 16k-token prefill chunk at TP4 on MI355X, each Engram layer spends 3.6 ms on the `[T, 6400]` all-gather and 0.63 ms on its re-layout copy (60k/64, c=16). The same gather takes 1.25 ms on B200.

**How.**

1. `wkv` becomes a `MergedColumnParallelLinear` with output sizes `[dim] * (hc_mult + 1)` and `gather_output=False`, so each rank holds one `dim / tp` slice of every key and of the value. The merged loader shards the fused checkpoint weight, block-32 FP8 scales included.
2. `_engram_gate_partials_kernel` packs, per token, the value slice and `(Σ key², Σ hidden·q·k·key)` over the rank's slice for each hc copy. Hidden states are replicated, so the hidden norm needs no exchange.
3. One `tensor_model_parallel_all_gather` along tokens exchanges those rows.
4. `_engram_gate_finish_kernel` sums the partials over ranks, computes the gate as `_fused_engram_post_wkv_kernel` does, and reads the value rank-major, with no re-layout.

**Decode.** Both paths run three kernels per Engram layer. At 1 token the partials kernel (2.3 µs) sits in front of the latency-bound collective, which leaves the sharded path 1.1 µs behind; from 2 tokens the smaller exchange wins. A 1-token fallback would need a second exchange and post kernel, since the weight layout is fixed at load time, to save about 2 µs per decode step. So there is no token-count threshold.

**Gating.** The ROCm model builds `RocmEngram` (`amd/engram.py`), which overrides two hooks of `Engram`: `_create_wkv` and `_post_wkv`. It shards on gfx942 or gfx950 (`get_cdna_version() in (3, 4)`) at TP > 1 without sequence parallel, and otherwise falls back to `Engram`. CUDA keeps the gathered layout because `nvidia/specialized_decode/engram/prefetch.py` runs `wkv` itself and reads the gathered output. The ROCm mono decode layer (`--monokernel`) calls the `Engram` module unchanged, so it takes the sharded path too. With Engram DP-sharded tables, DP sharding exchanges lookup rows before `wkv`, so it composes with the sharded gate; `EngramBatch` (batched DP lookups) requires TP1 and is unaffected.

**Complexity.** 256 non-comment lines in the new `amd/engram.py` (two Triton kernels, `RocmEngram`), 24 in `common/engram.py` (the two hooks, which move 9 existing lines) and 169 test lines.

**Limitations.** Benchmarked at on gfx950 and gfx942 TP4 only. Not benchmarked with Engram DP-sharded tables at TP > 1.

### Existing PRs

None of the open PRs found by searching for "engram", "wkv" and "engram all-gather" changes the TP layout of the Engram `wkv` output.

* #63326 (draft) runs the Engram WKV chain ahead of the decoder layers on ROCm. It conflicts with this PR in `common/engram.py` and `tests/kernels/test_engram.py`, and its ahead path reads the `ColumnParallelLinear` column split. This PR lands first. On its layout, #63326 keeps pushing each rank's whole `wkv` shard (the gate's dot product needs the layer's hidden states, which are not ready ahead) and only remaps its column offsets.
* #56989 (draft) packs FP8 Engram rows through the smaller `[T, 6, 256]` exchange before `wkv`; it composes with this PR.
* #60938 (draft) fuses the Engram update into the delayed mHC input on CUDA Blackwell TP1.
* #62091 replaces the Engram DP lookup collectives and does not touch the TP path.
