commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fix GPTQ checkpoint loading for PLaMo3
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix GPTQ checkpoint loading for PLaMo3, broken since #54809, by building its `lm_head` as most models do: store `quant_config` on `Plamo3ForCausalLM`, pass it to `lm_head`, and name the head `maybe_prefix(prefix, "lm_head")`.

## Claims

- GPTQ PLaMo3 checkpoints load again. They previously failed with `ValueError: There is no module or parameter named '...g_idx'`.
- PLaMo3's head is named `lm_head`, its state-dict name, instead of `.lm_head`, so quant config entries that name it exactly (e.g. compressed-tensors `ignore` / `targets: ["lm_head"]`) now match it.
- No change for BF16 checkpoints or for GPTQ with `lm_head: false`. Nested prefixes (e.g. `draft_model.lm_head`) are unchanged.

## Validation

Reproducer: `vllm serve` any PLaMo3 checkpoint quantized by GPTQModel, which writes `.g_idx` even with `desc_act=False`. We ran a PLaMo3 31B GPTQ checkpoint (internal) on 1x A100 with the nightly image at 042ab03 (`plamo3.py` is unchanged on current main):

| | Result |
|---|---|
| Before | Engine init fails with the `g_idx` `ValueError` |
| After | Serves; chat and completion requests return correct answers |

Head name matching, run on this branch:

| prefix | `should_ignore_layer(ignore=["lm_head"])` | `find_matched_target(targets=["Linear", "lm_head"])` |
|---|---|---|
| `.lm_head` (before) | `False` | `None` |
| `lm_head` (after) | `True` | `"lm_head"` |

On this branch:

- `pytest tests/model_executor/test_plamo3.py`: 1 passed (CPU-only host). This existing test does not build `Plamo3ForCausalLM` through `__init__`, so it does not cover this change.
- `pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --from-ref upstream/main --to-ref HEAD`: all hooks pass, including mypy.

## Details

**GPTQ loading.** Since #54809, GPTQ layers no longer register `g_idx`, and checkpoint `.g_idx` tensors are dropped by `QuantizationConfig.get_checkpoint_weight_mapper()`. `AutoWeightsLoader` takes this mapper from the first module, among the model and its direct children, that has a `quant_config` attribute. PLaMo3 set none, so the lookup stopped at `lm_head`, which `ParallelLMHead` gives `quant_config=None`, and the `.g_idx` tensors had nowhere to go. Storing `quant_config` on `Plamo3ForCausalLM` fixes the lookup. Passing it to `lm_head` too matches most models (e.g. Qwen3, Llama), and lets a head that the checkpoint quantizes get its quant method instead of always being unquantized (not tested, as we have no such PLaMo3 checkpoint).

**Head name.** `ParallelLMHead`'s `prefix` is the layer's full name in the state dict. `f"{prefix}.lm_head"` gave `.lm_head` for a top-level model, which matches no checkpoint key. Now that `lm_head` receives the quant config, quant methods look the head up by this name, so exact entries for `lm_head` would miss it. Weight loading is unaffected, since it resolves parameters by module path, and the online lm_head copies only carry the prefix over. The PLaMo3 checkpoints we know of do not quantize the head, so this does not change how they load.

No accuracy evaluation: the change only lets the loader drop `.g_idx` and renames the head, so it does not alter compute for any checkpoint that loads. No new test: CI has no GPTQ PLaMo3 checkpoint, a unit test for the loader lookup would need heavy stubbing, and checking the head name alone is trivial. No duplicate: among open PRs mentioning PLaMo3, `g_idx`, or `lm_head` quantization, only #45535 edits `plamo3.py`, and it passes `quant_config` to `embed_tokens` only, which neither the loader lookup (model and direct children) nor `lm_head` depends on. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; the submitter reviewed all changes and ran the tests.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Fix host-buffer h2d sync overwriting received KV
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With `kv_buffer_device="cpu"`, `sync_recved_kv_to_device` overwrites D's received KV with host pages NIXL never filled, for models with several KV cache groups or KV-sharing layers. Each group now copies only its own layers' host buffers; the multi-group case regressed in #53780.

## Claims

- With host buffers, D keeps the received KV for models with several KV cache groups or KV-sharing layers.
- Each layer of a transfer group is still copied once per request, as after #54483; KV-sharing layers are no longer copied.

## Validation

CPU, this PR (`a42440c748`) on main `a70e48deba`:
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py -k test_sync_recved_kv_copies_each_group_own_layers`: #54483's parametrized test now checks which layers and block ids each h2d copy gets, with a KV-sharing layer added. All 3 rows fail on main; with this PR they pass. The rest of `test_nixl_connector_hma.py`, `test_nixl_connector.py` and `test_nixl_push_connector.py` has the same pass/fail set as main.
- A local byte-level check runs real `allocate_kv_cache` tensors, `save_kv_to_host`, NIXL replayed between host buffers and `sync_recved_kv_to_device` on toy models at TP 1/1 and 2/2. On main, D's KV differs from P's in all 16 multi-group cases, which mix sliding-window and full-attention layers, and matches in all 4 full-attention-only cases. With this PR it matches in all 20.

GB10, Gemma-4-E2B-it, which has sliding-window and full-attention groups and 20 KV-sharing layers, P TP1 → D TP1, main `8530a778f7` without and with this PR (`a42440c748`, merged): with `kv_buffer_device="cpu"` on both sides, main's outputs differ from the same run with device buffers in all 4 prompts; with this PR all 4 are identical, logprobs bitwise equal.

<details>
<summary>GB10 runs</summary>

| | identical to device buffers | max \|Δlogprob\| per prompt |
|---|---|---|
| main `8530a778f7` | 0/4 | 3.27, 0.81, 3.74, 2.02 |
| this PR `a42440c748` merged with main `8530a778f7` | 4/4 | 0, 0, 0, 0 |

Both runs, P and D: `--attention-backend TRITON_ATTN --enforce-eager --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --block-size 64 --no-enable-prefix-caching --num-gpu-blocks-override 2048`, greedy, 4 code prompts of 1100–1300 tokens; D read 4880 tokens over NIXL. Host-buffer runs add `"kv_buffer_device": "cpu"` on both sides; both logged `use_host_buffer: True`.
</details>

## Details

On D, with `kv_buffer_device="cpu"`:

1. NIXL READ writes into D's per-layer host buffers. Each host buffer is its own region, and since #53780 each group's descriptors cover only its own regions, so a layer's host buffer is filled only at its own group's blocks. Layers that reuse another layer's KV cache have host buffers but no transfer group, so NIXL never fills them.
2. `sync_recved_kv_to_device` copies the host buffers into the device tensors, which layers of different KV cache groups share, as does a KV-sharing layer with its target.
   - Main copies every layer's host buffer at all groups' blocks, so unfilled host pages overwrite the other groups' received blocks. A KV-sharing layer, copied after its target, overwrites the target's received KV, even with one group.
   - This PR copies each group's layers at that group's blocks only.

The byte-level check matches in all 10 multi-group cases that build at #53780's parent and differs in all 10 at #53780.

`save_kv_to_host` still copies every layer for all groups' blocks; NIXL never reads the extra host pages.

#59037, a 60-file draft for hidden-state extraction with packed layouts, contains the same per-group copy; this PR is the standalone fix.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Distributed] Keep cross-node MNNVL groups off CUDA IPC all-reduce
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Addresses #52778: prevent cross-node MNNVL TP groups from entering node-local CUDA IPC all-reduce or graph-buffer registration, while retaining eligible MNNVL all-gather/reduce-scatter.

Updated against upstream main `08e3f264` following [the maintainer's request to resolve conflicts and run CI](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55835#issuecomment-6375569508). This synchronization preserves the reviewed guards; the PR diff is unchanged from the patch reviewed by the submitter.

## Claims

- Reject the CUDA IPC paths only for cross-node TP groups.
- Preserve same-node TP eligibility and existing topology/tensor checks; the wider DP/EP group does not determine this guard.
- Preserve upstream batch-invariance, capture-registration, fused-mHC, and newer multicast support changes.

## Validation

### November 1 CI refresh

Merged current `main` to include [the upstream benchmark header-casing fix, #63462](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63462). The complete PR patch relative to main retains the same stable patch fingerprint; no MNNVL guard or PR-specific test logic was changed.

With CI-pinned `aiohttp==3.14.5`, `multidict==7.1.0`, and `yarl==1.25.1`, restoring the old `dict(request.headers)` capture reproduces `KeyError: 'x-request-id'`. Restoring the upstream `request.headers.copy()` fix makes the full Responses benchmark test module pass: **30 passed**. This is an upstream test fix incorporated through the main merge, not a new change added by this PR.

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_responses_request_func.py -v
```

Latest local checks on macOS arm64, Python 3.12.11, PyTorch 2.13.0:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Custom-all-reduce suite | 59 passed, 8 GPU tests skipped |
| Adjacent communication suites | 32 passed, 4 GPU tests skipped, 10 distributed tests deselected |
| Scoped pre-commit, including Ruff, mypy and test tethering | Passed |
| Scoped whitespace check and independent merge-preservation review | Passed |

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_custom_all_gather_reduce_scatter.py tests/distributed/test_comm_ops.py -k 'not multi_process' -v
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/distributed/device_communicators/custom_all_reduce.py tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py
git diff --check origin/main HEAD -- vllm/distributed/device_communicators/custom_all_reduce.py tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py
```

The submitter confirmed reviewing the patch. The commands above were executed by Codex at the submitter's explicit direction; they are not represented as personally human-executed tests. Existing PyTorch warnings and an unchanged partial-test-object destructor warning remain; none were suppressed.

These are inherited CPU diagnostics with mocked GPU/process-group boundaries, not new hardware or serving-E2E validation. The reporter's [matched GB200 cross-node validation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55835#issuecomment-5587236720) applies to the earlier patch/baseline. No new GB300, same-node GPU control, AG/RS GPU regression, or model-output evaluation is claimed for this synchronization.

Still outstanding:
- [ ] Personally human-run relevant test confirmation.
- [ ] Same-node GPU controls, GPU AG/RS coverage and model-output evaluation.
- [ ] Remaining real-entry-point regression/documentation requirements and final CI/merge readiness.

Upstream CI has been requested using the maintainer-authorized `/ci run` workflow. CI status is separate from the local results above.

## Details

`CustomAllreduce` receives the TP group's CPU process group. `mnnvl_only` is the inverse of that group's same-node probe, so a node-local TP4 group remains eligible even in a DP4/EP16 deployment. The optional naming suggestion has not been folded into this merge-only refresh.

No new CUDA kernels, arithmetic changes, skipped assertions, relaxed tolerances, or CI-policy changes were introduced.

<details>
<summary>Earlier investigation, duplicate-work checks and validation history (earlier baselines)</summary>

## Purpose

Addresses #52778.

**Reporter-provided multi-node GPU validation is available below; same-node GPU controls and model-output evaluation remain pending.** Local validation uses CPU tests only; this PR does not claim submitter-run GPU tests.

Cross-node MNNVL-capable groups remain enabled for custom all-gather/reduce-scatter, but cannot exchange node-local CUDA IPC handles. `should_custom_ar()` currently admits TP=2 cross-node groups; CUDA-graph teardown can subsequently exchange their IPC handles and terminate the process inside `cudaIpcOpenMemHandle`.

This patch:

- declines node-local custom all-reduce when `mnnvl_only=True`, allowing the existing caller dispatch to try another backend;
- skips IPC graph registration for those groups, whose MNNVL collectives use pre-registered symmetric memory;
- preserves same-node custom all-reduce and the existing MNNVL all-gather/reduce-scatter eligibility;
- adds regression coverage in the existing custom-all-reduce test suite.

No CUDA kernels or arithmetic implementations are changed.

## Why this is not duplicate work

Before starting, #52778 had no assignee or visible work claim. Issue/timeline checks and open-PR searches for the issue number, cross-node IPC, MNNVL custom allreduce, `mnnvl_only`, and `register_graph_buffers` found no open implementation of this specific fix. The issue-number and `mnnvl_only` searches were repeated before opening this PR.

Related changes address different mechanisms:

- Merged #53253 prevents unsupported cross-node groups from reaching MNNVL rendezvous; its description explicitly distinguishes #52778. Supported Blackwell groups still reach the paths changed here.
- Open #53377 concerns FlashInfer fusion-workspace capability checks.
- Open #46515 concerns IPC-handle lifetime rather than cross-node eligibility.
- Open #50505 changes buffer sizing for batch invariance rather than node locality.

## Test Plan

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/distributed/test_custom_all_gather_reduce_scatter.py \
  tests/distributed/test_comm_ops.py -k 'not multi_process' -v
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/device_communicators/custom_all_reduce.py \
  tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py
git diff --check
```

## Test Result

Executed locally on Apple Silicon macOS with Python 3.12.11 and PyTorch 2.13.0:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| New regression tests with unpatched production code | 3 failed, 13 passed, 4 GPU tests skipped |
| Patched custom-all-reduce suite | 16 passed, 4 GPU tests skipped |
| Adjacent communication suites | 19 passed, 1 GPU test skipped, 10 distributed tests deselected |
| Applicable pre-commit hooks, including Ruff and mypy | Passed |
| Diff whitespace check | Passed |

The three baseline failures cover eager/captured cross-node all-reduce dispatch and cross-node IPC graph registration. Positive controls cover same-node registration and MNNVL collective eligibility.

These tests exercise real production Python methods and CPU tensors, with CUDA operations and process-group calls mocked at the boundaries. They do not execute CUDA IPC, NCCL, or MNNVL kernels. The precompiled editable install was unavailable on this host; the Python tests ran through normal source imports after installing dependencies with `uv`.

## Outstanding validation

- [ ] Human-run relevant tests and final line-by-line review under the contribution policy.
- [x] Reporter-validated matched unpatched/patched startup, CUDA-graph capture, and serving benchmarks on two MNNVL-capable GB200 NVL72 nodes with TP=2.
- [ ] Same-node TP=2 control and GPU all-gather/reduce-scatter regression run.
- [ ] Model-output/evaluation results for the serving-backend change.

**External GPU validation: the issue reporter confirmed the fix on September 8, 2026.** See [the full validation report](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55835#issuecomment-5587236720). On two GB200 NVL72 nodes with one GPU per node, cross-node TP=2, and custom all-reduce left enabled, the unpatched control aborts with `custom_all_reduce.cuh:143`. Applying this patch as the only change allows CUDA-graph capture, server startup, and serving benchmarks at concurrency 1/16/64/128 to complete. The reporter also confirmed that MNNVL setup remains active.

The submitter still has no GPU environment. Same-node GPU controls, GPU all-gather/reduce-scatter regression runs, model-output accuracy evaluation, and the remaining human-review requirements have not been reported as complete.

## AI assistance

OpenAI Codex assisted with issue triage, investigation, patch preparation, and execution of the local CPU tests and lint checks. The patch was approved for publication by the submitter. The outstanding checklist is intentionally incomplete. External GPU results above are attributed to the issue reporter; they do not attest to submitter-run GPU tests, model-output accuracy evaluation, or completion of the remaining human-review requirements. The commit includes AI attribution and sign-off.


## Main synchronization — September 23, 2026

Merged upstream `main` (`0f2a15c9`) without rewriting the original validated commit. Resolved the test-file insertion conflict by retaining both the PR's CPU fixture/regressions and upstream's new SM100 fused-mHC GPU regression.

- Production file is byte-for-byte unchanged from the prior PR head; all existing PR test/helper functions and both new upstream mHC functions are AST-identical to their respective originals.
- Custom-all-reduce suite: **16 passed, 5 GPU tests skipped**.
- Adjacent communication suites with `-k 'not multi_process'`: **20 passed, 1 GPU test skipped, 10 distributed tests deselected**.
- Changed-file pre-commit checks (including Ruff, mypy and test tethering), scoped whitespace checks, and independent resolution review passed.
- No GPU/model evaluation was rerun for this synchronization. Prior hardware results remain attributed to the reporter's original patch validation.

## CI status (original PR head)

The failing [`pre-run-check`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/34190799792/job/101948293711) is the repository's CI authorization gate, not a lint/test result. It requires one of `verified`, `ready`, or `ready-run-all-tests`, or at least four merged PRs from the author; the log reports one merged PR and no qualifying label. The actual `pre-commit` job was therefore skipped. GitHub's ready-for-review status is distinct from those authorization labels. Local changed-file pre-commit checks passed as reported above; upstream CI remains unexecuted behind that gate. No CI policy or authorization controls were modified.

</details>

---

commits.pr_title: [Model] Add ZAYA1 support
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds native support for Zyphra's ZAYA1 models (`ZayaForCausalLM`: [ZAYA1-8B](https://huggingface.co/Zyphra/ZAYA1-8B), [ZAYA1-74B-preview](https://huggingface.co/Zyphra/ZAYA1-74B-preview)), with `zaya` tool and reasoning parsers. Closes #42286.

This builds on Zyphra's #41999 (thanks @yury-tokpanov and the Zyphra team), reimplemented against current `main`: it reuses the Transformers `ZayaConfig`, the existing Mamba state and `ShortConv` metadata for CCA, `FusedMoEFactory`, and the `Qwen3Parser` grammar, so it adds ~870 lines (≈600 for the model) instead of ~2.8k, and needs no changes to shared MoE/Mamba/config code.

## Claims

- `ZayaForCausalLM` matches Transformers in float32 (greedy-exact on 8B; logprobs on a 5.2k-token 74B prompt) and runs with chunked prefill, prefix caching, CUDA graphs, TP, EP and online FP8.
- CCA state handling has no host syncs and no per-request loop (`VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` passes).
- `--tool-call-parser zaya --reasoning-parser zaya` parse ZAYA's `<zyphra_tool_call>` calls, including calls that end reasoning without `</think>`. `zaya_xml` is an alias matching the model cards.

## Validation

**Tests** (B300):

```bash
pytest tests/models/language/generation/test_hybrid.py -k zaya   # 1 passed
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_zaya_tool_parser.py                 # 3 passed
pytest tests/models/test_initialization.py tests/models/test_registry.py -k Zaya  # 2 passed
```

`test_zaya_cca_state` builds a random tiny ZAYA1 (full and sliding-window layers) and compares vLLM against Transformers in fp32 with chunked prefill (`max_num_batched_tokens=32`) and prefix caching (cold pass, then cached pass). It fails if decode history, prefill/prefix-cache history, or the delayed value state is dropped (each mutation checked). The released tiny checkpoints (`tiny-random/zaya1`) predate the released config format, so the test builds its own.

**Correctness vs Transformers**

| Model | Setting | Result |
|---|---|---|
| ZAYA1-8B | fp32, 3 prompts × 60 greedy tokens, single and batched | 60/60 each |
| ZAYA1-74B-preview | fp32, TP=2, prompt logprobs over 5,200 tokens (past the 4,097 sliding window) | mean \|Δlogp\| 2.2e-4; 6 tokens > 0.05 (max 0.21); max after token 4097: 0.0009 |

Transformers' own one-shot vs chunked prefill differs by up to 0.77 logprob on 8B: the hard top-1 router flips experts on near-ties (203 of 104k routing decisions on a 2.6k-token prompt), so bf16 and long-prompt greedy outputs are not token-exact across implementations or batch shapes. vLLM's deviations land on the same positions.

**Eval** (GSM8K, chat, `--reasoning-parser zaya`, temperature 1.0 / top-p 0.95 per the model card, 16k max tokens):

| Model | GPUs | Accuracy | Invalid | Mean output tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ZAYA1-8B | 1× B300 | 0.893 | 0.001 | 2,315 |
| ZAYA1-74B-preview | 1× B300 | 0.893 | 0.001 | 1,085 |

Full 1,319-question test set, single run with `--seed 0`. The model cards report no GSM8K score, so this checks end-to-end serving health rather than reproducing a published number.

```bash
vllm serve Zyphra/ZAYA1-8B --max-model-len 32768 --reasoning-parser zaya
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --use-chat-completions --max-tokens 16384 \
    --temperature 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --seed 0 --num-shots 0 --request-timeout-seconds 7200
```

**Other runs** (ZAYA1-8B): TP=2; EP (`--data-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel`) with a parsed tool call and a `json_schema` response after reasoning over `/v1/chat/completions`; `--quantization fp8`; default prefix caching (4,752 of 4,756 prompt tokens hit, cached output identical to cold).

## Details

- **CCA** (Compressed Convolutional Attention) mixes q/k with a two-stage causal conv over the current and two previous tokens, and takes half of v from the previous token's projection. Each layer keeps the last two raw q/k rows and the previous delayed value as Mamba state, reusing `ShortConvAttentionMetadata` (only per-request slots and query offsets are needed). Most tokens go through one conv over the flattened batch; only each request's first two tokens are recomputed against their saved history.
- **Router**: MLP router over `num_experts + 1` classes (the extra one skips the experts), with balancing biases and the previous layer's router state (EDA). Routing runs in the model and is passed to `FusedMoEFactory` through `custom_routing_function`. The weights slice is made contiguous: MoE kernels ignore the stride of a `[:, :topk]` view of the packed routing tensor and read token IDs as weights.
- Attention, CCA and router projections are replicated across TP ranks (2 KV heads); experts are TP/EP-sharded, as in #41999.
- Not supported: speculative decoding (raises), pipeline parallel, LoRA, EPLB.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm][Qwen4Exp] Remap Quark layer names for the MTP draft model
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Previously, `amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4` with MTP would fail with `RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (1280) must match the size of tensor b (2560)`.

Remap Quark's layer names (`exclude`, `layer_quant_config`) for the Qwen4Exp MTP draft (both AMD and NVIDIA copies) so that checkpoint names (`mtp.layers.0.*`) match the draft's layer names (`mtp.layers.48.*`), the same way `ignored_layers`, `exclude_modules` and ModelOpt `quantized_layers` are already remapped (#55513) in both copies.

Related checkpoint fix:https://huggingface.co/amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4/commit/89d245391842bf53fb9b0700646843c1f40de341.

**Checkpoint status:** AMD has updated `config.json` on both `amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4` and the `-PLEFP8` sibling with literal `mtp.layers.0.*` names only -- no catch-all regex -- matching the convention other AMD checkpoints use (e.g. `amd/Qwen3.5-397B`). Per AMD's confirmation on the checkpoint discussion linked above and the model card's own Reproduction section: without MTP, the formal `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.32.0` release runs the checkpoint as documented; with MTP enabled, that release does not remap Quark's exclude list for the draft, so this PR is required for MTP to load at all -- this is the checkpoint as shipped, not a hypothetical variant.

## Claims

- Bug fix: with a Quark checkpoint whose `exclude` list names MTP modules by checkpoint index (the form Quark exports), BF16 MTP layers are no longer built as quantized layers.
- Per-layer Quark schemes (`layer_quant_config`) for MTP modules are applied to the draft as well.
- No functional change for the target model, for no-MTP serving, or for ModelOpt checkpoints.
- Also fixes the identical bug on the NVIDIA backend: MXFP4 has real NVIDIA-native MoE backends (FlashInfer, vLLM CUTLASS, DeepGEMM, Marlin -- not just AMD's AITER path), so a Quark-quantized checkpoint with MTP hit the same dead-exclude-list bug there. Flagged by @okorzh-amd's review; same fix, ported to `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/mtp.py`.
- Scope: entries in Quark `exclude` and keys of `layer_quant_config` that **start with** `mtp.layers.<i>.` (for `i < mtp_num_hidden_layers`) are rewritten to `mtp.layers.<mtp_start_layer_idx + i>.`; this includes globs such as `mtp.layers.0.*`. Entries that start with `re:` or `*`, and non-MTP names, are left exactly as written, matching the existing `ignored_layers`/`exclude_modules`/`quantized_layers` remaps.

## Validation

**Unit test (CPU)**

```bash
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_config.py   # 15 passed
```

`test_qwen4_exp_mtp_remaps_quark_layer_names`, parametrized over `backend` (`amd`/`nvidia`, matching the existing `test_qwen4_exp_mtp_remaps_mixed_precision_layer_indices` convention), builds the draft config from a `QuarkConfig` and checks that MTP names in `exclude` and `layer_quant_config` shift to layer 48, non-MTP and `re:` entries are unchanged, and the checkpoint's list is not mutated. It also asserts the actual `get_quant_method_target` decision for the draft's routed experts (`UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod`, not the quantized MoE method), using an `exclude` fixture whose only regex entry (`re:mtp\.fc_hidden`) does not match the experts path on its own -- a broader catch-all regex would mask the bug this assertion exists to catch (see Scope above). Verified locally (and re-verified by removing the `apply_vllm_mapper` call on both backends) that the exclude-list assertion is what catches the bug: it fails cleanly without the fix and passes with it, on both backends.

**End to end (MI355X, TP2)**

Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-5555a2d8f7` with this PR. Checkpoint `amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4`. GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 questions; acceptance length (AL) over the GSM8K run, MTP k=3. Also confirmed on NVIDIA B300: this fix resolves the identical error with similar results to the MI355X run below. B300 additionally needed an out-of-scope workaround for a separate Quark/Qwen4Exp weight-conversion gap with the CUTLASS_MXFP4_MXFP4 MoE backend, tracked separately and not part of this PR; the NVIDIA fix itself is also covered by the parametrized unit test above, same code path as the AMD side.

| Checkpoint `exclude` | Without this PR | With this PR |
|---|---|---|
| exact MTP module names only (as Quark exports) | fails to load: `RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (1280) must match the size of tensor b (2560)` | loads; GSM8K 0.923 / 0.916; AL 3.52 (0.928 / 0.845 / 0.748) |

GSM8K is flexible-extract / strict-match (±0.007); AL per draft position in parentheses. With exact names only, the server log reports `Quark excludes shared experts at mtp.layers.48.mlp.shared_expert`, i.e. the checkpoint's `mtp.layers.0.*` entries now reach the draft.

No-MTP reference on the same setup: GSM8K 0.927 / 0.921 (flexible / strict).

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
vllm serve amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4 --served-model-name qfn \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --no-enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'

lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=qfn,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --apply_chat_template --fewshot_as_multiturn
```

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** The AMD Qwen4Exp draft builds its layers as `mtp.layers.<num_hidden_layers + i>`, while checkpoints name them `mtp.layers.<i>`. `_make_draft_vllm_config` shifts the checkpoint names in `ignored_layers`, `exclude_modules` and `quantized_layers`, but `QuarkConfig` keeps its layer names inside `quant_config` (`exclude`, `layer_quant_config`), which was not touched. Every literal MTP entry there was dead for the draft, so `QuarkConfig.get_quant_method` fell through to the global scheme (MXFP4) for BF16 MTP modules.

**Fix.** Rename them through Quark's existing hook for this, `QuarkConfig.apply_vllm_mapper`, with a `WeightsMapper` prefix map `mtp.layers.<i>.` -> `mtp.layers.<num_hidden_layers + i>.`. The mapper is built in the draft rather than declared as a class-level `hf_to_vllm_mapper` because the target index depends on `num_hidden_layers`.

**Why keep the layer offset.** Qwen3-Next removed the same offset in #25079 and Qwen3.5 builds its MTP layer as `mtp.layers.{idx}` (#34110), so their checkpoint names match without a remap. Qwen4Exp's offset (introduced with the model in #53896) is now relied on: #60023 documents `--kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers 48` to keep only the MTP layer's KV cache unquantized, and that option selects layers by index; the offset also keeps index-keyed PLE layer assignment (`ple_layer_ids`) off the draft. Renumbering would change both silently, so this PR keeps the offset and completes the existing remap.

**Scope.** AMD and NVIDIA Qwen4Exp MTP drafts; Quark only.

**Related.** Not duplicated by: #49900 (strips the synthetic `draft_model.` root for draft-model drafters), #59040 (`mtp.fc` in `qwen3_5_mtp.py`).

**CI.** The unit test runs on CPU in the existing Qwen4Exp test file. The end-to-end validation above was run outside CI.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this change.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Count reasoning_content deltas as streamed outputs in chat
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Some servers, like SGLang, send reasoning tokens in a field called `reasoning_content`. vLLM uses `reasoning`. Since #62341, the chat benchmark client only looks for `reasoning`, so it skips SGLang's reasoning tokens.

Two things go wrong:
- TTFT is measured to the first answer token instead of the first reasoning token, so it looks much slower than it really is.
- A response that ends before the model starts answering is counted as failed.

This PR makes the client accept `reasoning_content` too.

## Claims

- TTFT is measured to the first reasoning token again, as it was before #62341. A stub streaming SGLang's chunks went from 842 ms to 205 ms, against a true 201 ms.
- Reasoning-only responses go from 0/20 to 20/20 successful.
- No change for vLLM's own server, which streams `reasoning`.

## Validation

Two tests added to `tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py`: reasoning followed by an answer (TTFT and ITL), and a reasoning-only stream (success). Both are parametrized over `reasoning` / `reasoning_content` and both clients. 46 passed. The 4 `reasoning_content` cases fail on `main` (`assert 1 == (4 - 1)` and "Never received a valid chunk to calculate TTFT"). pre-commit passes.

End to end: `vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat`, 20 prompts, concurrency 4, against a local stub that streams SGLang's chunk sequence. The stub sends its first output at 200 ms, then 30 reasoning and 10 answer tokens 20 ms apart, and logs its own send times. Two runs each:

| | `main` | this branch | stub's send log |
|---|---|---|---|
| mean TTFT | 843 / 841 ms | 206 / 205 ms | first reasoning token ≈ 201 ms |
| reasoning-only, successful | 0 / 20 | 20 / 20 | 30 tokens sent per request |

<details><summary>Stub server and command</summary>

`stub_sglang_server.py` sends the same chunk sequence as SGLang's streaming chat endpoint, with fixed timings, and logs when it sent the first reasoning and answer tokens:

```python
"""Minimal stub of SGLang's streaming chat endpoint, for integration-testing a client.

It reproduces the chunk sequence SGLang streams as of sgl-project/sglang 504f9cf
(sse_utils.py StreamDelta/StreamChoice, omit_defaults=True; serving_chat.py):
  opening chunk  delta {"role": "assistant", "content": "", "reasoning_content": null},
                 sent when the first engine output arrives
  reasoning      delta {"reasoning_content": "..."}          (no `content` key)
  answer         delta {"content": "...", "reasoning_content": null}
  finish         delta {"reasoning_content": null}, finish_reason set
  usage          "choices": [] plus "usage"
Every choice carries logprobs, finish_reason and matched_stop, as StreamChoice serializes them.
It uses fixed, known timings and logs server-side send times per request as ground truth.

Usage: python stub_sglang_server.py --port 18731 --log ground_truth.jsonl
Binds to 127.0.0.1 only.
"""

import argparse
import asyncio
import json
import time

from aiohttp import web


def _chunk(delta: dict, finish_reason=None) -> bytes:
    # StreamChoice always serializes logprobs, finish_reason and matched_stop.
    choice = {
        "index": 0,
        "delta": delta,
        "logprobs": None,
        "finish_reason": finish_reason,
        "matched_stop": None,
    }
    body = {
        "id": "chatcmpl-stub",
        "object": "chat.completion.chunk",
        "created": int(time.time()),
        "model": "stub",
        "choices": [choice],
    }
    return f"data: {json.dumps(body)}\n\n".encode()


def _usage_chunk(usage: dict) -> bytes:
    # SGLang's final usage chunk carries no choices (serving_chat.py ~2792-2796).
    body = {
        "id": "chatcmpl-stub",
        "object": "chat.completion.chunk",
        "created": int(time.time()),
        "model": "stub",
        "choices": [],
        "usage": usage,
    }
    return f"data: {json.dumps(body)}\n\n".encode()


def make_app(args) -> web.Application:
    log = open(args.log, "a", buffering=1)

    async def chat(request: web.Request) -> web.StreamResponse:
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        await request.json()
        resp = web.StreamResponse(headers={"Content-Type": "text/event-stream"})
        await resp.prepare(request)

        sent = {}
        # SGLang sends the opening role chunk when the first engine output arrives.
        await asyncio.sleep(args.first_token_ms / 1000)
        await resp.write(_chunk({"role": "assistant", "content": "", "reasoning_content": None}))
        for i in range(args.reasoning_tokens):
            if i:
                await asyncio.sleep(args.itl_ms / 1000)
            await resp.write(_chunk({"reasoning_content": f"r{i} "}))
            sent.setdefault("first_reasoning_s", time.perf_counter() - t0)
        for i in range(args.answer_tokens):
            await asyncio.sleep(args.itl_ms / 1000)
            await resp.write(_chunk({"content": f"a{i} ", "reasoning_content": None}))
            sent.setdefault("first_answer_s", time.perf_counter() - t0)
        n = args.reasoning_tokens + args.answer_tokens
        # Finish chunk: build_sse_content(finish_reason=...) gives delta {"reasoning_content": null}.
        await resp.write(
            _chunk({"reasoning_content": None}, finish_reason="stop" if args.answer_tokens else "length")
        )
        await resp.write(_usage_chunk({"prompt_tokens": 8, "completion_tokens": n, "total_tokens": 8 + n}))
        await resp.write(b"data: [DONE]\n\n")
        log.write(json.dumps({**sent, "tokens": n}) + "\n")
        return resp

    async def models(_request: web.Request) -> web.Response:
        return web.json_response({"object": "list", "data": [{"id": "stub", "object": "model"}]})

    app = web.Application()
    app.router.add_post("/v1/chat/completions", chat)
    app.router.add_get("/v1/models", models)
    return app


if __name__ == "__main__":
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=18731)
    p.add_argument("--log", default="ground_truth.jsonl")
    p.add_argument("--first-token-ms", type=float, default=200.0)
    p.add_argument("--reasoning-tokens", type=int, default=30)
    p.add_argument("--answer-tokens", type=int, default=10)
    p.add_argument("--itl-ms", type=float, default=20.0)
    a = p.parse_args()
    web.run_app(make_app(a), host="127.0.0.1", port=a.port, print=None)
```

Run it, then benchmark it:

```bash
python stub_sglang_server.py --port 18731 &
vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --base-url http://127.0.0.1:18731 \
  --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --model stub --tokenizer Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 16 --random-output-len 40 \
  --num-prompts 20 --max-concurrency 4
```

For the reasoning-only case, start the stub with `--answer-tokens 0`.

</details>

## Details

SGLang streams reasoning only as `reasoning_content`; its reasoning deltas carry no `content` key (`StreamDelta` in `sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/sse_utils.py`). It fixed the same issue in its own benchmark client (sgl-project/sglang#23954). The Rust `vllm-bench` ports in #64626/#64627 have the same gap; I'll note it there.

No issue or PR covers this. #64703 edits the same file on different lines and applies independently.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to find this and write the change and tests. I reviewed every line and ran the tests and the end-to-end comparison.

cc @DarkLight1337, who reviewed #62341.

commits.pr_title: [Core] Handle new requests and aborts while waiting for model output
commits.pr_body:
With the multiproc executor, the engine core thread waits for each step's output by busy-polling the workers' response queues. New requests that arrive in the meantime sit in the input queue until the step completes, which with async scheduling is up to a full step later than necessary.

Instead, poll for the step's output without blocking and handle `ADD` and `ABORT` inputs from the input queue as they arrive. Any other input (e.g. a utility call) ends this early handling: it and all inputs after it are processed once the step completes, preserving their order.

Requests then reach the scheduler, and the KV connector's `on_new_request()`, up to a step earlier. This gives connectors with asynchronous lookups (e.g. external KV cache stores) a head start before the request is scheduled.

It also moves more work off of the CPU critical path.

The uniproc executor is unchanged, TBD about extending for this too.

commits.pr_title: [Recipe] Kimi-K3.1-Pro: pin Docker images, drop pip, add Rubin VR200
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #65684. The Kimi-K3.1-Pro recipe named its day-0 images only in an install note, so the builder's commands used `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` on NVIDIA. This pins the images, hides the pip tab, and adds Vera Rubin (VR200) with its CUDA 13.4 image.

## Claims

| Hardware | Image before | Image after |
|---|---|---|
| GB300, B300 | `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` | `vllm/vllm-openai:kimi-k31` |
| VR200 (new, `supported`) | not offered | `vllm/vllm-openai:kimi-k31-cu134` |
| MI355X | `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:kimi-k31` | unchanged, now from `model.docker_image.amd` |
| 810E, M890 | PPU image | unchanged |

- The pip tab is gone on all hardware, because K3.1 isn't in a wheel until #65685 lands.
- The builder no longer offers a CUDA 12.9 toggle for a `kimi-k31-cu129` tag that doesn't exist.

- **`min_vllm_version: "0.34.0"`:** this replaces `"nightly"`, which `cu129DockerImage` scores as 0.0.0, so it would derive a `-cu129` tag. 0.34.0 assumes K3.1 ships in the first release after v0.33.0, and `nightly_required` stays set until then.
- **`install: { pip: false }` on `vr200`:** pip is already off for the whole recipe. This override is there to replace the profile's note, which says its own `cu134-nightly` image is the only one that runs on Rubin.
